dimensions.summary: I read the baseline workflow/{automatic,interactive,pipeline,launch,sessions}.py on main and the three slice-A diffs (pr9.diff, pr10-sliceA.diff, pr11-sliceA.diff), then the full files in each worktree where the diffs cut context, and checked reachability claims against the installed LangGraph 1.2.11 runner and the on-disk run. On the shared controller surface PR 10 produced the cleanest generalisation: it extracted InteractiveSessions.reconcile()/launch() so run() and run_reviewer() are thin composers, keeps one node identity ("review") with a PANE_LABELS map, and funnels both transports through one finish_review(). PR 11 reaches the same reconcile/launch split and adds the best reusable validators (check_review, blocking_findings, reviewer_stop_pending) but pays for its edge-case coverage with the densest control flow, ~20 magic "review" strings in automatic.py while pipeline.py uses a REVIEW constant, a duplicated label conditional, and a non-idempotent pane attach. PR 9 is the smallest diff but generalised the least: run_reviewer is a 54-line near-verbatim copy of run(), the acceptance block is duplicated across review_worktree/native_review/print_review, it carries a dual reviewer/review identity bridged by file_prefix() in sessions.py, and it ships a real bug where an approved verdict with a resolved P0/P1 is blocked, contradicting its own contract.
dimensions.pr9: Structure: minimal and readable, but the generalisation stops at the surface. worktree()/receipt_path() (interactive.py:27-32) let locate()/attach-one serve the reviewer, yet run_reviewer (interactive.py:187-240, 54 lines) copies run() wholesale: the same reconcile block (plan-digest check, locate, receipt.update(status="attached_session_available"...)), the same launch-log/fsync/settle/needs_reconciliation block. Any fix to worker launch must be made twice. Naming: REVIEWER = "reviewer" lives in sessions.py:20 (a module whose ClaudeSessions.run still rejects it), while files, receipts, events, graph node and stop marker all use "review" via file_prefix() (sessions.py:23-25); attach-one takes --node reviewer, terminals.json key is "reviewer", node_id is "review". Two identities and a bridge function are the price. Acceptance logic duplicated 3x ("Reviewer worktree changed"/"Evidence changed during review" appear in review_worktree, native_review and print_review). Real bug: native_review (automatic.py:272) blocks any P0/P1 regardless of disposition while read_review_completion (:186-190) and the v1.ts cross-field rule only reject unresolved ones. wait_review raises on native state "blocked" with the worker's quota message (:208) although the reviewer runs dontAsk, where blocked means it needs a human; PR 10/11 both learned this live. resumable_review (:343-352) is wired into advance_failed_checks whose docstring says "never launches or review" (:355 vs :362) and is keyed on task.error, which LangGraph records only for Exception, so Ctrl-C never reaches it. Good parts: transport() reads DEFAULTS (single source, :43-44), REQUIRED_SETTINGS <= set <= DEFAULTS (:49), review_worktree/review_instructions extracted, stop_session returns intent (pipeline.py:112-140), attach_reviewer_pane is idempotent (interactive.py:367), Pipeline.launch_reviewer mirrors Pipeline.launch (pipeline.py:156-171), contract in v1.ts with cross-field rules mirrored. No live run, so the prompt still says "temporary file then rename" (:168) for a Write-only reviewer and the write permission is not allow-listed.
dimensions.pr10: Structure: the best abstraction of the three on the shared surface. InteractiveSessions.reconcile(node) (interactive.py:117-129) and launch(node, cwd, command, receipt) (:131-161) hold the common receipt fields, log/fsync, settle and needs_reconciliation handling once; run() (:177-221) and run_reviewer() (:163-175) only build their command and a 2-key receipt. One identity: REVIEW_NODE = "review", SESSION_NODES, PANE_LABELS (:24-26); the reviewer/review split is a label map, not a second name. launched_nodes() (:223) generalises status/attach to N sessions and attach_panels splits panes in a loop (:319-325). finish_review (automatic.py:264-280) is the single acceptance path for both transports (one copy each of "Evidence changed", "Reviewer worktree changed", the review dict, and the P0/P1 check fixed to honour disposition); review.json is persisted for blocked verdicts (:274) so the viewer can show why; the reviewer is stopped on any non-interrupt failure (:311), mirroring the worker policy. attach_reviewer_pane returns None for a headless run (:343-352) instead of throwing. Weaknesses: automatic.py imports interactive at module level (:21) and emits pane events itself, bypassing the Pipeline.launch wrapper convention that PR 9/11 follow; reviewer_transport() and validate_automatic each hard-code "print" (:45, :54) while DEFAULTS says "native" (:26), so the module states the default three ways; the stop-marker shortcut in wait_review (:196-198) is unreachable because review_native calls run_reviewer -> reconcile -> locate first, which fails for a stopped session; review_resumable (:216-226) has the same LangGraph dead-trigger issue as PR 9 and no direct unit test; review_candidate grew to ~45 lines carrying worktree creation and resume checks. Binding the completion to a self-reported reviewer_session UUID (:159, :184) deviates from the worker launch_token pattern, though the smoke artifacts show it worked. Outside the slice-A file set but verified: export_state bumped to 1.2.0 with server/projects.ts still z.literal('1.0.0').
dimensions.pr11: Structure: same reconcile()/launch() extraction as PR 10 (interactive.py:113-149) with run()/run_reviewer composing them, and the strongest reusable validators: blocking_findings and check_review(require_approved) (pipeline.py:42-70) serve validate_review, _decide and ExportRuntime alike; REQUIRED_KEYS, REVIEW_COMPLETION_LIMIT and REVIEWER_TRANSPORTS are named (automatic.py:26-28, :141). The one legitimate review retry (stop unconfirmed after a durable accept) is guarded precisely by reviewer_stopped/reviewer_stop_pending (:269-273, :467-478) and bounded in drive (:530-540); the CLI arg-order trap is explained where the command is built (interactive.py:220-223). Costs: automatic.py never imports REVIEW and uses ~20 literal "review", "review.interactive.json", "review.completion.json", "review.stop.json" strings (e.g. :185, :209, :216, :223, :271, :302, :332) while pipeline.py uses the constant; the label rule 'reviewer' if node == REVIEW else node is written twice (interactive.py:38, :353). Control flow is the densest of the three: review_candidate's nested resume branch (automatic.py:228-260) with inline reconcile error handling, a 15-line KeyboardInterrupt branch in _review_native that reads review.interactive.json to copy bound ids (:298-316), and Pipeline.launch_reviewer's except BaseException / if not isinstance(error, Exception): raise idiom plus a HERDR_ENV check that duplicates observer.herdr's own guard (pipeline.py:156-167). Pane attach is spread over allocate_reviewer_pane/attach_pane/attach_reviewer_panel with a redirect branch at the top of attach_panels (interactive.py:291-296) and a second allocation branch at its bottom (:338-340); attach_reviewer_panel raises if the pane already exists (:371-372) where PR 9/10 return the mapping. _decide rewrites the reviewer's verdict to "blocked" in review.json (:282), so the persisted record differs from what the reviewer wrote (original kept only in receipt["decision"]). Worktree/evidence checks are still duplicated between _accept_native and _review_print. The completion contract is a hand-written JSON schema with no v1.ts/examples/contract test, against the repo's contracts:export convention. write_private/prompt.txt (interactive.py:181-182, :213, :241) is slice-C material in the shared file.
dimensions.ranking_reason: PR 10 is the codebase I would rather own in six months: reconcile()/launch() and finish_review() mean the worker and reviewer lifecycles and the two transports each have exactly one implementation, the node identity is a single string plus a label map, and its rough edges (dead stop-marker shortcut, dead-trigger review_resumable, triple-stated default) are small and local. PR 11 achieves the same DRY split and adds the best validators and the only correct bounded-retry design, but a maintainer must hold four interrupt states across review_candidate/_review_native/_accept_native, hunt magic "review" strings that pipeline.py spells as a constant, and reason about a non-idempotent pane attach; that is more code to keep correct. PR 9 is last because it did not generalise the core: run_reviewer is a copy of run(), acceptance is copied three times, the reviewer/review dual identity needs file_prefix() to bridge it, and it ships a behavioural bug (resolved P0/P1 blocks an approved verdict) that PR 10 and 11 both fixed.
dimensions.verifier_note: I swap the top two. The reviewer's case against PR 11 rested on the magic-string and density findings, both of which I downgraded to low after checking the counts and line ratios; what remains against PR 11 on this dimension is the hand-written schema (a contracts-convention break, documented) and two duplicated evidence checks. What remains against PR 10 is structural: its review lifecycle contains two code paths that describe behaviour that cannot occur (the stop-marker shortcut in wait_review and the review_resumable classifier), and the ordering stop-then-accept leaves a real, if narrow, window that strands a run in manual reconciliation, which PR 11's accept-then-stop-with-retry closes. PR 11 also keeps event emission and pane attachment inside Pipeline.launch_reviewer/reconcile_reviewer (consistent with Pipeline.launch) where PR 10's automatic.py reaches into interactive.py directly, and its check_review/blocking_findings give the P0/P1 rule one home. PR 10 still has the tidier identity model (REVIEW_NODE plus PANE_LABELS), the single finish_review, and a generic reconcile() that makes a launch-window Ctrl-C safe without PR 11's explicit branch, so the gap is small. PR 9 is last and further back than the reviewer scored it: beyond the duplicated run_reviewer, the three-way acceptance copy and the dual identity, its reviewer launch command places the positional prompt immediately after the variadic --add-dir, so the composed command cannot deliver the task (new high finding), and it was never run live.

findings.title: native_review blocks an approved verdict that carries a resolved P0/P1, contradicting its own contract
findings.detail: read_review_completion enforces the v1.ts cross-field rule that only an UNRESOLVED P0/P1 invalidates an approval, and Pipeline.validate_review accepts resolved P0/P1, but native_review then re-checks severity alone and raises 'Independent reviewer blocked the candidate'. A reviewer who records a P1 as resolved and approves gets the run blocked. PR 10 (finish_review) and PR 11 (blocking_findings) both fixed this; PR 9 kept the baseline check while adding a contract that makes it wrong.
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:272 `if decision["verdict"] != "approved" or any(item["severity"] in {"P0", "P1"} for item in decision["findings"]): raise RuntimeError("Independent reviewer blocked the candidate")` vs :186-190 `if item["verdict"] == "approved" and any(finding["severity"] != "P2" and finding["disposition"] != "resolved" ...)` and contracts/workflow/v1.ts:174-175 'Approval cannot leave an unresolved P0/P1 finding'. Same severity-only check survives in print_review at :323.
findings.verifier_reason: The contradiction is real and I confirmed every cited line, but it is fail-closed, inherited verbatim from main's print-mode check (main automatic.py:177 has the identical severity-only test), and the reviewer prompt itself steers away from the 'resolved' disposition ('do not pretend to resolve defects'). PR 9 made it a contradiction by adding a contract that explicitly permits resolved P0/P1 in an approved verdict; that deserves fixing, but a conservative rejection of an unlikely verdict shape is not a merge-blocking bug. PR 10 (finish_review :275) and PR 11 (blocking_findings) both honour disposition.
findings.verifier_evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:272 `if decision["verdict"] != "approved" or any(item["severity"] in {"P0", "P1"} for item in decision["findings"]): raise RuntimeError("Independent reviewer blocked the candidate")`; :190-192 `if item["verdict"] == "approved" and any(finding["severity"] != "P2" and finding["disposition"] != "resolved" ...): raise ValueError("Approval cannot leave an unresolved P0/P1 finding")`; contracts/workflow/v1.ts:172-173 same rule; same severity-only test at :323 (print_review). Baseline: md-manager/workflow/automatic.py:177 identical severity-only check; main pipeline.py:320 validate_review only rejects `disposition != "resolved"`. Prompt :149-150 'Approve only with no unresolved P0/P1; do not pretend to resolve defects.'

findings.detail: The reconcile-existing-receipt block and the launch-log/fsync/settle/needs_reconciliation block are duplicated between run() and run_reviewer(). Any future change to how a native session is bound (e.g. the settle poll, the receipt fields, the HERDR_ env scrub) must be made in two places. PR 10 and PR 11 both extracted reconcile()/launch() so their run/run_reviewer are thin.

findings.title: Dual reviewer/review identity bridged by file_prefix() in a module that otherwise rejects the reviewer
findings.detail: REVIEWER = "reviewer" names the pane, launch name, terminals.json key and --node value, while receipts, events, graph node, stop marker and node_id all use "review"; file_prefix() exists solely to map one to the other. The constant lives in sessions.py, whose ClaudeSessions.run still does `if node not in NODES: raise ValueError("Unknown worker")` and whose prepare() never allocates it. PR 10 keeps one identity ("review") with a PANE_LABELS map in interactive.py, the module that owns native sessions.
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/sessions.py:20 `REVIEWER = "reviewer"`, :23-25 `def file_prefix(node): return "review" if node == REVIEWER else node`; interactive.py:31-32 receipt_path uses file_prefix; interactive.py:396 `--node choices=[*NODES, REVIEWER]`; RUNBOOK.md:179 `attach-one "$RUN" --node reviewer`; but interactive.py:217 `receipt = {"node_id": "review", ...}` and pipeline.py:158-170 `self.event("review", ...)`. Contrast md-manager-high/workflow/interactive.py:24-26 `REVIEW_NODE = "review"; SESSION_NODES = (*NODES, REVIEW_NODE); PANE_LABELS = {..., REVIEW_NODE: "reviewer"}`.
findings.verifier_reason: All cited facts check out. The constant and bridge live in sessions.py whose ClaudeSessions.run rejects the node; the receipt written by run_reviewer uses node_id "review" while the launch name, --node choice, terminals.json key and runbook use "reviewer". The only correction is the runbook path: it is workflow/RUNBOOK.md, not docs/RUNBOOK.md.
findings.verifier_evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/sessions.py:20 `REVIEWER = "reviewer"`, :24-26 `def file_prefix(node): return "review" if node == REVIEWER else node`, :131 `raise ValueError("Unknown worker")` in ClaudeSessions.run; interactive.py:32 `f"{file_prefix(node)}.interactive.json"`, :212 `receipt = {"node_id": "review", ...}`, :378 `mapping[REVIEWER] = ...`, :396 `choices=[*NODES, REVIEWER]`; pipeline.py:114 `f"{file_prefix(node)}.stop.json"`, :151 `self.stop_session(REVIEWER)`, :154 `self.event("review", "stopped", ...)`; workflow/RUNBOOK.md:179 `attach-one "$RUN" --node reviewer`. Contrast md-manager-high/workflow/interactive.py:24-26 `REVIEW_NODE = "review"; SESSION_NODES = (*NODES, REVIEW_NODE); PANE_LABELS = {..., REVIEW_NODE: "reviewer"}`.

findings.detail: The worktree-clean check, evidence-digest check, review dict construction and validate_review call are written three times (review_worktree's resume path, native_review, print_review). PR 10 has one copy in finish_review; PR 11 has two.

One overstatement: the review-dict construction and validate_review call appear twice (native_review, print_review), not three times; review_worktree's copy is only the worktree/evidence check used as a pre-resume guard. The worktree-clean and evidence-digest checks are genuinely written three times, so the finding stands at medium.

findings.title: wait_review treats native state 'blocked' as a quota failure and never stops the reviewer on failure
findings.detail: The reviewer runs with --permission-mode dontAsk (not bypassPermissions like the workers), so a 'blocked' row means it is waiting for a human (a question, or a denied write it reports). PR 9 copies the worker branch and raises with the worker's quota message; PR 10 and PR 11, having run it live, both treat blocked as a waiting state until the deadline and emit an event. Separately, PR 9 only stops the reviewer on success (stop_reviewer called once, at :281), so a blocked verdict or deadline leaves a live session that has --add-dir <run dir> and Write; the handoff documents this as intentional but it diverges from drive()'s worker policy of stopping sessions that cannot continue.
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:207-208 `if row["state"] == "blocked": raise RuntimeError("Reviewer blocked; inspect quota or native error. No billing/provider fallback.")`; grep stop_reviewer automatic.py -> only :281. docs/HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md:58 'A deadline does not stop the reviewer ... stopping it is left to the operator'. Compare md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:202-207 and md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:219-223 (blocked = waiting, event emitted).
findings.verifier_reason: Code facts verified: PR 9 raises on blocked with the worker's quota wording, stop_reviewer is called exactly once on the success path, and the handoff states the deadline intentionally leaves the reviewer running. PR 10 and PR 11 both treat blocked as a waiting state with an event and stop the reviewer on any non-interrupt failure. I cannot independently verify the CLI's semantics of 'blocked' under dontAsk without starting a session, but both live-tested PRs converged on the same reading and PR 9 has no live evidence either way.
findings.verifier_evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:207-208 `if row["state"] == "blocked": raise RuntimeError("Reviewer blocked; inspect quota or native error. No billing/provider fallback.")` (copied from wait_handoffs :116-117); `grep -n stop_reviewer workflow/automatic.py` -> only :281 inside the success path. docs/HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md: 'A deadline does not stop the reviewer. ... stopping it is left to the operator'. md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:206-212 blocked -> `runtime.event(REVIEW_NODE, "interactive", "Reviewer is waiting for input in its pane...")` and :307-313 stop_session on any BaseException; md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:219-223 same waiting treatment, :347-356 stop_reviewer on failure.

findings.title: 'Resumable review' classifiers are keyed on task.error, which LangGraph never records for KeyboardInterrupt; their real trigger re-executes a deterministic failure
findings.detail: Both PRs justify resumable_review/review_resumable as the path by which a Ctrl-C'd review re-enters its running session. The installed LangGraph runner commits a task error only inside `except Exception`, so KeyboardInterrupt leaves the review task pending with no error and the next drive() loop re-invokes it naturally; the classifier is not what makes the (passing) [75,130,75,0] tests work. The only way task.error is set while the receipt is still 'launching'/'running' is an Exception raised in review_candidate's prologue or review_worktree (e.g. validate_bundle or 'Reviewer worktree changed'), and then the classifier returns True and the same failure is re-run on every supervisor restart up to the 45 limit, the opposite of 'ambiguous invocations never replay'. PR 9 also placed it inside advance_failed_checks whose docstring says 'never launches or review'. PR 11 has no such classifier and would fail closed.
findings.evidence: .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/langgraph/pregel/_runner.py:221-223 `self.commit(t, None)` / `except Exception as exc: self.commit(t, exc)`; _runner.py:578-600 commit() only writes ERROR for exceptions it receives. md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:343-352 resumable_review, :355 docstring 'Retry only recorded failing verification packets, never launches or review.' vs :362 `if failures == ["review"]: return resumable_review(runtime)`; test_automatic.py:263-285 builds `SimpleNamespace(name="review", error="interrupted")` synthetically. md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:216-226 review_resumable, :459 wired into drive; `grep -n review_resumable test_automatic.py` -> no direct test.
findings.verifier_reason: Verified in the installed runner: the single-task fast path and run_with_retry both catch only Exception, and commit() writes ERROR only for the exception it receives, so a KeyboardInterrupt leaves the review task pending with no error and the next drive() simply re-invokes it. The only way the classifier returns True is an Exception raised before the native try block while the receipt is still launching/running (validate_bundle, 'Reviewer worktree changed', 'Evidence changed'); each restart then replays that failure until supervise's 45 loops run out. PR 9's handoff even admits LangGraph records no error for Ctrl-C, yet the docstring and inline comment still describe the branch as the Ctrl-C resume path. PR 10 has no direct test of review_resumable.
findings.verifier_evidence: .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/langgraph/pregel/_runner.py:221-223 `self.commit(t, None)` / `except Exception as exc: self.commit(t, exc)`; _retry.py:641 `except Exception as exc:` in run_with_retry; _runner.py:595-603 commit() appends `(ERROR, exception)` only for the exception passed in. md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:344 'An interrupted review resumes into its own live session', :355 docstring 'never launches or review' vs :362-365 `if failures == ["review"]: return resumable_review(runtime)`; test_automatic.py:269 `SimpleNamespace(name="review", error="interrupted")` synthetic. HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md: 'the four-process test still passed, because LangGraph records no task error for a KeyboardInterrupt'. md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:216-225 review_resumable, :459 wired; `grep -n review_resumable workflow/test_automatic.py` -> no match; the Ctrl-C tests at :441-455 and :457-500 pass through the pending-task path, not the classifier. Replay trigger: opus :222-225 / high :247-248 raise with status still launching/running.

findings.title: wait_review's stop-marker recovery shortcut is unreachable in the real flow
findings.detail: wait_review starts with 'if review.stop.json says stopped, accept the file bound to the stopped session'. But review_native always calls runtime.sessions.run_reviewer first, which for an existing receipt calls reconcile() -> locate(); for a stopped session locate() returns None or raises 'No live native PID', so run_reviewer raises 'Existing launch cannot be reconciled' before wait_review is ever entered. The branch documents a recovery that cannot happen. PR 11 handles the same scenario correctly by returning early from review_candidate on a succeeded receipt and retrying only the stop.
findings.evidence: md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:194-198 `stop = runtime.directory / f"{REVIEW_NODE}.stop.json"; if stop.exists() and read_json(stop)["stopped"]: return read_review_completion(...)`; review_native order :286 run_reviewer -> :297 wait_review; interactive.py:175-176 `if (...review.interactive.json).exists(): return self.reconcile(REVIEW_NODE)`; reconcile :123-125 `row = self.locate(...); if row is None: raise RuntimeError("Existing launch cannot be reconciled; no automatic relaunch")`. Compare md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:236-241.
findings.verifier_reason: Traced the only production caller: review_native calls run_reviewer first, which for an existing receipt goes straight to reconcile() -> locate(); a stopped session either has no inventory row (locate returns None -> 'Existing launch cannot be reconciled') or no live PID (raises). wait_review is therefore never entered once review.stop.json says stopped; the branch is exercised only by a test that calls wait_review directly. Worse, the scenario it was written for is real and unrecoverable in PR 10: stop_session runs before finish_review marks the receipt succeeded, so a Ctrl-C or crash during that window (stop_session does two inventory calls, a `claude stop` and a PID check) leaves status 'running' with a stopped session, and the next resume fails closed. PR 11 orders accept-then-stop and retries only the stop.
findings.verifier_evidence: md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:195-198 `stop = runtime.directory / f"{REVIEW_NODE}.stop.json"; if stop.exists() and read_json(stop)["stopped"]: return read_review_completion(...)`; caller order :286 `launch = runtime.sessions.run_reviewer(prompt, completion_path)` ... :297 `decision = wait_review(runtime, digest, bundle)`; interactive.py:175-176 `if (self.directory / f"{REVIEW_NODE}.interactive.json").exists(): return self.reconcile(REVIEW_NODE)`; :123-125 `row = self.locate(...); if row is None: raise RuntimeError("Existing launch cannot be reconciled; no automatic relaunch")`; locate :84-86 raises 'No live native PID' for a row without pid. Stop-before-accept window: :298 `intent = runtime.stop_session(REVIEW_NODE)` precedes :302 finish_review -> :278 `receipt.update(status="succeeded", ...)`. test_automatic.py:574 writes review.stop.json stopped=True and drives wait_review directly. Compare md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:236-241 succeeded-receipt path retrying stop_reviewer, :357-363 stop after durable accept.

findings.title: export_state bumped to 1.2.0 while the adapter still requires z.literal('1.0.0') (outside the slice-A file set, verified)
findings.detail: Not part of the five controller files, but it decides whether the merged branch is usable: any run exported after merging PR 10 is rejected by server/projects.ts until slice B lands. PR 9 leaves export_state untouched; PR 11 updates the adapter to accept 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0.

findings.title: Reviewer launch command puts the positional prompt directly after the variadic --add-dir, so the prompt is swallowed as a directory
findings.detail: `claude --help` documents `--add-dir <directories...>` as variadic. PR 9's run_reviewer builds `[..., "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]`, so the prompt text is parsed as a second directory and the reviewer session starts with no task (PR 11 observed exactly this live and reordered its command so the prompt follows the single-valued --permission-mode; PR 10's order also happens to be safe). PR 9's unit test only asserts the element after --add-dir is the run directory, not where the prompt lands, so the suite is green. Together with the missing Edit allow rule (already established), PR 9's native review path cannot produce a verdict: every run would idle to the 30-minute deadline and then leave the reviewer running.

findings.title: Journal-before-launch ordering makes reconcile() a correct generic handler for a launch-window Ctrl-C without a dedicated branch
findings.detail: launch() saves the interactive receipt before subprocess.run, and review_candidate saves the 'launching' review receipt before calling run_reviewer, so 'no review.interactive.json' provably means no `claude --bg` was issued and a fresh launch is safe, while an existing receipt is bound through reconcile()/locate() (including the launch.log UUID fallback). This covers the same launch-window interruption that PR 11 handles with its 15-line explicit KeyboardInterrupt branch, in far less code. PR 9 has the same journaling but duplicated per function.

dimensions.summary: I read workflow/automatic.py, the review-node helpers in pipeline.py and the reviewer launch/locate/stop code in interactive.py for all three PRs, plus the PRD, each handoff, the tests that model interruption, PR 10's live smoke artifacts, the installed CLI's --help and LangGraph 1.2.11's runner. The wait/accept/binding logic is broadly similar and fail-closed in all three, but they differ sharply at the edges. PR 9's native launch cannot work live: `--add-dir <dir> <prompt>` puts the prompt after a variadic option (the CLI help says `--add-dir <directories...>`), and Write under `dontAsk` with no allow rule is denied (established by both other PRs' live runs; PR 9's own handoff names this exact risk and admits the PRD's gating smoke test was not run). PR 10 works live and stops the reviewer on every failure, but a failed post-acceptance stop discards the accepted verdict, its `wait_review` stop-recovery branch is unreachable through `review_native`, and an approved-with-open-P1 file is recorded as `verdict: approved` on a blocked run. PR 11 is the most robust: verdict made durable before the stop and the stop retried on resume, explicit launch-window Ctrl-C handling, identity re-checked against the live inventory after the wait, and the contradictory verdict normalised, all covered by tests; its remaining issues are low.
dimensions.pr9: Control path as shipped cannot complete a live review. interactive.py:219-220 builds `--tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write --permission-mode dontAsk --add-dir <run> <prompt>`: `--add-dir <directories...>` is variadic in the installed CLI so the prompt is consumed as a directory (PR 11 saw exactly this live: session starts idle), and even with a prompt the single Write is denied under dontAsk without an allow rule (PR 10 attempt 2, PR 11's permtest; PR 9's handoff line 55 anticipates it and line 63 admits the PRD section 5 smoke test was never run). wait_review (automatic.py:196-211) fails immediately on native state `blocked` (207-208), which both other PRs found is the state a reviewer shows while waiting for a person, so the PRD's "operator answers a question" success case fails the run. On deadline/blocked/rejected file the reviewer is never stopped (288-290; documented at handoff line 58 as a decision, but a mid-turn reviewer keeps burning usage). stop_reviewer runs before the receipt is marked succeeded (281-282) and a failed stop lands in `except BaseException` → status blocked → next resume refuses ("needs reconciliation"), discarding an accepted verdict with no review.json. Strengths: zod schema with cross-field rules mirrored at 188-192, launch_token re-bound at reconcile (interactive.py run_reviewer refuses a receipt whose token differs), resumable_review refuses to resume into a vanished session (343-351), Ctrl-C mid-wait resumes correctly (4-process test, exit codes [75,130,75,0]), all rejections fail closed. Offline logic is decent; the launch and blocked-state handling make it unfit to merge for its stated purpose.
dimensions.pr10: Works live (smoke artifacts show a real reviewer UUID bound in review.completion.json, a blocked verdict written to review.json, review.stop.json stopped). Bindings follow the PRD table literally: schema consts for version/node_id, run/bundle/candidate checked, and `reviewer_session` must equal the live inventory row's UUID and differ from both worker UUIDs (automatic.py:181-185). Accepts the file in idle/done/blocked (211-212), treating `blocked` as waiting (documented in its PRD edit). Every failure path stops the reviewer (307-314). Weaknesses: stop_session runs before finish_review (298-302) and a failed stop → `except BaseException` → status blocked → next resume refuses, so an accepted verdict is discarded (same defect as PR 9); the wait_review "recovered after stop" branch (196-198) is unreachable in practice because review_native → run_reviewer → reconcile (interactive.py:107-108,117-125) must locate a live row first, so a crash between stop and receipt=succeeded still ends in manual reconciliation and the test at test_automatic.py:572 only exercises the function in isolation; finish_review writes review.json with the reviewer's `approved` verdict even when an open P0/P1 blocks the run (271-276), which its own validate_review_record (pipeline.py) then rejects on `export`; review_resumable (216-225) accepts only status `running` while review_candidate resumes {launching, running}, and both can re-invoke a pre-check that fails outside any try (247-248), bounded only by the supervisor's 45 restarts. Solid, fail-closed, live-proven, but weaker recoverability and record consistency than PR 11.
dimensions.pr11: Most robust of the three. Launch order pinned so the prompt follows the single-valued `--permission-mode` (interactive.py:222-226, test_interactive.py:245-249) with `--allowedTools Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json)`; live accept path proven (attempt 4). Bindings: schema consts version/node_id, run/bundle/candidate plus controller-issued launch_token (automatic.py:196-200); after the wait the live row is re-located and must equal the receipt's UUID and not be a worker UUID (332-335), then worktree, bundle and diff hashes are re-checked (336-339). Accepts only idle/done per PRD; `blocked` is noted once and waited on (219-225). Failure paths stop the reviewer (347-356). The audit fixes are real and correct: verdict made durable (review.json + receipt succeeded, 340-341) before stop_reviewer (357-363), a failed stop is retried on resume via review_candidate (236-241) and gated in drive by reviewer_stop_pending (467-479, 528, 536-539), tested at test_automatic.py:710; launch-window Ctrl-C handled for unissued/unbound/bound cases (301-315, reconcile_reviewer pipeline.py:169-181), tested at 616-670; approved-with-open-P1 normalised to `blocked` with the raw decision retained in the receipt (280-284), tested at 606-611. Nits: an interrupt before `claude --bg` was issued is marked needs_reconciliation although nothing was launched (302-307); pane attach gated on HERDR_ENV=1; run_reviewer does not assert `automatic` like the others. I found no acceptance of a bad verdict and no path that launches a second reviewer.
dimensions.ranking_reason: PR 11 handles every edge the dimension asks about (launch-window interrupt, durable verdict before stop with retry, identity re-check after the wait, blocked-as-waiting, contradictory verdict, no second reviewer) and proved the accept path live. PR 10 proved the launch and blocked/deadline paths live and stops on failure, but discards an accepted verdict when the stop fails, carries an unreachable recovery branch, and writes a misleading review.json for approved-with-open-P1. PR 9's offline logic is comparable to PR 10's but its launch command is non-functional on the installed CLI (variadic --add-dir swallows the prompt; Write denied under dontAsk), it fails the run the moment the reviewer is `blocked`, and it never stops the reviewer on failure, with the gating smoke test admittedly unrun.
dimensions.verifier_note: All seven findings survived verification unchanged. PR 11 is the only one whose protocol is correct at every edge I could check: prompt placement (interactive.py:223-226, pinned by test_interactive.py:245-249 and confirmed by my commander probe), Edit(//path) allow rule, blocked-as-waiting with idle/done acceptance per the PRD, post-wait identity/independence/worktree/evidence re-checks (automatic.py:332-339, tests 752-759), verdict durable before the stop with a resume retry (340-363, 236-241, drive 528/536-539, test 710-742), contradictory verdict normalised (280-284), and four live attempts culminating in a proven accept path; its deviation from the PRD binding is recorded in its PRD edit. PR 10 works live (artifacts verified: real UUID bound, review.stop.json stopped, blocked review.json with a P1) and stops on every failure, but three mediums stand: a failed stop discards an accepted verdict, a dead recovery branch with a test that only exercises it in isolation, and a review.json that its own export validator rejects because the Python side skips the cross-field rule its contract README requires. PR 9's offline binding/resume logic is comparable to PR 10's, and all three recover a launch-window interrupt through reconcile (PR 9 interactive.py:196-207, PR 10 :175-176, PR 11 explicitly with tests), but PR 9's launch cannot deliver the prompt or write the file on the installed CLI, it fails the run on `blocked`, it never stops the reviewer on failure, and it admits the PRD's gating smoke test was not run. Scores: PR 11 9, PR 10 7, PR 9 3.5.

findings.title: Reviewer launch puts the prompt after variadic --add-dir, so the session starts with no task
findings.detail: run_reviewer builds the command as `... "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt`. The installed CLI declares `--add-dir <directories...>` (variadic), so the prompt string is consumed as an extra directory and the native session starts idle. PR 11's live attempt 1 hit exactly this ("send a prompt to start") and its test pins the order; PR 9's test only asserts `command[command.index("--add-dir") + 1] == str(self.directory)` (test_interactive.py:189), which cannot detect the swallowed prompt. Under PR 9's wait_review an idle/blocked reviewer then either fails fast (blocked) or burns the 30-minute deadline.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:219-220 `"--tools", self.reviewer_tools, "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]`; `claude --help | grep add-dir` → `--add-dir <directories...>  Additional directories to allow tool access to`; PR 11 handoff section 4 attempt 1; PR 10 (interactive.py:184-186) and PR 11 (interactive.py:225-226) both place the prompt after `--permission-mode dontAsk`.
findings.verifier_reason: The command literally ends `"--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt`; the installed CLI declares --add-dir variadic, and a commander probe with PR 9's exact ordering shows the prompt absorbed into addDir with an empty positional list. PR 11 observed the same live (session started idle, 'send a prompt to start'). PR 9's only test on the option cannot detect it.
findings.verifier_evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:217-220 `command = [self.executable, "--bg", "--name", ..., "--tools", self.reviewer_tools, "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]`. `claude --help` (2.1.280): `--add-dir <directories...>`. Scratch probe (npm install commander@12 in scratchpad/probe): PR9-order → `opts {"tools":["Read,Write"],"permissionMode":"dontAsk","addDir":["/run","my prompt"]} args []`; PR11-order → `addDir:["/run"] ... args ["my prompt"]`. PR 9's handoff explicitly anticipates this ("single constants if the live smoke test shows dontAsk refuses that write") and admits the PRD section 5 smoke test that gates the merge was not run. findings.title: Reviewer is never stopped on deadline, blocked state or rejected file
findings.detail: native_review's `except BaseException` only records status=blocked and re-raises; unlike drive's worker path (which calls stop_workers so no session keeps consuming usage) nothing stops the reviewer. The handoff records this as a decision ("an idle reviewer does not [consume usage]"), but at the deadline the reviewer may be mid-turn, and after a `blocked`-state failure it is left running indefinitely. PR 10 (307-314) and PR 11 (347-356) stop the reviewer with the identity re-check on every failure path.

findings.title: A failed post-acceptance stop discards the accepted verdict and dead-ends the run
findings.detail: Both PRs call the stop before the receipt is marked succeeded and route any stop failure into the generic `except BaseException` that sets status=blocked. On the next controller process review_candidate sees status blocked and raises "Prior reviewer invocation needs reconciliation; no automatic relaunch"; no review.json exists (PR 9) or the run cannot proceed (PR 10). A transient `claude stop` non-zero exit or an unproven termination therefore converts a valid, fully bound verdict into a manual-reconciliation case. PR 11 fixed this ordering: review.json and receipt=succeeded are written first, the stop is outside the try, and review_candidate/reviewer_stop_pending retry it on resume (tested).

The stop itself has a realistic transient failure: stop_session checks pid_alive immediately after `claude stop` returns, with no grace period, and raises 'termination is not established'. findings.title: wait_review's stop-recovery branch is unreachable through review_native; the crash-after-stop window still needs manual reconciliation

The recovery branch is dead code and test_stopped_reviewer_recovery_rereads_the_accepted_file only calls wait_review directly, so the test passes without the path being reachable in the graph.

findings.title: Resume gate re-invokes a review node whose pre-check fails outside the try, looping until the supervisor's 45-restart limit
findings.detail: LangGraph 1.2.11 commits only `Exception` (not KeyboardInterrupt) as a task error, so the resume gates only matter for recorded exceptions. In both PRs some checks run before the try that sets status=blocked (PR 9: validate_bundle at the top of review_candidate and review_worktree at native_review:257; PR 10: the cwd/HEAD/patch checks at 247-248). If one of those fails on resume the receipt stays `running`, the error is recorded, PR 9's resumable_review / PR 10's review_resumable return True, and drive re-invokes the node which fails identically. With single_step (the only production caller) each failure exits 75 and the supervisor repeats up to 45 times before "restart limit exhausted", hiding the real cause. PR 11 fails closed once in this case (gate requires status succeeded).
findings.evidence: .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/langgraph/pregel/_runner.py:222 `except Exception as exc: self.commit(t, exc)`; PR 9 automatic.py:236-237, :257, :343-351, :362-365; PR 10 automatic.py:247-248, :216-225, :459; pipeline.py `drive(runtime, single_step=True)` at opus:570 / high:620; supervise loop `for _ in range(45)`.

findings.title: review_resumable accepts only status `running` while review_candidate resumes {launching, running}
findings.detail: The two resume predicates disagree: drive's gate treats a `launching` receipt with a recorded error as non-retryable, but review_candidate would happily reconcile it. Harmless today only because Ctrl-C is not recorded as a task error by LangGraph; the inconsistency is a latent trap if a recorded Exception ever leaves the receipt at `launching`.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:225 `return receipt.get("transport") == "native" and receipt.get("status") == "running"` vs :244 `resumable = receipt.get("transport") == "native" and receipt.get("status") in {"launching", "running"}`.

findings.detail: run_reviewer saves review.interactive.json before running the launch helper, so its absence proves no session was launched. _review_native nevertheless marks the receipt needs_reconciliation and the next resume refuses with "needs reconciliation; no automatic relaunch", forcing manual intervention for a case with no ambiguity. Fail-closed and explicitly tested, so a nit rather than a bug.

findings.title: Verdict made durable before the stop; failed stop retried on resume without relaunch
findings.detail: Acceptance writes review.json and marks the receipt succeeded inside the try, the stop runs afterwards, a failing stop raises a distinct REVIEW_STOP_NOTE from drive, and review_candidate retries stop_reviewer (idempotent via review.stop.json) when the receipt is succeeded but reviewer_stopped() is false. This is the correct fix for the defect PR 9 and PR 10 share, and the test walks both processes and asserts exactly one launch.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:340-341, :357-363, :236-241, :269-272, :467-479, :528, :536-539; test_automatic.py:710-745 asserts receipt succeeded with no error after the failed stop, then stopped=true and reviewer_launches()==1 after resume.

findings.title: Identity, independence, worktree and evidence re-checked after the wait, with a test for each refusal
findings.detail: After wait_review returns, the live inventory row is re-located and must equal the receipt's UUID and not be a worker UUID, then HEAD/cleanliness and bundle/diff hashes are re-verified; each refusal is a separate test (identity changed, worker-as-reviewer, reviewer vanished after the file, worktree edited, diff rewritten). This closes the validation-to-acceptance TOCTOU more explicitly than PR 9 (relies on locate inside stop_session) or PR 10 (uses the row from the same poll).
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:332-339; test_automatic.py:753-780 (test_reviewer_identity_changed_after_the_file_is_refused, test_reviewer_that_is_a_worker_session_is_not_independent, test_reviewer_missing_after_the_file_is_refused, test_reviewer_worktree_change_is_refused, test_evidence_change_during_review_is_refused).

findings.title: Live-proven launch and blocked/deadline paths; reviewer stopped on every failure
findings.detail: The smoke run directory shows a real reviewer session (UUID distinct from the workers) whose completion file bound bundle, candidate and its own UUID, a blocked verdict persisted to review.json, review.stop.json stopped, and the receipt marked blocked with the reason. review_native's failure path stops the session with the identity re-check on deadline, rejected file and blocked verdict alike, and the tests assert review.stop.json.stopped in each case.

"review.stop.json")["stopped"]`.

findings.title: Launch token re-bound at reconcile and interrupt recovery proven across four real controller processes
findings.detail: run_reviewer refuses to reuse a receipt whose plan_digest or launch_token differs from the review node's intent, so a stale review.interactive.json cannot be adopted; resumable_review only re-enters a live session with a launching/running native receipt; and the recovery test runs four real processes (exit codes [75,130,75,0]) with the reviewer interrupted mid-review and re-entered without a second launch.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:197-199 `if receipt["plan_digest"] != digest or receipt["launch_token"] != launch_token: raise RuntimeError("Reviewer launch intent changed; refusing session reuse")`; automatic.py:343-351; docs/HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md:43; test_automatic.py:392-420.

findings.title: Completion prompt instructs a temp-file-then-rename write the reviewer's tool set cannot perform
findings.detail: The protocol text tells the reviewer to write the completion file 'atomically (temporary file then rename)', but the session is launched with only Read, Glob, Grep and Write (no Bash), so a rename is impossible; and under any single-file allow rule (the fix PR 10/11 needed) the temporary path would itself be denied. PR 11's prompt says the opposite explicitly ('It cannot be written under a temporary name and renamed, so write it once').
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:167-169 'On completion write the following JSON shape atomically (temporary file then rename) to ...'; interactive.py:184 `reviewer_tools = "Read,Glob,Grep,Write"`. PR 11 automatic.py:175-177 'It cannot be written under a temporary name and renamed, so write it once, complete, as your last action'.

findings.title: PRD binding row left unchanged while the code binds launch_token; the low 'deviation not recorded' item applies to PR 9, not PR 11
findings.detail: PR 9's completion file binds a controller-issued launch_token, but its PRD edit leaves the table row 'Bound to ... reviewer session UUID' as on main, so the deviation is unrecorded. PR 11 rewrote that row with the reason and date, so the low-severity item in the list must not be counted against PR 11.

findings.title: Launch-window interrupt already recovers through reconcile in PR 9 and PR 10; PR 11's advantage there is explicitness and tests, not correctness
findings.detail: In both PRs run_reviewer reconciles whenever the interactive receipt exists, regardless of its status, and locate binds the background id from review.launch.log, so a Ctrl-C inside settle or the pane attach resumes into the same session on the next controller process with no relaunch. The automatic receipt stays 'launching' and review_candidate treats that as resumable. PR 11 adds session_id binding into automatic-review.json, an 'interrupted' event and three tests; it does not close a hole the others have.

PR 10 interactive.py:175-176 `return self.reconcile(REVIEW_NODE)`; locate :59-67 reads `claude attach <id>` from the launch log; automatic.py:244 resumes {launching, running}. PR 11 automatic.py:301-315, tests 616-668.

findings.title: A valid completion file written before the reviewer ends its turn with a question is not accepted until someone answers in the pane
findings.detail: wait_review accepts only in native state idle/done, exactly as the PRD table says, but both live runs showed that a session which ends its turn asking a person is listed as `blocked`. A reviewer that writes a valid file and then asks 'anything else?' is therefore held until an operator answers; unattended, the deadline stops it and the verdict is discarded (receipt blocked, no review.json). PR 10 accepts the file in `blocked` too. Operator-recoverable and PRD-conformant, so low.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:224 `if row["state"] in {"idle", "done"} and path.exists(): return read_review_completion(runtime)`; :219-223 blocked only noted. Main PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:28 'Accepted when | file validates against the schema and the native session is `idle` or `done`'. PR 10 handoff line 59 'ended its turn asking a person ... reported the session as `blocked`'; PR 10 automatic.py:211 `in {"idle", "done", "blocked"}`.

findings.title: Live smoke artifacts verified on disk: the full native protocol ran, bound a real UUID and stopped the session
findings.detail: The claim of a working live run is backed by retained artifacts, not just the handoff: the launch log carries the `claude attach 5865c9a6` line locate binds from, the interactive receipt has the session UUID and observed_state working, the completion file carries that UUID with verdict blocked and a P1, review.json records the blocked verdict, review.stop.json is stopped:true with a PID and timestamp, and automatic-review.json is blocked with 'Independent reviewer blocked the candidate'. This is the blocked-verdict path, live.

dimensions.summary: I read the reviewer launch, pane, attach and stop code (workflow/interactive.py, pipeline.py, sessions.py, plus the review node in automatic.py) in all three worktrees against main, extracted each reviewer argv, and checked it against `claude --help` (2.1.278), the Claude Code permissions docs, commander's variadic-option semantics, the on-disk smoke artifacts and the native registry (`claude agents --json --all`). PR 9 is live-broken twice over: its argv puts the prompt directly after the variadic `--add-dir <dir>` so the reviewer never receives its task, and it launches `Write` under `dontAsk` with no allow rule so the reviewer could not write its verdict even if it had one; its `wait_review` also treats the `blocked` state as fatal, which is exactly the state a reviewer enters when it asks for the permission it lacks. PR 10 and PR 11 both build an argv that works against the real CLI (`--allowedTools "Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json)"`, prompt after the single-valued `--permission-mode`), and the registry confirms their claimed live sessions (PR 10: dccd22b5, 5865c9a6; PR 11: 7eb01f17, a4c348e5, 25d99bf4, f36b923d). PR 11 is the most complete on this dimension: it pins the option order in a test, binds the verdict to a controller-issued launch token, makes `attach` add the reviewer pane to an existing tab, stops the reviewer on every failure path and retries a failed post-acceptance stop on resume; PR 10 works but binds to a session UUID the model has to discover, does not pin the prompt position, and cannot add the pane through `attach`.
dimensions.pr9: Argv (interactive.py:216-220): `claude --bg --name workflow-<run>-reviewer --safe-mode --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config {"mcpServers":{}} --tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write --permission-mode dontAsk --add-dir <run> <prompt>`, cwd review-worktree. Two independent live-breaking defects: (1) `--add-dir <directories...>` is variadic and commander consumes following non-dash arguments, so the prompt becomes a second directory and the session starts idle (PR 11 observed exactly this live, session 7eb01f17); (2) `dontAsk` auto-denies every call that would prompt unless an allow rule matches, and `--add-dir` directories follow the permission mode for edits, so the reviewer's single Write is denied (PR 10 observed "Permission to use Write has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode"). A third defect compounds them: automatic.py:207-208 raises on state `blocked`, which is the state a reviewer shows when it ends a turn asking a person, contradicting the PRD's acceptance criterion that a reviewer question can be answered in the pane. The reviewer is never stopped on deadline, rejection or blocked verdict (documented choice, handoff "A deadline does not stop the reviewer"), `status()` (interactive.py:242-250) omits the reviewer, and `attach` never adds the third pane (only the review node's `attach_reviewer_pane` does). The code structure itself is clean (attach_pane extraction, stop_session generalisation with identity re-check and event, Pipeline.launch_reviewer with running/interactive/blocked/detached events, launch_token binding, KeyboardInterrupt leaves the reviewer running) and the PR is honest that no live test ran and that the write is unproven, but the test at test_interactive.py:188-189 asserts the `--add-dir` value without the prompt position, so the suite passes with the bug. Worker paths: no regression found.
dimensions.pr10: Argv (interactive.py:181-186): `claude --bg --name workflow-<run>-reviewer --safe-mode --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config {...} --add-dir <run> --tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write --allowedTools Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json) --permission-mode dontAsk <prompt>`. This works against the real CLI: the prompt follows the single-valued `--permission-mode`, and `Edit(//abs/path)` is the documented spelling (docs: file permissions are checked against Edit(path)/Read(path) rules only, a Write(...) rule is accepted but never consulted; `//path` is absolute from the filesystem root). Proven live on disk: review-smoke-001/review.launch.log "backgrounded · 5865c9a6", review.completion.json accepted, review.stop.json stopped:true with stopped_at, terminals.json has the review pane w5:pW, and the registry lists dccd22b5 (stopped) and 5865c9a6 (done). Pane: attach_reviewer_pane returns None without a mapping and is idempotent; attach_panels builds three panes on a fresh tab via launched_nodes(); but attach_panels:283-284 still refuses when terminals.json exists, so `attach` cannot add the reviewer to a tab created at `start --herdr`. Stop: stop_session generalised with identity re-check and stopped_at, stop issued before finish_review, and attempted again on failure. Weaknesses: the completion binds `reviewer_session`, which the model has to discover (the live transcript shows it copied the UUID from the controller's own events.jsonl and automatic-review.json in the run directory), whereas the identity is already enforced out of band at automatic.py:298-299; the test does not pin the prompt position (test_interactive.py:204-230), so the swallow bug can be reintroduced by a reorder; no Pipeline.launch_reviewer symmetry (no "running"/"blocked" launch events); receipt carries `launch_token: None`; run_reviewer checks a clean worktree but not HEAD == candidate. Worker paths: `launch()`/`reconcile()` refactor preserves main's ordering (name-conflict check, receipt journal, then `claude --bg`); one low regression is that `attach` on a fresh tab raises after the reviewer has been stopped because launched_nodes() still includes it.
dimensions.pr11: Argv (interactive.py:223-226): `claude --bg --name workflow-<run>-reviewer --safe-mode --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config {...} --tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write --allowedTools Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json) --add-dir <run> --permission-mode dontAsk <prompt>`, with an explicit comment that `--tools`, `--allowedTools` and `--add-dir` are variadic and the prompt must follow the single-valued option, and a test that pins it (test_interactive.py:245-249: `command[-3:-1] == ["--permission-mode","dontAsk"]` and every variadic option before it). Proven live: four registry rows under workflow-project-workflows-001-reviewer (7eb01f17 stopped = the swallowed-prompt attempt, a4c348e5, 25d99bf4, f36b923d done) and the accept-path artifacts in the ultra scratchpad smoke-run (review.interactive.json bound to f36b923d with launch_token a29c684b…, events running → interactive → "Reviewer pane attached" → stopped, review.stop.json stopped:true, automatic-review.json succeeded with accepted_at, terminals.json review pane w5:p11). The verdict is bound to a controller-issued launch_token placed in the prompt plus an out-of-band identity/independence check (automatic.py:325-328), which is deterministic where PR 10's UUID discovery is not. Pane/attach is the most complete: attach_panels extends an existing workers' tab (interactive.py:291-295), a fresh tab gets the third pane (334-336), attach_reviewer_panel refuses duplicates, Pipeline.launch_reviewer is best-effort and propagates Ctrl-C after recording it. Stop is the most complete: stop_reviewer re-checks identity (pipeline.py:183-221), every failure path stops the reviewer (automatic.py:353), a failed post-acceptance stop keeps the durable verdict and is retried on resume (automatic.py:240, 358-362; reviewer_stop_pending at 467), and a Ctrl-C inside the launch window is reconciled through reconcile_reviewer rather than relaunched. Minor: the pane is only attempted when HERDR_ENV == "1" (no timeline note otherwise), attach_reviewer_panel is not idempotent (harmless since resume bypasses launch_reviewer), worker run() gains a `<node>.prompt.txt` side effect for slice C, and run_reviewer no longer requires an automatic plan. Worker paths: no regression found.
dimensions.ranking_reason: PR 9's reviewer never receives its prompt (variadic --add-dir swallows it) and could not write its verdict if it did (Write under dontAsk with no allow rule), and its wait treats the resulting `blocked` state as fatal; by the rubric a live-broken reviewer scores accordingly regardless of its otherwise clean structure. PR 10 and PR 11 both produce an argv that works against the real CLI and both have registry-confirmed live sessions; PR 11 ranks above PR 10 because it pins the option order in a test, binds the completion to a prompt-supplied launch token instead of a UUID the model must discover, adds the reviewer pane through `attach` to an existing tab, stops the reviewer on every failure path and retries an unconfirmed post-acceptance stop on resume, whereas PR 10 leaves the prompt position unpinned, cannot extend an existing tab via `attach`, and records fewer launch events.
dimensions.verifier_note: All seven high/medium findings survive verification. PR 9's reviewer cannot receive its task (commander probe reproduces the swallow on its exact argv shape) and could not write a verdict if it did (no allow rule under dontAsk, denied live in both other PRs), and its wait raises on the `blocked` state that a promptless or questioning session shows; that is live-broken regardless of its clean structure. PR 10 and PR 11 both produce an argv that parses correctly and both have registry-confirmed sessions and on-disk accept-path artifacts. PR 11 stays ahead of PR 10: it pins and explains the option order, binds the file to a controller-issued token instead of a UUID the model had to scavenge from the controller's own files, extends an existing tab through `attach` (with tests), persists the verdict before the stop and retries a failed stop on resume. Two new low findings on PR 10 (an unreachable stop-recovery branch hidden by the test fake, and a failed post-acceptance stop discarding the verdict, shared with PR 9) and one low risk on PR 11 (a valid file written by a session that ends `blocked` waits until the deadline) do not change the order.

findings.title: Reviewer prompt is swallowed by the variadic --add-dir option; the session starts with no task
findings.detail: PR 9 places the positional prompt immediately after `--add-dir <run>`. `claude --help` declares `--add-dir <directories...>` (variadic) and commander consumes following arguments as further values until the next dash-prefixed argument, so the prompt is parsed as a second directory and the reviewer never receives its instructions. PR 11 hit exactly this live (attempt 1: "the prompt that followed it was swallowed and the session started idle", session 7eb01f17 present in the native registry as stopped). PR 9's test asserts the `--add-dir` value but never the prompt's position, so the suite is green with the bug. Main's worker launch is unaffected because its prompt follows `--permission-mode <mode>` or the boolean `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:216-220: `command = [self.executable, "--bg", "--name", self.launch_name(REVIEWER), "--safe-mode", "--strict-mcp-config", "--mcp-config", '{"mcpServers":{}}', "--tools", self.reviewer_tools, "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]`. `claude --help`: `--add-dir <directories...>  Additional directories to allow tool access to`. commander README (Variadic option): values are read "until the first argument starting with a dash". `claude agents --json --all` → `7eb01f17 ... workflow-project-workflows-001-reviewer background stopped` (PR 11's attempt 1). Test gap: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/test_interactive.py:189 `self.assertEqual(command[command.index("--add-dir") + 1], str(self.directory))` with no assertion on `command[-1]`'s neighbour.
findings.verifier_reason: Personally reproduced with a commander probe on the exact argv shape, and cross-checked against `claude --help`, PR 11's live record and the native registry. PR 9's test asserts only the --add-dir value, so the suite is green with the bug.
findings.verifier_evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:217-220: `"--tools", self.reviewer_tools, "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]`. `claude --help` (2.1.280) line 10: `--add-dir <directories...>`; line 147: `--permission-mode <mode>`. Probe `node scratchpad/probe/variadic.js` (commander 12.1.0): PR9 shape -> `"addDir":["/run","Review this candidate"],"args":[]`; PR10 shape -> `"addDir":["/run"],...,"args":["Review this candidate"]`; PR11 shape -> `"args":["Review this candidate"]`. PR 11 handoff line 53: "`--add-dir` is variadic, so the prompt that followed it was swallowed and the session started idle". `claude agents --json --all`: `7eb01f17 workflow-project-workflows-001-reviewer stopped`. Test gap: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/test_interactive.py:189 asserts `command[command.index("--add-dir") + 1] == str(self.directory)` and nothing about the prompt's neighbour.

findings.title: Write under --permission-mode dontAsk with no allow rule: the reviewer cannot write its completion file
findings.detail: PR 9 gives the reviewer the Write tool but no `--allowedTools` rule and runs it in `dontAsk`. The permissions docs state dontAsk auto-denies every call that would otherwise prompt except tools pre-approved by allow rules, and that files in `--add-dir` directories follow the current permission mode for edits. So the one write the protocol depends on is denied. PR 10's live attempt 1 recorded the exact denial message. PR 9's own PR body flags this as unproven; its handoff's proposed fallback ("--add-dir plus a bypass mode") would remove containment rather than fix the rule.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:184-185: `reviewer_tools = "Read,Glob,Grep,Write"` / `reviewer_permission_mode = "dontAsk"`; no `--allowedTools` anywhere in the file (`grep -n allowedTools` returns nothing). Docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions): `dontAsk` — "Auto-denies every call that would otherwise prompt; file reads in your working directories ... still run, as do tools pre-approved via /permissions or permissions.allow rules"; additional directories — "file editing permissions follow the current permission mode". PR 10 handoff: "had its Write to review.completion.json denied twice ('Permission to use Write has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode')". PR 9 body: "dontAsk plus a write into an --add-dir path ... are unproven".
findings.verifier_reason: PR 9 passes no allow rule at all; both live PRs recorded that even an explicit `Write(//path)` rule is denied under dontAsk, so a bare Write with no rule is certainly denied. PR 9's own body and handoff admit this is unproven and propose a bypass mode as the fallback.
findings.verifier_evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:184-185: `reviewer_tools = "Read,Glob,Grep,Write"` / `reviewer_permission_mode = "dontAsk"`; `grep -rn allowedTools md-manager-opus/workflow/` -> exit 1 (no matches). PR 10 handoff /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:59-60: "denied twice ('Permission to use Write has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode')" and "four print-mode probes ... `--allowedTools "Write(//abs/path)"` is ignored (denied, with and without `--safe-mode`); `--allowedTools "Edit(//abs/path)"` allows that one write". PR 11 handoff line 54: "under `--permission-mode dontAsk` a rule spelled `Write(//path)` never matches". PR 9 handoff line 63: "`dontAsk` plus a write into an `--add-dir` path ... are all still unproven"; line 55: "the fallback would be `--add-dir` plus a bypass mode".

findings.title: wait_review treats the native `blocked` state as fatal, killing the run when the reviewer asks a human
findings.detail: PR 9 mirrors wait_handoffs and raises as soon as the reviewer row reports `blocked`. Both live PRs observed that a reviewer which ends its turn asking a person (for example for the permission it lacks) is reported as `blocked` by `claude agents`. The slice A PRD's acceptance says a reviewer that stops to ask a question can be answered in the pane and the run resumes. In PR 9 that is impossible: the operator never gets the chance, and combined with the two launch defects the run is guaranteed to end without a verdict.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:207-208: `if row["state"] == "blocked": raise RuntimeError("Reviewer blocked; inspect quota or native error. No billing/provider fallback.")`. /home/agentops/dev/md-manager/docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:63: "A reviewer that stops to ask a question can be answered in the pane, and the run resumes when the completion file appears and the session goes idle." PR 10 handoff attempt 1: "It ended its turn asking a person to grant the permission or paste the JSON; `claude agents` reported the session as `blocked`; `wait_review` treated `blocked` as fatal" (PR 10 then changed this; PR 11 automatic.py:219-223 likewise treats it as waiting).
findings.verifier_reason: The raise is there and the PRD acceptance criterion it contradicts is verbatim. Both live PRs observed that a reviewer needing a person (and even a promptless session) reports `blocked`, so PR 9's reviewer would be killed immediately. It does mirror main's wait_handoffs (automatic.py:104-105), which the PRD asked for, but the PRD's acceptance bullet overrides that mirror.
findings.verifier_evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:207-208: `if row["state"] == "blocked": raise RuntimeError("Reviewer blocked; inspect quota or native error. No billing/provider fallback.")`. /home/agentops/dev/md-manager/docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md section 5: "A reviewer that stops to ask a question can be answered in the pane, and the run resumes when the completion file appears and the session goes idle." PR 10 handoff line 59: "It ended its turn asking a person ... `claude agents` reported the session as `blocked`; `wait_review` treated `blocked` as fatal". PR 11 handoff line 53 (swallowed-prompt session): "the controller then saw the session's `blocked` state and stopped it". Main /home/agentops/dev/md-manager/workflow/automatic.py:104-105 has the same raise for workers. PR 10 fixes it at md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:201-210; PR 11 at md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:219-223.

findings.title: Reviewer is never stopped on deadline, rejected file or blocked verdict
findings.detail: native_review's failure path only marks automatic-review.json blocked; no stop is issued, so a reviewer still `working` at the deadline, or one whose file was rejected, keeps consuming usage until an operator notices. The handoff documents this as a deliberate choice for the deadline, but the same code path covers every failure. PR 10 and PR 11 both stop the reviewer with the identity re-check on every failure path.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:284-288: `except BaseException as error: receipt.update(status="blocked", error=str(error)); raise` with no stop call; stop_reviewer is only invoked on the success path at automatic.py:281. Handoff HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md: "A deadline does not stop the reviewer." Compare /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:308-313 and /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:349-356 which call the stop on failure.
findings.verifier_reason: The only stop call is on the success path; the shared failure handler marks the receipt blocked and re-raises without any stop. The handoff documents the deadline case but the same handler covers rejection and blocked verdicts too.
findings.verifier_evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:281: `runtime.stop_reviewer()  # Identity re-checked; the transcript stays resumable.` (success path only); 284-288: `except KeyboardInterrupt: raise` / `except BaseException as error: receipt.update(status="blocked", error=str(error)); raise` with no stop. `grep -n stop_reviewer` in opus/workflow: only automatic.py:281 and pipeline.py:149 (def). Handoff HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md:58: "A deadline does not stop the reviewer." Compare md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:308-313 and md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:349-356, which stop on every failure.

findings.title: status() omits the reviewer and `attach` never adds the third pane
findings.detail: InteractiveSessions.status() still iterates NODES only, so `workflow.interactive status` never shows the reviewer session. attach_panels was refactored but its node set is unchanged, so `attach` (fresh tab or existing) never allocates a reviewer pane; only the review node's own attach_reviewer_pane call does, and if that fails the only recovery is attach-one. The PRD's work item 3 asks for the third pane in attach_panels and attach-one; only the latter was delivered.

findings.title: Prompt asks for an atomic temp-file-then-rename write the reviewer's tool set cannot perform; naming inconsistencies
findings.detail: The completion prompt tells the reviewer to write the file "atomically (temporary file then rename)", but the reviewer has no Bash and Write cannot rename; PR 11's prompt explicitly says the opposite. The test named `..._launches_read_only_...` asserts a tool set that includes Write. The reviewer is `--node reviewer` with REVIEWER="reviewer" but all its files are `review.*` through file_prefix(), while PR 10 and PR 11 use `--node review` throughout.

findings.title: Clean generalisation and honest reporting despite the live defects
findings.detail: The refactors are small and behaviour-preserving: attach_pane extracted from attach_panels, stop_session extracted from stop_workers with the same identity re-check and marker, Pipeline.launch_reviewer records running/interactive/blocked/detached events symmetric with the workers, the completion is bound to a controller-issued launch_token in the prompt, a KeyboardInterrupt leaves the reviewer running and resumable, and worktree/bundle/diff hashes are re-checked before acceptance. The PR body and handoff state plainly that no live test ran and that the write is unproven, which is what let the defects be found.

findings.title: Launch argv works against the real CLI and the live run proves the full protocol
findings.detail: The reviewer argv uses the documented `Edit(//absolute/path)` allow-rule spelling under dontAsk, keeps Bash/MCP/bypass out, and places the prompt after the single-valued `--permission-mode`, so it is not swallowed. The on-disk smoke run shows the session launched, the pane attached, the completion file accepted, and the stop confirmed; the native registry corroborates both claimed sessions.

findings.title: Completion binding relies on the reviewer discovering its own session UUID
findings.detail: PR 10 requires the completion file to carry `reviewer_session` equal to the launched UUID, and the prompt tells the model to take it "as shown by `claude agents`", a command the reviewer cannot run (no Bash). In the live run the model found the UUID only because it read the controller's own events.jsonl and automatic-review.json inside the --add-dir'd run directory; a reviewer that does not happen to read those files cannot produce an acceptable file and the run times out. The field adds no security, since the controller already checks the live row's sessionId against the launched UUID and worker distinctness out of band. PR 9 and PR 11 instead put a controller-issued launch_token in the prompt.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:159: `"reviewer_session": "<your own session UUID as shown by `claude agents`; the controller verifies it>"`; automatic.py:184: `if item["reviewer_session"] != session_id or session_id in worker_ids: raise`. Transcript ~/.claude/projects/-home-agentops--local-state-md-manager-workflows-smoke-review-smoke-001-review-worktree/5865c9a6-….jsonl: first content mention of the UUID is line 205, a tool_result reading events.jsonl ("Reviewer session 5865c9a6-… launched in review-worktree"), then line 300 reading automatic-review.json (`"session_id": "5865c9a6-…"`), then the Write at line 311. Out-of-band check already at automatic.py:298-299: `intent = runtime.stop_session(REVIEW_NODE); if intent["session_id"] != decision["reviewer_session"]`.
findings.verifier_reason: The prompt instructs the model to use a command it cannot run (no Bash), and the live transcript shows the UUID entered the model's context only by reading the controller's own files in the --add-dir'd run directory. The controller independently binds the file to the live row and checks worker distinctness, so the field adds no assurance and one failure mode.

findings.title: Prompt position is not pinned; the swallow bug can be reintroduced silently
findings.detail: PR 10 avoided the variadic trap but the launch test only checks each option's value, not that the prompt directly follows a single-valued option. Nothing in the code or tests records why the order matters, so a future reorder (for example moving `--add-dir` last to match PR 9's shape) would pass the suite and break the reviewer live. PR 11 pins the order with an explicit assertion and comment.

Compare /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/test_interactive.py:245-249: `self.assertEqual(command[-3:-1], ["--permission-mode", "dontAsk"])` and `for option in ("--tools", "--allowedTools", "--add-dir"): self.assertLess(command.index(option), command.index("--permission-mode"))`.
findings.verifier_reason: PR 10's launch test checks each option's value and that the prompt is last, but nothing about what precedes it; the code's docstring explains only the Edit-rule family, not the ordering constraint. PR 11 pins both.
findings.verifier_evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/test_interactive.py:216-227: asserts `--tools`, `--allowedTools`, `--permission-mode`, `--add-dir` values, forbidden flags, and `self.assertTrue(command[-1].startswith("Review this candidate"))` only. Docstring interactive.py:164-171 mentions `Edit(//absolute/path)` and `Write(...)` being ignored, nothing about variadic ordering. Compare md-manager-ultra/workflow/test_interactive.py:245-249: `self.assertEqual(command[-3:-1], ["--permission-mode", "dontAsk"])` and `for option in ("--tools", "--allowedTools", "--add-dir"): self.assertLess(command.index(option), command.index("--permission-mode"))`, plus the comment at interactive.py:219-221.

findings.title: `attach` cannot add the reviewer pane to an existing tab; attach after the reviewer stopped fails for the workers too
findings.detail: attach_panels still refuses whenever terminals.json exists, so after a normal `start --herdr` only the review node's own attach_reviewer_pane call can create the third pane; if that fails the operator's only recovery is attach-one. On a fresh tab, launched_nodes() includes `review` as soon as its receipt exists, so `attach` after the reviewer was stopped raises "Cannot attach an unverified/missing session" even though both workers are attachable. The reuse-observers branch iterates the observer mapping rather than launched_nodes, so it would not attach a launched reviewer either (not reachable from pipeline.py's `attach`).

PR 11 handles the existing-tab case at /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:291-295.

findings.title: Less launch/event symmetry with workers: no Pipeline.launch_reviewer, null launch_token, no HEAD check in run_reviewer
findings.detail: The review node calls sessions.run_reviewer directly and records only an `interactive` event after a successful launch; there is no `running` event before it and a launch failure produces no `blocked` review event (only an incidental "Could not confirm reviewer stop"). The reviewer receipt records `launch_token: None`. run_reviewer verifies the review worktree is clean but not that HEAD is the candidate commit (PR 9 and PR 11 check both); the caller checks it on the resume path only.

Compare ultra interactive.py:205-206 `if git(cwd, "rev-parse", "HEAD") != candidate_commit or git(cwd, "status", "--porcelain")`.

findings.title: Argv correct, ordering explained and pinned, launch_token binding, four registry-confirmed live sessions
findings.detail: PR 11 found the variadic swallow live, documented it in a code comment, fixed the order and pinned it in a test that asserts the prompt follows `--permission-mode dontAsk` and that every variadic option precedes it. The completion binds a controller-issued launch_token that is in the prompt (deterministic) and identity/independence are checked out of band against `claude agents`. The accept-path artifacts on disk show the full protocol: launch, pane, acceptance with accepted_at, identity-checked stop, resumable transcript.
