findings.title: Most complete pane, attach, stop and interrupt handling
findings.detail: attach_panels extends an existing workers' tab with the reviewer pane and refuses duplicates, a fresh tab gets three panes, launch_reviewer is best-effort and records the reason while propagating a Ctrl-C after recording it. stop_reviewer re-checks identity and records the intent; the reviewer is stopped on every failure path; a failed stop after acceptance keeps the durable verdict and is retried on resume; a Ctrl-C inside the launch window binds the session that the launch produced via reconcile_reviewer rather than relaunching.

findings.title: Pane attempt gated on HERDR_ENV leaves no timeline note; attach_reviewer_panel is not idempotent
findings.detail: launch_reviewer only tries the pane when terminals.json exists and HERDR_ENV == "1", so a controller run from a non-Herdr terminal against a run that has a tab records nothing about the missing pane (PR 9 records `detached`, PR 10 records the failure). attach_reviewer_panel raises on an existing reviewer pane instead of returning the mapping as PR 9/10 do; this is unreachable through the automatic resume path (which bypasses launch_reviewer) but a second `attach` yields only the generic "Terminal mappings already exist" message.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/pipeline.py:155: `if (self.directory / "terminals.json").exists() and os.environ.get("HERDR_ENV") == "1":`; interactive.py:371-372: `if REVIEW in mapping: raise RuntimeError("Reviewer pane already allocated; ...")`. herdr() itself raises without HERDR_ENV (main workflow/observer.py:43-45).

findings.title: Worker launch path gains a prompt-file side effect and run_reviewer drops the automatic-plan check
findings.detail: run() now writes `<node>.prompt.txt` (0600) before every worker launch to feed slice C's run-inputs export; benign (same write-then-chmod pattern as sessions.py's print mode, inside a 0700 directory) but it widens the shared worker path for a slice A change. run_reviewer requires only `mode == interactive`, not an automatic plan as PR 9 and PR 10 do; harmless because only the automatic review node calls it.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:181-182: `write_private(self.directory / f"{node}.prompt.txt", prompt)`; 241-243 write_private = write_text then chmod 0o600; 197-198: `if self.plan.get("mode") != "interactive": raise ValueError("Expected an interactive run plan")` versus opus interactive.py:189 `if self.plan.get("mode") != "interactive" or not self.plan.get("automatic")`.

findings.title: No regression to the worker launch/attach/stop paths; shared flags verified against the CLI; attach-one naming differs in PR 9
findings.detail: None of the three PRs changed the worker argv (`--bg --name --safe-mode --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config --tools --permission-mode [--dangerously-skip-permissions] <prompt>`), and `--safe-mode`, `claude stop <id>` and `claude attach <id>` all exist in the installed CLI. PR 10's launch()/reconcile() extraction and PR 11's launch()/reconcile() extraction keep main's ordering (name-conflict check, receipt journalled, then `claude --bg`, then settle). PR 9 and PR 11 keep stop_workers' semantics through stop_session; PR 10 adds `stopped_at`. The only cross-PR discrepancy an operator will hit is `attach-one --node reviewer` (PR 9) versus `--node review` (PR 10/11), while all three name the native session `workflow-<run>-reviewer` and the files `review.*`.
findings.evidence: main /home/agentops/dev/md-manager/workflow/interactive.py:148-153 worker argv unchanged in all three diffs; `claude --help`: `--safe-mode`, `--bg`, `--permission-mode <mode>` (single value); `claude stop --help`: "Usage: claude stop <id>"; `claude attach --help`: "Usage: claude attach <id>". opus interactive.py:400 `choices=[*NODES, REVIEWER]` (REVIEWER="reviewer"); high interactive.py:384 `choices=SESSION_NODES` ("review"); ultra interactive.py:399 `choices=NODES + (REVIEW,)` ("review").

findings.title: wait_review's stopped-reviewer recovery branch is unreachable through review_native; the fake hides it
findings.detail: wait_review returns early from a confirmed review.stop.json, intended for a controller interrupted between the stop and finish_review. But review_native reaches wait_review only after run_reviewer -> reconcile -> locate, and the real locate raises for a stopped row ("Session is not attachable: 'stopped'" or "No live native PID") and reconcile raises on None, so the branch is dead in production and the accepted file on disk is discarded (status blocked, manual reconciliation). The unit test calls wait_review directly, and FakeSessions.run_reviewer returns the receipt without calling locate, so the suite cannot see this. The window is sub-second (between automatic.py:298 and 301), hence low, but the handoff's "stopped-reviewer recovery" claim overstates the coverage.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:171-174: `if stop.exists() and read_json(stop)["stopped"]: return read_review_completion(runtime, digest, bundle, read_json(stop)["session_id"])`. Path to it: automatic.py:285 `launch = runtime.sessions.run_reviewer(prompt, completion_path)` -> interactive.py:175-176 `if (...interactive.json).exists(): return self.reconcile(REVIEW_NODE)` -> interactive.py:120-122 `row = self.locate(...); if row is None: raise RuntimeError("Existing launch cannot be reconciled...")` -> interactive.py:83-89 `if row.get("state") not in {"idle","working","blocked","done"}: raise RuntimeError(f"Session is not attachable: ...")` / `if not isinstance(pid, int) or pid <= 0: raise RuntimeError("No live native PID...")`. Registry shows stopped sessions with state `stopped` (dccd22b5). Test: test_automatic.py:572-576 `test_stopped_reviewer_recovery_rereads_the_accepted_file` calls `self.wait()` directly; FakeSessions.run_reviewer test_automatic.py:36-41 returns the receipt unconditionally and FakeSessions.inventory (63-64) returns [] once review.stop.json exists.

findings.title: A failed post-acceptance stop discards the accepted verdict
findings.detail: In PR 9 and PR 10 the reviewer stop is issued before the verdict is persisted; a stop that raises (non-zero `claude stop`, or a pid still alive at the immediate single check) lands in the generic failure handler, marks the receipt blocked, never writes review.json, and the next resume refuses ("needs reconciliation; no automatic relaunch"). The completion file remains on disk but an operator must hand-reconcile a finished, paid review. PR 11 persists review.json and status succeeded first, then stops, and retries an unconfirmed stop on resume. Low because live stops succeeded in both smoke runs and stop_session mirrors main's worker stop.
findings.evidence: PR 9 /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:280-282: `runtime.validate_review(review); runtime.stop_reviewer(); receipt.update(status="succeeded", review=review)` then 286-288 `except BaseException ... status="blocked"`. PR 10 /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:298-301: `intent = runtime.stop_session(REVIEW_NODE)` ... `return finish_review(...)` (review.json written inside finish_review at 271), 308-315 blocked on any exception; review_candidate 236-239 refuses non-launching/running receipts. stop_session's single immediate check: pipeline.py `if any(row ... pid) or pid_alive(intent["pid"]): raise RuntimeError(... "termination is not established")` (opus pipeline.py:135-137, same in high). PR 11 /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:336-337 `_decide` + `save_json(receipt_path, receipt)` before 358-363 stop with "resume retries the stop", and review_candidate 238-241 retries via `reviewer_stopped`.

findings.title: A valid completion file written by a session that ends `blocked` waits until the deadline
findings.detail: PR 11's wait_review accepts the file only when the row is idle or done; a reviewer that writes a valid file and then ends its turn with a question shows `blocked` (as both live PRs observed for questioning sessions), so the controller waits up to review_timeout_seconds, then fails the run and stops the reviewer with a valid verdict on disk and no second reviewer. PR 10 accepts in the blocked state too. PR 11 is PRD-literal ("the session goes idle") and its prompt tells the reviewer to end its turn after the write, and attempts 3 and 4 accepted normally, so this is a low risk rather than a bug.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:219-225: `if row["state"] == "blocked" and not attention: ... runtime.event("review", "interactive", "Reviewer needs attention ... waiting until the deadline")` then `if row["state"] in {"idle", "done"} and path.exists(): return read_review_completion(runtime)`; deadline raise at 214-215. PR 10 /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:210: `if row["state"] in {"idle", "done", "blocked"} and path.exists(): return ...`. PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md section 5: "the run resumes when the completion file appears and the session goes idle". PR 11 prompt automatic.py:176-178: "write it once, complete, as your last action, then end your turn and do not modify it afterwards. The controller accepts it only when your session is idle." PR 11 handoff line 54 (attempt 2): the controller waited through `done` to the 1205 s deadline when no file existed.

findings.title: The live accept-path artifacts match the handoff, and the blocked-as-waiting fix is tested

dimensions.summary: I compared the contract and schema work in the three worktrees against main's conventions (contracts/*/README.md, v1.ts as the zod source of truth, export.ts regeneration, verification.py's jsonschema helper), the PRD tables, and the real run data on disk (project-workflows-001's plan.json/policy.json/review.json, PR 10's smoke artifacts). I regenerated every PR's JSON on scratchpad copies (all three: no drift), probed each completion schema with the venv's jsonschema, and traced each PR's Python binding/cross-field code and the persisted-review validators. Headline: PR 11 has the best-designed and only end-to-end-coherent contracts (enums taken from the policy schema, nullable transport matching old runs, adapter validates with the contract at serve time, viewer keeps loading 1.0.0 exports), with its one convention break, a hand-written reviewCompletion schema, documented and Python-tested but leaving no TS type or drift test. PR 9 ships a small, convention-pure reviewCompletion with the best cross-field rules in both languages but loose patterns, a triplicated finding schema and a PRD row contradicting its own launch_token binding. PR 10 does the most contract work with good tests and READMEs, yet has two contract-vs-reality bugs (check kinds missing typecheck/integration; reviewer_transport required while its own export omits it for the reference run), a shape change under a fixed 1.1.0 literal, a version/contract_version inconsistency with no workflow README update, an export bump that breaks the viewer for new runs, and a latent approved-with-open-P1 review.json its own validateReviewResult rejects.
dimensions.pr9: Slice A only. reviewCompletion is done the repo way: zod in contracts/workflow/v1.ts:94-109 inside the schemas map, examples.ts fixture, three new contract tests (~15 negative cases), README table row plus an authority paragraph, and the committed JSON is byte-identical to a fresh `contracts:export` run. It is the only PR that enforces both cross-field rules (blocked needs findings; approved cannot carry an unresolved P0/P1) in TS (v1.ts:168-175) and mirrors them in Python (automatic.py:188-192), and the Python side uses the repo's validate_schema helper. Weaknesses: the schema uses the workflow envelope's contract_version but binds `launch_token: id` (any non-empty string; probe accepted 'x'), candidate_commit inherits the 40|64-hex `sha`, and run_id is unconstrained, so it is the loosest of the three; the finding schema is defined a third time by hand in automatic.py:128-140 for print mode; and the PRD's "Bound to" row (docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:26) still says "reviewer session UUID" while the schema binds a launch token, with no explanation in the handoff. No projects/export work, so nothing to fault on (2) or (3), but nothing to credit either.
dimensions.pr10: Broadest contract surface: reviewCompletion (zod, generated, examples, tests), projects reviewResult 1.1.0, runInputs 1.2.0, a runInputsResponse wrapper for the null case, requirement_verbatim, validators, thorough labeled negative tests and a README versions paragraph; print-mode structured output is derived from the generated JSON (single source), and the live smoke proves the reviewer_session UUID binding works. But the design has concrete defects: runInputs.checks[].kind (v1.ts:94) omits `typecheck` and `integration` that main's verification.schema.json allows, so a valid policy yields inputs the contract rejects; automatic.reviewer_transport is required (v1.ts:132) while export_state.py:103 passes plan.automatic through raw and test_export.py:107 asserts the key is absent for a re-exported 1.0.0 run, i.e. the reference run exports data its own contract rejects (README tells the adapter to "treat as print"); reviewResult keeps `contract_version: '1.1.0'` (v1.ts:66) while gaining a field labelled 1.2.0 (v1.ts:62); reviewCompletion uses `version` (v1.ts:111) unlike every other message's `contract_version`, and contracts/workflow/README.md is untouched; export jumps 1.0.0 to 1.2.0 while server/projects.ts:52 still requires 1.0.0, so new runs are rejected by the viewer until slice B (acknowledged); and finish_review (automatic.py:271-276) persists an approved verdict with an open P0/P1 before raising, a shape validateReviewResult throws on.
dimensions.pr11: Projects contracts are the strongest: reviewResult and runInputs at 1.2.0 with a shared isBlockingFinding, nested reviewer identity with `independent: literal(true)`, requirement_found_in as lane list, check kinds equal to the policy schema's enum (v1.ts:105), nullable reviewer_transport that matches what old plans actually have (v1.ts:138, export_state.py legacy tests), rich cross-field rules (unique ids, browser checks need scenarios, automatic settings iff automatic mode, links need a quote), labelled negative tests, and a README Versions section. It is the only PR whose export section, adapter zod (server/projects.ts:72-165 mirrors export_state.py), projection and serve-time validateReviewResult/validateRunInputs (server/projects.ts:697,705) form a closed loop, and EXPORT_VERSIONS 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 keeps project-workflows-001 loading. The reviewCompletion schema is hand-written (no v1.ts entry, no TS type, no examples.ts fixture, no drift/negative test in contract.test.ts) which breaks the "v1.ts is authoritative" rule; it is documented in the README as hand-written with the verification.schema.json precedent, is the strictest of the three (uuid launch_token, 40-hex commit, run_id pattern), and is covered by 11 Python schema negatives plus a prompt-enum test. Smaller issues: 1.1.0 is documented but never emitted; `mode` is redefined as automatic|manual (v1.ts:131, export_state.py:143), dropping plan.json's actual `interactive` value the PRD C table asks for; _decide rewrites an approved-with-open-P1 verdict to blocked in review.json (automatic.py:282), so the record differs from the reviewer's file; stop.confirmed_at is file mtime (export_state.py:121).
dimensions.ranking_reason: PR 11 leads because its contracts are the only ones proven coherent from export to adapter to viewer on the real run, its enums and nullability are drawn from the policy schema and the actual receipts rather than one observed run, and its single convention break is explicit, precedented, stricter than the generated alternatives, and tested from the only language that consumes it. PR 9 is second: a small surface with no contract-vs-reality defect, the best cross-field rules in both TS and Python, and full adherence to the generate-from-v1.ts convention; it drops points for loose patterns, a triplicated finding schema and a PRD binding row it contradicts. PR 10 is last despite the most contract work because it carries the most real defects on this dimension: two enums/required fields that reject valid data (check kinds; reviewer_transport on the reference run), a shape change under a fixed 1.1.0 literal, a version-key inconsistency with no README update, an export bump that breaks the viewer for new runs before slice B lands, and a persisted approved-with-open-P1 record that its own validateReviewResult would throw on.
dimensions.verifier_note: Ranking unchanged after verification. PR 11 leads on this dimension: its projects contracts take enums and invariants from the sources of truth (policy schema kinds at v1.ts:105; the browser-scenario rule at v1.ts:226 is the same rule workflow/verification.py:67 enforces on policies, so the contract never rejects a policy the verifier accepts), its nullable reviewer_transport is derived from receipts rather than defaulted, and it is the only PR whose export section, adapter zod mirror and serve-time validateRunInputs/validateReviewResult (server/projects.ts:697,705) form a loop that still loads the 1.0.0 run on disk. Its one convention break, the hand-written reviewCompletion schema, is documented, precedented, stricter than the generated alternatives, and tested from Python; its `version` key choice is shared with PR 10. PR 9 is second: a small, convention-pure surface (zod in the schemas map, fixture, three tests, README row and paragraph, byte-identical regeneration), the only PR enforcing both cross-field rules in TS and Python before anything is persisted; it loses points for the loosest patterns (launch_token and run_id are any non-empty string, candidate_commit accepts 64-hex), a third hand-rolled copy of the finding schema for print mode, and a PRD binding row it contradicts without explanation. PR 10 is last despite the most contract work and the best-labelled negative tests, because it carries the only contract-vs-reality defects: reviewer_transport required while its own export and test produce inputs without it for the reference run (high), the check-kind enum narrower than the policy schema (medium), an approved-with-open-P1 record persisted that both its TS validator and its own `workflow export` reject (medium), and an export bump that hides every new run from the viewer until a separate feature run lands (medium). Two of the reviewer's PR 10 findings (`version` key, 1.1.0 label) were overstated and are now low; that does not change the order because the remaining defects are the ones that matter.

findings.title: runInputs check kind enum rejects kinds the policy schema allows
findings.detail: PR 10's runInputs contract restricts checks[].kind to build|unit|browser|contract, derived from the one observed policy, while main's policy schema permits typecheck and integration as well. Any policy using those kinds (valid today) would export inputs that fail the contract and, once slice C's adapter validates with it, 500 the inputs route. PR 11 copies the policy schema's enum exactly.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/contracts/projects/v1.ts:94 `kind: z.enum(['build', 'unit', 'browser', 'contract'])`. Main policy schema: python walk of contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json printed `/properties/workers/items/properties/checks/items/properties/kind ['build', 'typecheck', 'unit', 'integration', 'contract', 'browser']`. PR 11: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/contracts/projects/v1.ts:105 `kind: z.enum(['build', 'typecheck', 'unit', 'integration', 'contract', 'browser'])`.
findings.verifier_reason: The enum gap is real: PR 10's contract accepts only four kinds while main's policy schema allows six, so a policy with a `typecheck` or `integration` check (valid today) would export inputs the contract rejects. But it is latent: the only real policy on disk uses build/unit/browser/contract only, no adapter validates runInputs yet, and the fix is one line. A real contract bug, not a merge blocker.

Live policy.json kinds (python): ui frontend-build build, frontend-unit-regression unit, project-workflows-browser browser; adapter backend-unit unit, backend-regression unit, shared-contract contract, backend-build build. PR 10's own re-export test asserts the key is absent, and the feature README tells the future adapter to 'treat as print', i.e. the adapter must patch data to satisfy the contract. findings.title: Persisted review.json can be approved-with-open-P1, a shape its own contract validator rejects
findings.detail: finish_review writes review.json with the reviewer's literal verdict and findings, then raises if the verdict is approved with an unresolved P0/P1. export_review copies that verdict verbatim, and validateReviewResult throws on 'approved' + unresolved P0/P1, so slice B's adapter would fail to serve the review for exactly the run where a reader most needs to see why it stopped. PR 9 rejects such a file before anything is persisted; PR 11 normalises the verdict to blocked so the record validates.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:271-276 `review = {... "verdict": decision["verdict"], "findings": decision["findings"]}` ... `save_json(runtime.directory / "review.json", review)` ... `if review["verdict"] != "approved" or any(x["severity"] in {"P0", "P1"} and x["disposition"] != "resolved" ...): raise RuntimeError("Independent reviewer blocked the candidate")`. read_review_completion (automatic.py:174-185) checks only schema and bindings. contracts/projects/v1.ts validateReviewResult: `if (review.verdict === 'approved' && review.findings.some(f => (f.severity === 'P0' || f.severity === 'P1') && f.disposition !== 'resolved')) throw new Error('An approved review cannot carry an unresolved P0/P1 finding')`. Contrast PR 9 automatic.py:190-192 raises ValueError before persisting; PR 11 automatic.py:282 `review["verdict"] = "blocked"`.
findings.verifier_reason: finish_review persists the reviewer's literal verdict and findings before checking the blocking rule, and read_review_completion checks only schema and bindings. The controller's export_state copies review.json verbatim into run-state.json, which validateReviewResult would reject. Worse than stated: PR 10's own `workflow export` refuses to re-export such a run at all via validate_review_record, so the record can never be served by any path. Medium is right: it needs a reviewer to make a contradictory file, which the prompt discourages.

findings.title: reviewCompletion schema is hand-written outside v1.ts: no TS type, fixture or drift test
findings.detail: The repo convention is that v1.ts holds the authoritative zod schemas, `*.schema.json` is generated, examples.ts has a fixture for every message and contract.test.ts checks drift. PR 11 adds a 39-line hand-written JSON Schema, does not add it to the schemas map, and has zero TypeScript references to it. Mitigations: the README bullet states it is hand-written and points to the existing separately-authored verification.schema.json precedent; the only consumer is Python, which tests it with 11 schema-negative subtests plus malformed JSON and symlink cases and a test that the prompt names every enum; and it is the strictest of the three schemas. Still, a future TS consumer (e.g. the viewer rendering completion files) has no type, and export.ts cannot protect it from drift.

findings.title: Controller rewrites an approved verdict to blocked in review.json
findings.detail: When the reviewer writes verdict approved with an unresolved P0/P1, _decide persists review.json with verdict 'blocked' instead of rejecting the file or recording the reviewer's literal verdict plus an override marker. The persisted record (and therefore the exported reviewResult) no longer matches review.completion.json, and nothing in the contract says the verdict was normalised. This keeps the record consistent with validateReviewResult, but it is lossy; PR 9's approach (reject the contradictory file before persisting) preserves both properties.

Contrast PR 9 automatic.py:190-192 `raise ValueError("Approval cannot leave an unresolved P0/P1 finding")`.
findings.verifier_reason: The rewrite exists, but the finding's 'lossy' claim is wrong: two lines later the controller stores the reviewer's literal decision in the receipt (`receipt["decision"] = decision`), and review.completion.json itself stays on disk, so the original verdict is retained in two places. The prompt also tells the reviewer in advance that any unresolved P0/P1 ends the run, so a reviewer who writes approved with an open P1 is told the outcome is blocked. The persisted record is consistent with validateReviewResult and with the run's actual outcome. Only a nit remains: the contract has no override marker.

dimensions.summary: I read workflow/export_state.py and the export_run/ExportRuntime/`workflow export` code in PR 10 and PR 11 against main, read both export test files, diffed server/projects.ts, and then proved the compatibility story on scratchpad copies of the live run: each PR's `python -m workflow export` was run on its own copy (both exit 0, worktrees untouched), and the resulting run-state.json files plus the untouched 1.0.0 original were served through the real adapter of main and of PR 11 via a 15-line tsx probe. PR 11 is the only PR whose export and adapter are coherent: the 1.0.0 run loads (review/inputs answer 404 REVIEW_NOT_FOUND / INPUTS_NOT_FOUND) and the re-exported 1.2.0 run serves the verdict, six findings, the diff artifact and both workers' inputs. PR 10 bumps the export to 1.2.0 while shipping main's `z.literal('1.0.0')` adapter unchanged, so every new run is `RUN_STORAGE_INVALID ... expected "1.0.0"` in the viewer, and the existing run breaks the first time anyone runs `workflow status` on it (status -> report() -> export_state rewrites the file at 1.2.0); its export also contradicts its own contract for the very run the PRD says to re-export. PR 9 does not touch export at all and is therefore fully compatible but contributes nothing on this dimension. Ranking on this dimension: PR 11, then PR 9 (safe by omission), then PR 10 (ships a viewer regression).
dimensions.pr9: No change to workflow/export_state.py, server/ or contracts/projects (`git diff 61e4752 99c770f --stat -- workflow/export_state.py server/ src/ contracts/projects/` is empty). Export stays 1.0.0 and the adapter stays `z.literal('1.0.0')`, so project-workflows-001 and any new run keep loading exactly as on main (probe: main adapter + 1.0.0 run -> 200 list, 200 detail). There is no `workflow export` action, no review/inputs section and no re-export path; a blocked native verdict is not visible in the viewer, but that is slice B's job under the umbrella PRD, which PR 9 follows. Merging as-is leaves the viewer working for new runs. Score reflects perfect compatibility with zero contribution.
dimensions.pr10: export_state.py (134 lines) adds `export_review`/`export_inputs`, `iso()` for epoch-ms and offset timestamps, a 256 KiB export-side truncation with marker, symlink-refusing `optional_json`, and `export_run` in pipeline.py with a SimpleNamespace runtime, controller lock and a new `validate_review_record`. The tests are good (real driven fixture downgraded to a 1.0.0 shape, CLI under a held lock, byte-identical idempotence, blocked verdict, truncation). But the compat outcome is bad: EXPORT_VERSION is "1.2.0" (export_state.py:16) with no server/ change, so a new run is rejected by the shipped adapter (probe: `500 RUN_STORAGE_INVALID ... run-state.json version: Invalid input: expected "1.0.0"`), and the existing run is only safe until the first `workflow status`, because report() (pipeline.py:479-481) re-exports at 1.2.0; the handoff (lines 76-77) discloses the new-run break but not the status path. The export of the live run also violates PR 10's own runInputs contract (no `reviewer_transport` in `automatic`, `mode: "interactive"` for an automatic run, `feature: null`), passes `{node}.handoff.json` through unvalidated, and duplicates the review validator. Merging as-is does NOT leave the viewer working for new runs.

findings.title: Transport is inferred from file existence, ignoring the receipt's own `transport` field
findings.detail: `recorded_transport` returns 'native' if review.interactive.json exists, else 'print' if automatic-review.json exists. But `_review_native` writes automatic-review.json with `transport: "native"` before `launch_reviewer` creates review.interactive.json; if the launch fails before the interactive receipt exists (the needs_reconciliation path), a plan without `reviewer_transport` exports `inputs.automatic.reviewer_transport: "print"` for a run that attempted a native review. Reading `receipt.get("transport")` first (as PR 10 does) would be both simpler and correct; the file-existence inference only exists to serve the one pre-slice-A receipt that lacks the field.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/export_state.py:62-68; automatic.py:295-297 `receipt = {"transport": "native", ...}; save_json(receipt_path, receipt)` then :299 `runtime.launch_reviewer(...)`, :321-325 `except BaseException ... status="needs_reconciliation"`; automatic.py:58-60 legacy plans default to native so this path is reachable. Live receipt keys (no transport): `session_id, bundle_sha256, candidate_commit, status, patch_sha256, pid, review`.

findings.title: `stop.confirmed_at` is file mtime, which the docstring's 'copied run still exports' promise does not preserve
findings.detail: The export presents the stop marker's mtime as a confirmation time. That is a reasonable proxy for the original directory, but a `cp -r` copy (no `-p`) re-stamps it, so the same run exports different evidence from a copy. PR 10 instead writes `stopped_at` into the marker for new runs and exports null for old ones, which is more honest. Both PRs also fall back to mtime for `reviewed_at` when no event/receipt time exists.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/export_state.py:121 `"confirmed_at": utc(path.stat().st_mtime) if item["stopped"] else None`; pipeline.py:416-419 docstring "a copied or finished run whose worktrees are gone still exports". PR 10 pipeline.py:155 `intent["stopped_at"] = now()`, export_state.py:100.

findings.title: `inputs_section` indexes policy keys the validator does not require, and ExportRuntime copies Pipeline.__init__
findings.detail: `policy["feature"]` and `policy["version"]` are read without a guard although `validate_policy` checks neither; a policy lacking them would raise KeyError from report() (a traceback, not the CLI's 'Blocked:' message). All shipped policies carry both, so this is latent. Separately, `ExportRuntime.__init__` restates the plan/automatic/policy-digest checks from `Pipeline.__init__` rather than sharing a helper, the same duplication PR 10's `export_run` has, just wrapped in a class; both PRs also restate prepare's 'never started' SimpleNamespace state.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/export_state.py:142 `"feature": policy["feature"], "policy_version": policy["version"]`; main verification.py:48-71 `validate_policy` (no feature/version check; `check["scenarios"]` is required at :66 so that index is safe). pipeline.py:112-123 vs :422-433; :451 vs :625 `SimpleNamespace(values={}, next=("launch_ui", "launch_adapter"), tasks=[])`. PR 10 pipeline.py:447-471.

findings.title: Truncation placement: PR 11 keeps the export lossless and bounds at the adapter; PR 10 cuts inside the private record
findings.detail: PR 10 truncates task text to 256 KiB bytes in run-state.json (`decode(errors="ignore")` plus marker, `task_truncated` flag) and leaves path redaction to a future adapter. PR 11 exports the full task and the recorded prompt, and the adapter redacts first and then bounds at 64 KiB characters with a surrogate-safe cut and a marker that counts what was dropped, so the verbatim requirement-quote lookup runs on the full text and no cut can expose a partial path. PR 11's placement is the better separation of evidence from presentation; PR 10's is acceptable but loses text from the exported record (plan.json still has it).
findings.evidence: PR 10 export_state.py:17-18, :81-83; contracts/projects/v1.ts `task_truncated: z.boolean()`. PR 11 export_state.py:127-128 (`task`, `prompt`), server/projects.ts `const TEXT_LIMIT = 65536`, `function boundedText(raw)` (redactPaths then cut, marker `[… truncated by the viewer API: N more characters]`), `lanesQuoting` requires the quote to survive in `boundedText(text).text`; server/projects.test.ts:1089-1114.

findings.title: The two 1.2.0 export shapes are mutually incompatible
findings.detail: Both PRs call their export 1.2.0 but the section shapes differ (PR 10: `review.reviewer`, `review.session`, `inputs.workers` as a list with `task_truncated`/`stopped`/`stopped_at`, `feature` nullable; PR 11: `review.reviewer_session_id`, `inputs.workers` keyed by lane with `prompt`/`stop{stopped,confirmed_at}`, `policy_version`, `failure_drill`). Relevant only if pieces of both branches are combined: PR 11's adapter rejects PR 10's export outright.
findings.evidence: Probe, PR 11 adapter serving PR 10's export: `500 RUN_STORAGE_INVALID ... review.reviewer_session_id: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined; review: Unrecognized keys: "reviewer", "session"; inputs.feature: Invalid input: expected string, received null`. Field lists from the two probe dumps: PR 10 review keys `[attempt, bundle_sha256, candidate_commit, diff, findings, independent, reviewed_at, reviewer, session, transport, verdict]`; PR 11 `[..., reviewer_session_id, transport, verdict]`.

findings.title: Compatibility preserved by leaving the export and adapter untouched, as the umbrella PRD prescribes for slice A
findings.detail: PR 9 changes nothing under workflow/export_state.py, server/ or contracts/projects, so both the existing run and any new run export and load at 1.0.0 exactly as on main. The cost is that nothing new is visible (no review section, no `workflow export`), but the umbrella PRD assigns that to slice B's run. There is no compat risk to report.
findings.evidence: `git diff 61e4752 99c770f --stat -- workflow/export_state.py server/ src/ contracts/projects/` -> empty. main export_state.py:38 `"version": "1.0.0"`; main server/projects.ts:52 `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)`. Probe: main adapter + on-disk 1.0.0 run -> `200 runs=[["project-workflows-001","paused"]]`, `200 detail`. docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md: ship A alone, B's feature run adds the review section and `workflow export`.

findings.title: One 1.2.0 export in a registered runs_root hides every run in that workflow's list, not only the new run
findings.detail: Main's adapter (shipped unchanged by PR 10) fails the whole run listing when any run directory in the runs_root is invalid. After PR 10 merges, the first run prepared into (or `status`-ed inside) a registered runs_root writes a 1.2.0 export, and from then on the run list for that workflow answers 500; the existing 1.0.0 run still loads by direct URL but disappears from the list. PR 10's handoff describes the effect as 'the current adapter rejects [it] for that run's listing', which understates it. Feature runs default to a per-feature root (not registered today), so on the registered project-workflows root this bites when a new project-workflows run is prepared there or when the operator runs `status` on the existing run (finding 2); it also means any newly registered feature root shows an empty, erroring list until B's adapter merges.
findings.evidence: Probe with main's adapter over a root containing the untouched 1.0.0 run plus a PR 10-exported copy renamed project-workflows-002: `500  :: {"error":{"code":"RUN_STORAGE_INVALID","message":"Run \"project-workflows-002\" has malformed or contradictory persisted state: run-state.json version: Invalid input: expected \"1.0.0\""}}` for the list route, while `200 /project-workflows-001 :: status=paused review_node={...}` by direct URL. Registered root: ~/.config/md-manager/projects.json -> `md-manager feature-implementation /home/agentops/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/project-workflows`. /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/launch.py:16 `DEFAULT_RUN_ROOT = Path.home() / ".local/state/md-manager-workflows"`, :79 `run_root = (args.run_root or DEFAULT_RUN_ROOT / args.feature)`. Handoff docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:77 'which the current adapter rejects for that run's listing'. (PR 11's adapter has the same fail-closed listing, but nothing in PR 11 produces an export it rejects.)

findings.title: The low finding 'unguarded policy["feature"]/["version"]' is wrong: the policy schema requires them and both runtimes validate before export
findings.detail: inputs_section indexes policy["feature"], policy["version"], check["scenarios"] and scenario["description"] directly, but every one of these is a required key in the verification policy JSON schema, and validate_pipeline_policy (which runs validate_schema) is executed by both Pipeline.__init__ and ExportRuntime.__init__ before export_state can run. A policy lacking them is refused with a ValueError, never a KeyError in the export.
findings.evidence: contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json: top-level required `['version', 'feature', 'workers', 'independent_review', 'integration_approval']`, check required `['id', 'kind', 'argv', 'timeout_seconds', 'scenarios']`, scenario required `['id', 'description']`, `additionalProperties: false`. /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/verification.py:48-49 `def validate_policy(policy): validate_schema("verification", policy)`; pipeline.py:35-39 `validate_pipeline_policy` calls it; :431 ExportRuntime `self.policy = validate_pipeline_policy(read_json(policy_path))`. Live policy keys include `feature` and `version` ('1.1.0'); every live check has a `scenarios` key.

findings.title: report() now reads review.json at every CLI boundary and indexes it without shape checks; a wrong-shaped file raises an uncaught KeyError
findings.detail: Main's export_state never opened review.json. Both PRs' export sections index review["findings"], review["reviewer"], finding["severity"] etc. directly. In the export CLI path both PRs validate first (validate_review_record / check_review), but in the report() path used by every other action there is no such check: PR 11's load_optional only swallows JSON syntax errors, PR 10's optional_json swallows nothing. A syntactically valid review.json missing a key (hand-edited, or a partially written file from a crashed reviewer path) turns every subsequent controller action into a Python traceback, because the CLI catches only ValueError/RuntimeError/OSError/SubprocessError. Exposure is limited to tampered or corrupted run directories, hence low.
findings.evidence: PR 10 /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/export_state.py:66-69 `findings = [{"severity": f["severity"], ...} for f in review["findings"]]` / `review["verdict"], review["reviewer"], review["independent"]`; pipeline.py:479-481 report() -> export_state; :689 `except (ValueError, RuntimeError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError)`. PR 11 /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/export_state.py:86-89 same direct indexing in review_section; :43-50 `load_optional` catches only ValueError; pipeline.py:506-508 report() -> export_state. main export_state.py never reads review.json (lines 23-46).

findings.title: ExportRuntime never checks that review.json/review-bundle.json belong to this run's plan.json
findings.detail: check_review compares review.run_id with bundle.run_id and the bundle hash with review.bundle_sha256, but nothing compares either against plan["run_id"]. A mutually consistent review.json + review-bundle.json pair copied from another run directory exports as this run's review with no refusal. PR 10's validate_review_record does compare review.run_id with plan.run_id. Cheap to fix by adding `bundle["run_id"] != runtime.plan["run_id"]` to ExportRuntime; the adapter has no way to detect it because the export carries only the section.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/pipeline.py:47-51 `check_review`: `review["run_id"] != bundle["run_id"] or review["bundle_sha256"] != digest or review["candidate_commit"] != bundle["candidate_commit"]` (no plan comparison); :434-440 ExportRuntime passes `read_json(review_path), read_json(bundle_path), digest_file(bundle_path)` only. Compare PR 10 /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/pipeline.py:428 `review["run_id"] != plan["run_id"]`.

findings.title: Handoff section 5 claim 'the run projects as succeeded' is accurate on a faithful copy
findings.detail: The prior reviewer's probes showed `paused` for every adapter/export combination, which could have read as a PR 11 handoff overstatement. The cause was the copy recipe: an unanchored `candidate` exclude also dropped `verification/candidate/*`, so the candidate verification nodes had no packets. With anchored excludes the candidate packets are present and PR 11's export + adapter project the run as `succeeded`, matching the handoff.
findings.evidence: Prior copies: `ls scratchpad/runs-legacy/project-workflows-001/verification` -> `worker` only; live run has `verification/candidate/{adapter,ui}/1`. Full copy via `rsync -a --exclude '/candidate/' --exclude '/review-worktree/' ...` then PR 11 export -> probe `200 :: runs=[["project-workflows-001","succeeded"]]`, `200 /project-workflows-001 :: status=succeeded ...`. Handoff /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:63 'served through the real adapter, the run projects as `succeeded`'.

dimensions.summary: I read main's server/projects.ts and projectRoutes.ts as the style baseline, PR 11's full server/ diff (projects.ts +305, projectRoutes.ts +29, projects.test.ts +446), its contracts/projects/v1.ts and export_state.py to check producer/adapter shape agreement, and the two adapter-task.md specs (PR 10 and PR 11) against PRD_REVIEW_RESULT.md / PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md. I probed the old and new redactPaths regexes on edge-case strings and zod's timestamp/error-message behaviour in the scratchpad, and inspected the live project-workflows-001 run's receipts to confirm the adapter's normalisations match real files. PR 11 is the only PR with adapter code and it is careful, security-minded work that matches the existing adapter's conventions: strict section schemas, a materially better redaction regex, a hash-and-size-checked review.diff artifact reusing the no-follow bounded reader, verbatim-only requirement lookup with a served-text guard, 404-not-500 for absent sections, and a test file whose negative-path matrix is stronger than main's. PR 10's adapter-task.md is a competent specification with a detailed verification list but leaves load-bearing choices open (artifact id, content type, 404 code), imposes a costly design for diff_artifact, and its contract carries enum/pattern gaps a faithful worker would inherit; its own export bump to 1.2.0 against an adapter still pinned to 1.0.0 leaves new runs unviewable until the feature run merges. PR 9 ships nothing on this dimension and correctly needed nothing.
dimensions.pr9: Not applicable: no server/ change and none required by slice A. The one thing worth crediting is restraint, and it is real: PR 9 leaves export_state at 1.0.0, so the adapter on main keeps validating every new run (z.literal('1.0.0') in server/projects.ts:37 on main) and the existing live run keeps loading. It neither describes nor implies adapter work. Scored 0 per instructions.
dimensions.pr10: Specification only (features/review-result/adapter-task.md, features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md), no adapter code. The B task is precise on ownership, version acceptance ("major 1 and minor >= 0", forward-compatible), the review node fields, redaction, old-run behaviour, and a strong verification list (1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 load, three transports, blocked review, attempt 2 and missing review are 404, diff confinement/symlink/hash/oversize, redaction). But it leaves choices open that the UI worker and browser seeds depend on: "artifact_id of your choice", "text/x-diff or text/plain", "404 with a code that says no review is recorded" (no code named). Its diff_artifact rule ("null when the file fails its checks, the reviews route still succeeds") forces the reviews route to open, bound-read and hash up to 32 MiB on every request and silently downgrades tampering to null. The C task's requirement_verbatim compares redacted quote to redacted task, which can false-link a literal "<path>" quote. The contract feeding the spec has gaps a faithful worker would inherit: checks[].kind omits typecheck/integration (policy schema allows six), check/scenario id use the route-ID pattern (rejects labels like test:unit), mode is z.enum(['interactive']), source_branch is required so runs without it get inputs:null. It says nothing about what happens when a review/inputs section is malformed. Meanwhile PR 10 bumps EXPORT_VERSION to "1.2.0" while main's adapter is z.literal('1.0.0'): every run recorded after merging PR 10 is RUN_STORAGE_INVALID in the viewer until B's feature run merges; disclosed at docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:76-77 but self-inflicted by shipping the producer bump before the consumer. Two workers given this spec would produce broadly equivalent but not interchangeable code.
dimensions.pr11: Shipped adapter code of high quality, consistent with main's style (ProjectApiError codes, readBounded/openDirectory/withRunsRoot reuse, JSDoc one-liners, routes registered via the paths map so the 405 loop and HEAD cover them). Export acceptance is an explicit enum of 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 (server/projects.ts:44) with review/inputs optional-or-null and strictly validated (:73-90, :123-142), and values.review is never mined. Redaction is materially improved (:57): my probe shows main leaves "[/home/u/x]", "|/home/u/x|", "<~/x/y>", "*~/a/b*" and "file:///home/..." unredacted while PR 11 redacts all of them, with no regression on URLs, relative paths or "2/3". review.diff is registered only under the literal path "review.diff" (:89), served via the existing artifact route with the same no-follow bounded read, an added size check (:651), text/plain + nosniff + CSP sandbox, and the test fixture deliberately embeds "<script>alert(1)</script>". requirement_found_in matches raw quote against raw task/prompt and additionally requires the redacted quote to survive in the served (64 KiB-bounded) text (:397-406); nothing is inferred. Absent sections are 404 REVIEW_NOT_FOUND/INPUTS_NOT_FOUND (:592-605), malformed ones are RUN_STORAGE_INVALID naming only the run. Tests (30, up from 22) assert no root path and no /home|/tmp|/var in every error body, snapshot the run tree to prove reads never write, cover 405/HEAD on the new routes and a 22-case malformed-section matrix. Weaknesses are modest: exact-version enum plus eager section validation means one 1.3.0 or one bad receipt field in one run makes the whole workflow list 500 (pre-existing pattern, larger surface now); checks[].command and setup[].command pass through unredacted by design; validateReviewResult runs three times per review request; native_started_at above 8.64e15 ms throws RangeError into the generic 500 path; the feature README still says "not an implementation" while the same PR ships it. Its own adapter-task.md matches the shipped code line for line and is precise enough to reproduce it.
dimensions.ranking_reason: PR 11 is the only PR with adapter code and the code is careful, well-tested and stylistically consistent with main; on the security points that matter here (redaction, artifact registry checks, bounded reads, path-free errors, never guessing a match) it is verifiably better than what main has today. PR 10's specification is competent and its verification list is good, but it leaves load-bearing details open, prescribes a heavier diff_artifact design, inherits contract gaps, and ships an export bump that breaks the viewer for new runs until the future adapter lands. PR 9 has nothing on this dimension, which is correct for slice A, so it ranks last by definition rather than by fault.
dimensions.verifier_note: Ranking unchanged after verification, but the gap between PR 11 and PR 10 is a little narrower than the reviewer painted: two of the three PR 10 findings were overstated (the open spec choices are not load-bearing for the UI worker, and the diff_artifact sentence is a spec nit), and the export-bump problem, while real, follows the PRD's own pre-run sequencing and is disclosed. PR 11 remains clearly ahead on this dimension because it is the only PR with adapter code and that code survives scrutiny: I re-derived the producer/adapter agreement field by field against export_state.py and the live run's plan/handoff/launch/completion/stop/policy files, probed the old and new redaction regexes on 36 strings (seven new redactions, zero regressions), confirmed the kind enum matches the policy schema exactly, and confirmed that every error body is asserted path-free and that reads are snapshot-checked as non-writing. Its one design weakness on this dimension (exact-version enum with eager projection) is a low nit inherited from a stricter main. PR 10's specification is competent and its verification list is good, and its contract mirrors plan.json more literally than the reviewer credited (mode 'interactive' is what the plan stores), but it delivers no adapter and ships a producer bump that the merged adapter rejects. PR 9 has nothing on this dimension and correctly needed nothing; 0 denotes not-applicable, not fault.

findings.title: Redaction regex genuinely closes Markdown-punctuation and file:// gaps
findings.detail: PR 11 replaces main's lookbehind allow-list with a negative lookbehind on path characters plus an explicit file:// branch. A scratch probe shows main leaves paths inside [], ||, <>, ** and file:/// unredacted while PR 11 redacts all of them, and neither regex touches https URLs, relative paths, './x', '../x' or '2/3'. The test at server/projects.test.ts:1197 pins every spelling.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:57 `text.replace(/(?:file:\/\/(?=\/)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9._@~+/-]))(?:~|\/[A-Za-z0-9._@~+-]+)(?:\/[A-Za-z0-9._@~+-]*)+/g, '<path>')`. Probe (node redact.mjs): input `see [/home/u/x](/home/u/x) and |/home/u/x| and <~/x/y> *~/a/b*` -> main: `see [/home/u/x](<path>) and |/home/u/x| and <~/x/y> *~/a/b*`; ultra: `see [<path>](<path>) and |<path>| and <<path>> *<path>*`. `file:///home/u/repo/x.ts` -> main unchanged, ultra `<path>`. `https://example.com/a/b`, `src/projects/api.ts`, `../up/x`, `2/3` unchanged in both.

findings.title: review.diff artifact registration is pinned, hash-and-size checked and served with safe headers
findings.detail: The export's diff registration only validates with path literally 'review.diff' (traversal is rejected at schema level, tests review-diff-path / review-diff-traversal), the artifact id is derived from the registered hash, the file is read through the existing no-follow bounded reader under artifactByteLimit, and the served bytes must match both registered sha256 and byte count. Content type is text/plain with nosniff and CSP sandbox; the fixture embeds a script tag to prove it is inert. Untrusted packets do not block the review diff and a tampered registration surfaces as ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH rather than a silently null link.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:89 `diff: z.strictObject({ path: z.literal(REVIEW_DIFF_FILE), sha256: hex64, bytes: ... })`; :617 `registered.push({ components: [REVIEW_DIFF_FILE], kind: 'patch', ... bytes: run.reviewDiff.bytes })`; :651 `if ((artifact.bytes !== null && bytes.length !== artifact.bytes) || sha256(bytes) !== artifact.sha256)`. Test server/projects.test.ts:979-1024 covers served/tampered/shorter/missing/symlinked-outside/oversize/none with `assert.equal(served.headers['content-type'], 'text/plain; charset=utf-8')`, nosniff, `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, and `assert.ok(!linked.body.includes('top secret'))`.

findings.title: requirement_found_in never guesses and is guarded against the served-text cut
findings.detail: A lane is linked only when the raw quote is a substring of the raw task (or prompt when the task is empty) AND the redacted quote survives in the bounded served text, so a link can never point at text the viewer cannot show. A quote written with the literal '<path>' marker does not match raw text; a paraphrase does not match; a null requirement yields []. The contract's cross-field validator additionally rejects links without a quote and duplicate lanes.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:397-406 `return text.includes(requirement) && boundedText(text).text.includes(served)`. Tests: server/projects.test.ts:932-960 asserts `requirement_found_in` = `[['ui'], [], [], ['ui'], [], ['adapter'], []]` for verbatim / paraphrase / none / path-in-quote / '<path>'-literal / both / legacy-null; :1197-1234 asserts a quote verbatim in the raw task but past the 64 KiB cut yields `[]`.

findings.title: Test file is stronger than main's on negative paths and leak checks
findings.detail: Every error assertion routes through assertError, which checks the body shape, that the temp root never appears, and that the message matches no /home|/tmp|/var path. The read-only test snapshots the run tree before and after hitting all routes including the new ones, checks 405+Allow for five methods and HEAD 200. The malformed-section test enumerates 22 mutations (unknown version, wrong types, extra keys carrying absolute paths, absolute/traversal owned_paths, foreign lane, duplicate check ids, browser without scenarios, unconfirmed stop with a time) and asserts the run list names only the run directory. Fixtures mirror real receipts (offset +00:00 timestamps, epoch-ms native_started_at) as found in the live run's ui.interactive.json.
findings.evidence: server/projects.test.ts:287-295 assertError; :396-418 read-only/405/HEAD over `url('alpha','main','run-002','/reviews/1')`, `/inputs` and `/artifacts/patch-review-<sha12>`; :1141-1195 malformed matrix with `assert.ok(!list.body.includes('/home/someone') && !list.body.includes('/etc/passwd'))`; :208-212 fixture `launch_requested_at: '2026-03-01T10:00:00.331982+00:00', native_started_at: Date.parse(...)` matching ~/.local/state/.../project-workflows-001/ui.interactive.json (`"launch_requested_at": "2026-09-21T14:33:25.331982+00:00", "native_started_at": 1790001207771`).

findings.title: Adapter code follows main's conventions and its adapter-task.md matches the shipped code
findings.detail: New routes are added to the paths map so the existing 405 loop and Fastify HEAD handling cover them; conform() is reused; errors are ProjectApiError with upper-snake codes; invalidRun() redacts issue text; helper functions carry the same one-line JSDoc style. PR 11's features/*/adapter-task.md names the exact version set, route, error codes, artifact id format, content type, headers, truncation limit and marker string, timestamp normalisation and launch_node_id rule, and each item corresponds to shipped code.
findings.evidence: server/projectRoutes.ts:110-111 paths.review/paths.inputs; :167-180 `conform(schemas.reviewResult, crossChecked(() => validateReviewResult(review), log), log)`. features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md:37 "truncated to 65536 characters with the marker `\n\n[… truncated by the viewer API: N more characters]`" matches server/projects.ts:378-385; features/review-result/adapter-task.md:14 "artifact id `patch-review-<first 12 hex of sha256>` ... `text/plain; charset=utf-8` inline" matches :366-368 and CONTENT_TYPES.patch.

findings.title: Exact-version enum plus eager section validation lets one run poison the whole workflow list
findings.detail: exportSchema.version is z.enum(['1.0.0','1.1.0','1.2.0']) and review/inputs are projected eagerly inside projectRun, which listRuns calls for every run. One run exported at 1.2.1/1.3.0, or one receipt field the strict section schema rejects (e.g. a policy check kind outside the enum, a non-UTC timestamp string, an unexpected key), makes GET .../runs a 500 for the entire workflow. This is main's pre-existing pattern for the core export, but the validated surface grew from about a dozen fields to roughly sixty optional-receipt fields. PR 10's spec asks for 'major 1 and minor >= 0', which is more forward-compatible. The test explicitly pins the whole-list failure.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:44 `const EXPORT_VERSIONS = ['1.0.0', '1.1.0', '1.2.0'] as const`; :693 `// Sections are projected eagerly so a contradictory review or assignment fails the run as a whole`; server/projects.test.ts:1163 case `{ ...base, runId: 'unknown-version', version: '1.3.0', ... }` and :1187-1188 `const list = await get(app, url('alpha', 'main')); assertError(list, 500, 'RUN_STORAGE_INVALID', root)`. Contrast features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):11 "Accept run-state.json exports whose version has major 1 and minor >= 0 (1.0.0, 1.1.0, 1.2.0, later 1.2.x)".
findings.verifier_reason: The mechanism is real (exact enum, eager projection, listRuns throws, test pins the whole-list 500) but the finding's concrete triggers are mostly impossible and the pattern is inherited from main, where the check was stricter (z.literal). Non-UTC timestamps are accepted by the section schemas; the check kind enum is identical to the policy schema's six kinds; unexpected keys cannot arrive from receipts because export_state.py builds every section from explicitly named keys. The residual risk is an in-repo version bump (1.2.1/1.3.0) that the producer and consumer would change together, with 30 tests to catch it. A design nit, not something that should block or be fixed before merge.

findings.title: Oversized native_started_at reaches the generic 500 path instead of RUN_STORAGE_INVALID

findings.title: Review payload is validated three times per request and redaction is recomputed per lane per finding

findings.title: Spec leaves load-bearing choices open that the UI worker and seeds depend on
findings.detail: The B task says the artifact_id is 'of your choice', the content type is 'text/x-diff or text/plain', and the missing-review 404 uses 'a code that says no review is recorded' without naming it. The UI worker runs in parallel against the same spec and must mock the reviews route, seed candidate-mode runs and branch on the 404 code, so two workers could ship non-interlocking choices (e.g. UI expects REVIEW_NOT_FOUND, adapter emits NO_REVIEW). Compare PR 11's adapter task, which fixes `patch-review-<sha12>`, `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND`, `INPUTS_NOT_FOUND` and the exact truncation marker.

findings.title: diff_artifact null-on-check-failure forces a full diff read on every reviews request and hides tampering
findings.detail: The spec requires diff_artifact to be null 'when the export has no diff or the file fails its checks (the reviews route still succeeds)'. To know whether the file fails its checks the reviews route must open, bound-read (up to 32 MiB) and hash review.diff on every call, and a hash mismatch or symlink is then reported as 'no diff' rather than as evidence tampering. The live run's review.diff is 289 KB, so the cost is real but bounded; the bigger issue is that a security signal (ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH) is downgraded to an absence. PR 11 instead links by registry and lets the artifact route fail loudly (test 'tampered' asserts the link is present and the artifact route returns ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH).
findings.evidence: features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):14 "`diff_artifact` is `null` when the export has no diff or the file fails its checks (the reviews route still succeeds)". Live run: `-rw-rw-r-- 1 agentops agentops 289187 Sep 21 15:36 review.diff`. PR 11 server/projects.test.ts:1019-1021 `const tampered = validateReviewResult(...); assert.equal(tampered.diff!.artifact_id, \`patch-review-${'e'.repeat(12)}\`)` with :1009 `assertError(await artifact('tampered', ...), 500, 'ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH', root)`.
findings.verifier_reason: The sentence exists as quoted, and nulling a hash mismatch does contradict the adapter's own header principle that contradictory evidence is never reported as success, so the critique is fair. But 'forces a full read on every request' is overstated: the spec never says which checks, so a worker can satisfy it with registry-level checks (path confinement, hash format) and leave content verification to the artifact route; and even a full read is bounded and cheap (the live review.diff is 289 KB). It is one sentence in a spec for a future worker who can escalate it, not shipped behaviour.
findings.verifier_evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/features/review-result/adapter-task.md:14 "`diff_artifact` is `null` when the export has no diff or the file fails its checks (the reviews route still succeeds)" (confirmed). Main's stated principle in server/projects.ts:10-16 "Missing or contradictory evidence is reported as an error or a paused/failed state, never as success." Live size: `ls -la ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/project-workflows/project-workflows-001/review.diff` → 289187 bytes. findings.title: Redaction regex change verified: seven new redactions, no regressions on a 36-string probe

dimensions.summary: I read PR 11's ten changed UI files (ReviewDetail, Assignment, WorkerInputs, RunView, NodeDetail, api, panels, status, App.css, index.css) and its six browser-test files against main's src/projects conventions and the PRD B/C acceptance tables, then read PR 10's review-result and run-inputs ui-task.md/policy.json/README as a specification and cross-checked every field name they cite against PR 10's own contracts and main's WorkerResult schema. PR 11 ships well-structured, accessible, defensively scoped UI with strong, non-conditional browser assertions that cover every PRD B/C scenario id exactly once in both verification phases; its weaknesses are duplication (a half-finished helper extraction, a third copy of the tab keyboard handler that focuses via a data-testid), doubled loading/error panels for one resource, and a few low-level nits. PR 10's spec is clear, consistent with its own contract and policy scenario lists, and gives good legacy-state and reuse guidance, but one deliverable is unimplementable as written (link required checks to executed checks "with the same id" when executed checks carry no id) and two bullets are ambiguous. PR 9 has no UI or browser-test content and scores 0 on this dimension by construction.
dimensions.pr9: Not applicable. PR 9 (slice A only) changes no file under src/ or tests/project-workflows/ and ships no ui-task.md; there is nothing to review on this dimension. Score 0 as instructed, which is a statement of scope, not of quality.
dimensions.pr10: Specification only (features/review-result/ui-task.md, features/run-inputs/ui-task.md, policy.json, README.md). Strengths: every contract name the briefs cite (reviewer_session, diff_artifact, requirement_verbatim, runInputsResponse, task_truncated, stopped/stopped_at) exists in PR 10's contracts/projects/v1.ts; policy.json pins 10 and 14 browser scenario ids whose descriptions match the PRD tables verbatim and the "exactly one test title with one screenshot:<id>" rule matches the existing suite's convention; legacy states are specified as explicit non-error, non-spinner states; reuse pointers (existing text-artifact viewer, react-markdown already present) and ownership/no-new-deps/never-skip rules are explicit. Defects: run-inputs/ui-task.md:14 tells the worker to link each required check "to the executed check with the same id in the node's worker result", but main's executed-check schema (contracts/workflow/v1.ts checkSchema) has command/cwd/started_at/finished_at/exit_code/log_artifact_id and no id, so the instruction cannot be followed literally; the same file's bullet 17 says "never guess a match client-side" while also requiring the client to pick "the first task that contains it" for worker=both; bullet 15 asks the UI to render the launch token, which for workers on main is just the session id again (workflow/automatic.py:52,73). The brief is well-formed but was not dry-run against the shapes it depends on.
dimensions.pr11: Shipped UI and browser tests. Structure: three new components of 98-218 lines with clear sub-components (ReviewPanel/ReviewResultView/FindingRow; TaskPanel/LaunchReceipt/WorkerSignals/StopLine), NodeDetail grows 263→320 by delegation, and everything reuses main's useResource/AppLink/ErrorPanel/StatusBadge idioms and data-testid style. Safety: scopedReviewPath regex, run_id cross-check in fetchReviewResult, and the diff link is only rendered when review.diff.uri strictly equals the run's own artifact route (otherwise an alert, no link). Legacy states: NOT_RECORDED codes distinguish REVIEW_NOT_FOUND/INPUTS_NOT_FOUND from other 404s; review-none, inputs-none, worker-inputs-none and worker-inputs-unmatched are all explicit sentences. Accessibility: proper tablist with roving tabindex and Arrow/Home/End, aria-pressed toggles inside labelled role=group, th scope=col, <q> for quotes, visually-hidden "(blocks integration)" plus a left border so blocking is not colour-only, <mark> with light/dark tokens (~12:1 and ~5.9:1 contrast), focusable check anchors (li tabIndex=-1 id=check-N). Tests: 9 new scenarios, each PRD B/C id in exactly one title with one attach, no phase conditionals, strong assertions (exact summary strings, per-group counts, class/attr/href, diff bytes fetched from inside the page, keyboard ArrowLeft/Enter, in-viewport poll on the mark, highlight cleared on leaving the node, absent receipts stated), and a raw-vs-projected fixture design with a `leak` parameter so candidate phase exercises real adapter redaction. Deductions: projects.spec.ts still carries private copies of everything support.ts extracted; RunView.onTabKey is a third verbatim copy of DocumentView/Editor's handler and focuses via querySelector on a data-testid instead of refs; header and NodeDetail render duplicate LoadingPanel/ErrorPanel (two role=alert, two Retry) for the same inputs resource; no focus move after the finding→task jump; a speculative /reviews/N fetch that can only 404 against PR 11's own adapter; hard-coded /tmp|/home in the redaction assertion; minor CSS ordering and non-null-assertion nits.
dimensions.ranking_reason: PR 11 is the only PR with shippable UI and tests on this dimension, and what it ships is solid: consistent with main's component idioms, defensively scoped, accessible, with legacy states handled honestly and browser tests whose assertions are exact, unconditional and cover every PRD B/C scenario id in both phases. Its defects are quality/duplication issues, not correctness bugs. PR 10's specification is competent and internally consistent with its own contract, but one deliverable is literally unimplementable (check-id matching against id-less executed checks) and it delivers no working UI. PR 9 has nothing on this dimension.
dimensions.verifier_note: PR 11 is the only PR with UI and browser tests to judge, and what it ships holds up under re-reading: 15 scenario ids each appear in exactly one test title with exactly one screenshot attachment (grep count), the two new specs contain no phase conditionals or skips (grep returned nothing), assertions are exact (summary strings, per-group counts, class/attr/href, diff bytes fetched from inside the page, ArrowLeft focus, in-viewport poll on the mark, highlight cleared on leaving), the candidate seed includes a genuine 1.0.0 export (seed.ts:257-274) so the on-disk live-run shape is proven to load in both phases, and fixtures thread a `leak` argument that the candidate seed fills with a real absolute path (seed.ts:140-142) so adapter redaction is exercised for real. The mark tokens compute to 12.4:1 (light) and 5.8:1 (dark). The three confirmed quality/design defects are real and one is broader than reported (inputs Loading/Error is rendered in three places, so both the worker node and the Assignment tab show two role=alert panels), plus four rendered states have no test coverage; none is a correctness bug. That keeps it at 8, not higher. PR 10 delivers a specification only; it is internally consistent (policy descriptions were updated when paths-redacted widened to inputs, every cited contract name exists) but one deliverable is unimplementable as written (required-check id vs id-less executed checks) and it ships nothing runnable on this dimension, so 6. PR 9 changes nothing under src/, tests/project-workflows/ or features/*/ui-task.md; its 1 is the floor of the scale and a statement of scope, not quality.

findings.title: Every PRD B/C scenario id is covered by exact, unconditional assertions in both phases
findings.detail: review.spec.ts and inputs.spec.ts contain one test per id (review-verdict, review-blocked, review-legacy, paths-redacted, run-assignment, worker-inputs, finding-to-task, inputs-legacy, plus inputs-paths-redacted), each with exactly one attach(). Assertions are strong: exact summary strings, per-group row counts, class/attribute/href checks, the diff artifact fetched from inside the page and byte-compared, keyboard operation (ArrowLeft, Enter), an in-viewport poll on the <mark>, highlight cleared after leaving the node, and absent receipts asserted as explicit sentences. No `if (phase ...)` branches exist in the new specs.
findings.evidence: grep of `scenario:` across specs: each of the 15 ids appears exactly once; attach() calls: 15, one per test. review.spec.ts:50 `toHaveText('approved with 6 findings: 4 open, 2 accepted, none blocking')`; :84-87 `fetchFromPage` then `expect(served.text).toBe(REVIEW_DIFF)`; inputs.spec.ts:113 `expect(await page.getByTestId('task-source').textContent()).toBe(uiTask())`; :206-209 `expect.poll(() => highlight.evaluate(... box.top >= 0 && box.bottom <= innerHeight)).toBe(true)`; :212-218 highlight cleared on return; grep `if (|phase ===` in review.spec.ts/inputs.spec.ts returns nothing.

findings.title: Fixture design shares one logical dataset across mock and seed phases and forces real redaction in candidate mode
findings.detail: fixtures.ts defines raw export sections (the shape export_state.py writes) and their projections onto the contract (what mocks serve). Every free text takes a `leak` argument: seeds pass a real absolute path under the temp root so the real adapter must redact it, mocks pass the literal `<path>`, so both phases render identical text. RUN_LEGACY is written as a 1.0.0 export that still carries `values.review`, proving the adapter never mines it. The mock's launch nodes were also corrected to link to worker results, matching the real adapter (server/projects.ts WORKER_OF includes launch_ui/launch_adapter).
findings.evidence: fixtures.ts header comment lines 7-11; `uiPathQuote = (leak = PATH_TOKEN) => ...`, `reviewFindings(runId, leak)`, `rawInputsSection(runId, leak)`; seed.ts `leakFor(runsRoot, runId)` returns `join(runsRoot, runId, 'worktree-ui', 'test-results')`; seed.ts RUN_LEGACY block: `version: '1.0.0'` with `review: {...}` inside values; fixtures.ts `const launched = { launch_ui: done(UI_SESSION, 'ui'), ... }` with comment 'like the real adapter, link to the worker's verified result'; main server/projects.ts:124 `WORKER_OF = { launch_ui: 'ui', launch_adapter: 'adapter', ... }`.

findings.title: Review/inputs links are scope-checked and legacy 404s are distinguished from real errors
findings.detail: api.ts refuses any review result_uri outside `${paths.run(scope)}/reviews/<positive int>`, cross-checks run_id on both new payloads, and treats only the contract's REVIEW_NOT_FOUND / INPUTS_NOT_FOUND codes as 'not recorded'; any other failure still reaches ErrorPanel. ReviewResultView only renders the diff link when `review.diff.uri` strictly equals the run's own artifact route and otherwise shows a role=alert and no link. This matches main's scopedResultPath/result-unscoped pattern.
findings.evidence: api.ts:196-201 `scopedReviewPath` with `/^[1-9][0-9]*$/`; :203-209 `if (review.run_id !== scope.runId) throw`; :221-233 `isNotRecorded`/`orNotRecorded`; ReviewDetail.tsx:105-106 `diffHref = paths.artifact(scope, review.diff.artifact_id)`, `diffScoped = review.diff.uri === diffHref`; :145 role="alert" 'is outside this run's artifact route and was not linked'; NOT_RECORDED codes emitted by server/projects.ts:595,603.
