findings.title: Third copy of the tab keyboard handler, and it focuses through a data-testid selector
findings.detail: RunView.onTabKey is a line-for-line copy of DocumentView.onTabKeyDown and Editor.onTabKeyDown (Arrow/Home/End cycling). The two existing copies focus the next tab via `tabRefs.current[next]`; the new one queries the DOM for `[data-testid="tab-..."]`, coupling production focus management to a test hook and diverging from the codebase's own pattern. A shared useTabList hook or at least the refs approach would remove both problems.
findings.evidence: RunView.tsx `event.currentTarget.parentElement?.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(`[data-testid="${TABS[next].testId}"]`)?.focus()`; main src/document/DocumentView.tsx:95-106 and src/document/Editor.tsx:124-135 have the identical if/else chain ending in `tabRefs.current[next]?.focus()`.
findings.verifier_reason: RunView.tsx:66-77 onTabKey is the same if/else chain as DocumentView.tsx:95-106 and Editor.tsx:124-135 (ArrowRight/Down, ArrowLeft/Up, Home, End, preventDefault, setTab). The only divergence is the focus line: the two existing copies use `tabRefs.current[next]?.focus()` (DocumentView:105, Editor:134) with refs assigned at DocumentView:167 / Editor:170, while RunView:76 does `event.currentTarget.parentElement?.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(`[data-testid="${TABS[next].testId}"]`)?.focus()`. Functionally it works (inputs.spec.ts:85-88 asserts ArrowLeft focuses the Run tab), so this is a quality issue, not a bug. Note the two-copy duplication predates PR 11; the new part is the third copy and the testid coupling. Medium is defensible: a reviewer would ask for refs (or a shared hook) before merge.
findings.verifier_evidence: ultra src/projects/RunView.tsx:66-77; main src/document/DocumentView.tsx:95-106 (`tabRefs.current[next]?.focus()` at :105) and src/document/Editor.tsx:124-135 (:134); `grep -rn 'role="tablist"\|onTabKey\|tabRefs' src/` on main shows tabRefs only in the two document components.

findings.title: Duplicate loading and error panels for the one inputs resource
findings.detail: The run header (RunView) and the worker NodeDetail both render 'Loading the run inputs…' and, on failure, an ErrorPanel (role="alert", Retry button) for the same `inputs` resource. On a worker node with inputs failing the page shows two identical alerts and two Retry buttons; screen readers announce the failure twice. The header should own the panel and NodeDetail should only state the consequence ('task cannot be shown').
findings.evidence: RunView.tsx:102 `{(inputs.status === 'loading' || inputs.status === 'idle') && <LoadingPanel>Loading the run inputs…</LoadingPanel>}` and :103 `<ErrorPanel error={inputs.error} what="The run inputs" onRetry={reloadInputs} />`; NodeDetail.tsx:241 `{isWorker && (inputs.status === 'loading' || inputs.status === 'idle') && <LoadingPanel>Loading the run inputs…</LoadingPanel>}` and :242 `<ErrorPanel error={inputs.error} what="The run inputs" onRetry={onRetryInputs} />`; panels.tsx ErrorPanel renders `role="alert"`.
findings.verifier_reason: True and slightly broader than stated. The run header block (RunView.tsx:81-120) is rendered outside the tab switch (tabs start at :122, panel choice at :142), and it renders `LoadingPanel`/`ErrorPanel` for `inputs` at :102-103. NodeDetail.tsx:241-242 renders the same two panels for the same `inputs` prop on worker nodes, and Assignment.tsx:22-23 renders them a third time on the Assignment tab. ErrorPanel (panels.tsx:22) is `role="alert"` with a Retry button (:28). So a failed inputs fetch produces two alerts and two Retry buttons on a worker node, and also two on the Assignment tab.
findings.verifier_evidence: RunView.tsx:102 `{(inputs.status === 'loading' || inputs.status === 'idle') && <LoadingPanel>Loading the run inputs…</LoadingPanel>}`, :103 `<ErrorPanel error={inputs.error} what="The run inputs" onRetry={reloadInputs} />`; NodeDetail.tsx:241-242 `{isWorker && ... <LoadingPanel>Loading the run inputs…</LoadingPanel>}` / `<ErrorPanel error={inputs.error} what="The run inputs" onRetry={onRetryInputs} />`; Assignment.tsx:22-23 same pair; panels.tsx:22 `<div className="projects-error" role="alert" ...>`, :28 `<button ...>Retry</button>`.

findings.title: Finding-to-task jump scrolls the mark into view but never moves focus
findings.detail: After clicking a finding link the review node unmounts (focus falls to body), the task panel mounts on Source and scrolls the <mark> into view, but nothing receives focus. The <pre> is already focusable (tabIndex=0), so focusing it (or the mark with tabIndex=-1) in the same effect would let keyboard and screen-reader users land at the highlight. The test asserts only geometric visibility.
findings.evidence: WorkerInputs.tsx:36-40 `useEffect(() => { if (activeQuote === null) return; markRef.current?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' }); onHighlightApplied() }, ...)` with no focus call; :65 `<pre className="task-source" data-testid="task-source" tabIndex={0}>`; inputs.spec.ts:206-209 checks bounding box only, no `toBeFocused()`.

findings.title: ReviewPanel issues a speculative /reviews/N request that can only 404 against PR 11's own adapter
findings.detail: When a review node has result_uri null and status other than pending, ReviewPanel still fetches `paths.review(scope, max(attempt,1))` and relies on the REVIEW_NOT_FOUND 404 to render 'not recorded'. PR 11's adapter sets result_uri whenever the export carries a review, so the fetch never finds anything; every visit to an awaiting or legacy review node costs a request and a 404 in the server log. PR 10's spec handles the same case without a request ('no result_uri → No review recorded').
findings.evidence: ReviewDetail.tsx:193-195 `const reviewPath = node.result_uri !== null ? scopedReviewPath(...) : node.status === 'pending' ? null : paths.review(scope, Math.max(node.attempt, 1))`; server/projects.ts:876 `result_uri = reviewRoute(scope, state.run_id, state.review.attempt)`; PR 10 features/review-result/ui-task.md:18.

findings.title: Redaction assertion hard-codes /tmp and /home; worker-phase redaction tests are near-vacuous by design
findings.detail: renderedText() rejects `/\/tmp\/|\/home\//`, but the suite root is `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), ROOT_PREFIX))`, which is /var/folders/... on macOS, where the negative check becomes inert and only the positive `<path>` check remains. In worker phase the mocks carry the literal `<path>`, so both paths-redacted scenarios cannot fail there; only candidate phase exercises real redaction. Deriving the forbidden prefix from MD_MANAGER_PROJECTS_TEST_ROOT would make the negative check portable.
findings.evidence: support.ts:57 `expect(text, ...).not.toMatch(/\/tmp\/|\/home\//)`; playwright.config.ts:41 `const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), ROOT_PREFIX))`; fixtures.ts header: 'the mocks use the already-redacted marker `<path>`'; review.spec.ts:159 `expect(text).toContain(PATH_TOKEN)`.

findings.title: CSS ordering, non-null assertions and line length nits
findings.detail: Three review-findings rules are appended after the `@media (max-width: 760px)` block, outside the 'Run views' section they belong to. `.findings-table { min-width: 560px }` forces horizontal scrolling at phone width (mitigated by `.table-wrap { overflow: auto }`). Three `!` non-null assertions paper over lost narrowing (`finding.requirement!`, `activeQuote!`, `stop.confirmed_at!`). ReviewDetail.tsx has four lines over 200 characters where main's NodeDetail has none.
findings.evidence: App.css tail: `.review-findings-head {...}` `.review-group-toggle {...}` after the media query; App.css `.findings-table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; min-width: 560px; ... }`; ReviewDetail.tsx:79 `const quote = finding.requirement!`; WorkerInputs.tsx:70 `text.slice(index + activeQuote!.length)`; :192 `formatTime(stop.confirmed_at!)`; `awk 'length > 200'` counts: ReviewDetail 4, WorkerInputs 1, Assignment 1, main NodeDetail 0.

findings.title: Pending highlight is only cleared once TaskPanel mounts
findings.detail: RunView keeps `pendingHighlight` until TaskPanel's effect calls onHighlightApplied. If the target node's TaskPanel never mounts (inputs error, or the inputs list no worker for that launch node), the pending quote survives navigation to other nodes and would apply on a later visit to that node once inputs load. Clearing it in RunView when selectedNodeId changes away from pendingHighlight.nodeId would close the gap.
findings.evidence: RunView.tsx `const highlight = pendingHighlight !== null && pendingHighlight.nodeId === selectedNodeId ? pendingHighlight.quote : null` (derivation only, no reset); NodeDetail.tsx:248-253 TaskPanel rendered only when `worker !== null`; WorkerInputs.tsx:36-40 the only call site of onHighlightApplied.

findings.title: ui-task tells the UI worker to link required checks to executed checks 'with the same id', but executed checks have no id
findings.detail: run-inputs/ui-task.md deliverable 4 says each check id links to the executed check with the same id in the node's worker result. The executed-check schema in contracts/workflow/v1.ts (unchanged by PR 10) has command, cwd, started_at, finished_at, exit_code and log_artifact_id only. The instruction cannot be followed as written; the worker would have to infer a match on `command` (which PR 10's runInputs check schema does carry) or escalate. PR 11 resolved the same problem explicitly in its contract by documenting `command` as the join key.
findings.evidence: PR 10 features/run-inputs/ui-task.md:14 'each check id links to the executed check with the same id in the node's worker result when one exists'; PR 10 contracts/workflow/v1.ts:18-25 `checkSchema = z.strictObject({ command, cwd, started_at, finished_at, exit_code, log_artifact_id })`; PR 11 contracts/projects/v1.ts checks.command comment 'The approved argv joined exactly as the verifier records executed commands, so check IDs can be matched to executed checks'.
findings.verifier_reason: PR 10's required-check schema carries `id`, `kind`, `command`, `timeout_seconds`, `scenarios` (contracts/projects/v1.ts:92-98). Executed checks in the worker result use `checkSchema` from contracts/workflow/v1.ts, which PR 10 leaves byte-identical to main: `command, cwd, started_at, finished_at, exit_code, log_artifact_id`, no `id`. Nothing in PR 10's run-inputs README names a join key (grep for check/verbatim/link only finds the scenario row and the JSON example). The instruction at ui-task.md:14 therefore cannot be followed literally; a worker must either infer `command` as the key or stop under the 'stop and report' rule. PR 11 resolved the same question explicitly (contract comment v1.ts:106; its ui-task.md:15 says 'a check whose command equals an executed check's command').
findings.verifier_evidence: PR 10 features/run-inputs/ui-task.md:14 'each check id links to the executed check with the same id in the node's worker result when one exists'; PR 10 contracts/projects/v1.ts:92-98 `checks: z.array(z.strictObject({ id: id, kind: ..., command: z.string().min(1), timeout_seconds, scenarios }))`; `diff <(awk checkSchema main) <(awk checkSchema high)` -> identical: `command, cwd, started_at, finished_at, exit_code, log_artifact_id`; PR 11 contracts/projects/v1.ts:106 '/** The approved argv joined exactly as the verifier records executed commands, so check IDs can be matched to executed checks. */'.

findings.title: Ambiguous 'both' handling: client must search task text while told never to guess client-side
findings.detail: The finding-to-task bullet says that when requirement_verbatim is true the quote links to the worker's task, 'both links to the first task that contains it', and 'never guess a match client-side'. For worker=both the flag alone does not say which task contains the quote, so the client must run its own substring search over both task texts, which is the client-side matching the same sentence forbids. Stating that a verbatim substring check is allowed (only fuzzy matching is not) would remove the tension.
findings.evidence: PR 10 features/run-inputs/ui-task.md:17; README run-inputs 'Public API additions' row: `true` when the quote is found verbatim in the named worker's task text (both tasks for `both`).

findings.title: Launch token asked to be displayed is redundant with the session id for workers
findings.detail: run-inputs/ui-task.md lists 'launch token' among the receipt fields to render. On main the worker's launch_token in receipts and completion files is the plan's session id, so the panel would show the same UUID twice. PR 11 omits launch_token from the served contract for that reason.
findings.evidence: PR 10 features/run-inputs/ui-task.md:15 'launch receipt (session UUID, launch token, requested and native start times, ...)'; main workflow/automatic.py:52 `"launch_token": plan["nodes"][node]["session_id"]` and :73 comparison against the same; PR 11 contracts/projects/v1.ts runInputWorkerSchema.launch has no launch_token.

findings.title: Candidate seed carries a real 1.0.0 export, so the live run's shape is proven to load in the browser
findings.detail: RUN_LEGACY is seeded as `version: '1.0.0'` with `values.review` present but no review/inputs section, which is exactly the shape of the existing project-workflows-001 run on disk (1.0.0 export plus a print-mode review.json). review-legacy and inputs-legacy then assert `projects-error` count 0, `result-unscoped` count 0 and the explicit not-recorded sentences on the run header, the Assignment tab and a worker node, in both phases. Combined with the `leak` parameter (fixtures default to `<path>`, the candidate seed substitutes a real path under the temp root), the redaction and legacy scenarios test the real adapter rather than the mock's own output.

The Assignment tab has a dedicated `assignment-reviewer-transport` testid, yet run-assignment only asserts `toContainText('native')` on the whole panel, which would also pass on any other occurrence of that substring.

findings.title: UI hard-codes the `launch_<lane>` graph naming convention as a fallback for finding links
findings.detail: When run inputs are not loaded, `launchNodeFor` guesses the launch node for a lane by probing the pinned definition for a node literally named `launch_<lane>`, else falls back to the lane id. It is commented and only a fallback, but it encodes a graph-authoring convention in the viewer that the contract does not promise.

findings.title: Run/Assignment tab state is not reflected in the URL
findings.detail: The selected tab lives in component state initialised to 'run', so a reload while on the Assignment tab returns to the Run tab, and while on the Assignment tab the address still reads `/nodes/<id>` although the node detail is hidden. Minor for a read-only viewer, but every other view state in this app is addressable.

dimensions.summary: I read main's four slice-A test modules and the full test diffs of PR 9 (opus), PR 10 (high) and PR 11 (ultra), mapped each PR's new tests to PRD_REVIEWER_PANE work item 5 and the four section-5 acceptance bullets, and verified suspected weaknesses against the controller code (no suites were run; only an import-only loader count with bytecode writing disabled). PR 11 is clearly the strongest suite: it runs all five pre-existing graph tests under both transports via a mixin, asserts the exact exit sequence [75,130,75,0] in a fresh-process reviewer interruption, has separate fail-closed tests for wrong hash/token/candidate plus identity/worktree/evidence re-checks, and pins both live-discovered launch defects (argument order, Edit allow rule) with regression tests; its costs are a seven-knob fake, several mega-tests and coupling to feature data files. PR 10 correctly encodes the live-observed 'blocked means waiting for a human' behaviour and has good WaitReviewTests, but pinned the pre-existing graph tests to print, loosened the multi-process assertion to (4,1,0), uses a vacuous assertRaises(Exception) for the six foreign-binding cases, and never exercises the real stop path for the review node. PR 9 has the cleanest fake and the most readable tests, but one of them pins the opposite of acceptance bullet 2 (a blocked reviewer raises rather than waits), its launch test asserts only negatives on --tools so it could not have caught the live-denied Write, and the code's independence/worktree/evidence guards have no tests at all.

dimensions.ranking_reason: PR 11 covers every work-item-5 bullet and every section-5 acceptance bullet with behaviour-level assertions, keeps the pre-existing graph tests running under both transports, asserts exact exit sequences, and encodes both live-found launch defects as regression tests; its readability and fake-complexity costs are real but do not weaken any oracle. PR 10 and PR 9 are close. PR 10 encodes the correct acceptance behaviour for a questioning reviewer and exact launch flags, but pinned the pre-existing tests to print, loosened the multi-process order, has a vacuous assertRaises(Exception) on the PRD's core fail-closed cases and never drives the real stop path for the review node. PR 9 has the cleanest fake and strongest exit-code/regex assertions, but one test pins the opposite of acceptance bullet 2 (a blocked reviewer raises instead of waiting), its launch test asserts only negatives on --tools so it could not have caught the live-denied Write, and the controller's independence, worktree-change and evidence-change guards have no tests. A wrong oracle plus three untested guards outweighs PR 10's weak-but-not-wrong assertions.
dimensions.verifier_note: Verification confirmed seven of nine findings and downgraded two (PR 10's stop-path gap is covered by the generic stop_session through the unchanged stop_workers tests; PR 11's fake knobs are a nit). Nothing changed the order. PR 11 is clearly the strongest suite on this dimension: every work-item-5 bullet and every section-5 acceptance bullet has a behaviour-level oracle, the five pre-existing graph tests run under both transports via SharedGraphTests, exit sequences are exact, the three post-acceptance guards and the blocked-as-waiting state are tested, and both live-found launch defects are pinned with exact flag and ordering assertions (test_interactive.py:238-249). Its costs (mega-tests, 16-24 lines over 140 chars per file, GraphFixture collected empty, fake-launches.log in the run directory) do not weaken any oracle. PR 10 and PR 9 remain close. PR 10 has the correct blocked-state oracle, the exact Edit(//...) assertion and a good WaitReviewTests class, but pinned the pre-existing graph tests to print (default-transport coverage regressed), loosened the four-process sequence to (4,1,0), used assertRaises(Exception) for the PRD's core fail-closed cases, and its graph-level deadline test expires on the first poll. PR 9 has the cleanest fake and most readable tests with exact [75,130,75,0] and regex oracles, but it pins a blocked reviewer as fatal (contrary to acceptance bullet 2, and PR 9 ran no live smoke test to discover otherwise), asserts only negatives on the tool list, and leaves the independence, worktree-change and evidence-change guards untested. A wrong oracle on an acceptance bullet plus three untested guards outweighs PR 10's weakened-but-not-wrong oracles.

findings.title: Test pins a blocked reviewer as a fatal error, contrary to PRD acceptance bullet 2
findings.detail: PRD_REVIEWER_PANE section 5 requires that 'a reviewer that stops to ask a question can be answered in the pane, and the run resumes when the completion file appears'. PR 10 and PR 11 both observed live that such a session reports state `blocked`. PR 9's wait_review raises on that state and the test enshrines it, so a reviewer question would end the run; a reader of the test would take blocked==failure as the spec.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:207-208: `if row["state"] == "blocked": raise RuntimeError("Reviewer blocked; inspect quota or native error...")`. /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/test_automatic.py test_a_missing_or_blocked_reviewer_stops_rather_than_relaunching: `self.runtime.sessions.locate = lambda node, rows: {"state": "blocked"}` then `assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "Reviewer blocked")`. Contrast PR 10 test comment: '# Observed live: a reviewer that ends its turn asking a person shows as `blocked`.' and PR 11 automatic.py:219-223 which emits 'Reviewer needs attention in its pane' and keeps waiting.
findings.verifier_reason: PR 9's wait_review raises on native state `blocked` and the unit test enshrines it. Two independent live runs (PR 10 attempt 1, PR 11 attempt 1) observed a reviewer that needs a human reporting `blocked`, and main's interactive.py already lists `blocked` as a normal native state. PRD bullet 2 requires the run to resume after a question is answered in the pane; with PR 9's oracle the run dies at the first `blocked` poll. PR 9 declares the live smoke test was not run, and its PRD edit does not change bullet 2 (it only adds a section 7 note), so the test pins an oracle the spec forbids.

findings.title: Launch test asserts only negatives on --tools and no allow rule, so it could not detect the live-denied Write
findings.detail: The reviewer's only write (the completion file) is the protocol's linchpin. PR 9's launch test checks that Edit and Bash are absent and the permission mode is dontAsk, but never asserts the positive tool list or any allow rule. PR 10 and PR 11 both found live that Write is denied under dontAsk without `--allowedTools Edit(//<path>)` and assert the exact flag.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/test_interactive.py test_reviewer_launches_read_only_in_the_candidate_worktree: `self.assertNotIn("Edit", command[command.index("--tools") + 1])`, `self.assertNotIn("Bash", ...)`, `assertEqual(command[command.index("--permission-mode") + 1], "dontAsk")`; no assertion on --allowedTools. PR 10: `assertEqual(command[command.index("--allowedTools") + 1], f"Edit(//{completion.resolve().as_posix().lstrip('/')})")`. PR 11 additionally asserts option order: `assertEqual(command[-3:-1], ["--permission-mode", "dontAsk"])`.
findings.verifier_reason: The test never asserts the positive tool list or any --allowedTools; it would pass if `reviewer_tools` were 'Read,Glob,Grep' (no Write at all) and it pins nothing about how the one permitted write is authorised. Caveat on the title: no offline test can detect a live permission denial; the real defect is that the test does not document the write path, which is the protocol's linchpin. PR 10 and PR 11 assert the exact `Edit(//...)` rule and PR 11 the option order.
findings.verifier_evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:184-185 `reviewer_tools = "Read,Glob,Grep,Write"`, `reviewer_permission_mode = "dontAsk"`, no --allowedTools in the command at :219. /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/test_interactive.py:186-191 only `assertNotIn("Edit", ...)`, `assertNotIn("Bash", ...)`, `assertEqual(... "--permission-mode" ..., "dontAsk")`. PR 10 test_interactive.py:218 `assertEqual(command[command.index("--allowedTools") + 1], f"Edit(//{completion.resolve().as_posix().lstrip('/')})")`; PR 11 test_interactive.py:238-249 asserts tools == 'Read,Glob,Grep,Write', the Edit rule, `command[-3:-1] == ["--permission-mode", "dontAsk"]` and that every variadic option precedes it.

findings.title: Independence, worktree-change and evidence-change guards in the controller have no tests
findings.detail: PR 9's review_candidate raises 'Reviewer session is not independent of the workers', 'Reviewer worktree changed' and 'Evidence changed during review', but no test triggers any of them. The only independence assertion compares the reviewer UUID against plan launch tokens in a happy-path test. PR 11 tests all three via assert_refused_after_wait; PR 10 tests independence at unit level.
findings.evidence: grep over /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/test_*.py for 'Evidence changed|worktree changed|not independent' returns nothing; code sites at /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:223,225,270,275,277. The happy-path check is `self.assertNotIn(review["reviewer"], {f.plan["nodes"][node]["session_id"] for node in ("ui", "adapter")})` in test_review_node_records_the_reviewer_session_and_its_findings.
findings.verifier_reason: grep for the three error strings across all PR 9 test modules returns nothing. findings.detail: The new four-process test accepts any ordering with one 130 and a final 0, so [130,75,75,0] (an interruption before verification) would pass. The step sequence is deterministic (drill block, review interrupted, review resumed, integrate), and PR 9 and PR 11 assert it exactly. findings.verifier_reason: The sequence is deterministic: process 1 blocks on the drill (75), process 2 retries verification and reaches the review node where the interrupt fires (130), process 3 resumes the review (75), process 4 returns the commit (0). PR 9 and PR 11 assert exactly [75,130,75,0] and both suites pass. The handoff shows the author expected the third process and, on seeing the second, replaced the order assertion rather than correcting it; (4,1,0) also accepts [130,75,75,0].

dimensions.summary: I mapped PRD_REVIEWER_PANE's six work items, eight design-table rows and four acceptance bullets (plus the section-5 live-smoke merge gate) to each branch's code, diffed all four PRDs against main per branch, verified the smoke-test claims against `claude agents --all`, transcripts and run directories, and checked `claude --help` for the variadic-option defect. PR 10 is the only one that does slice A as specified (binds the reviewer session UUID, extends both attach_panels and attach-one, runs the gating smoke test twice with artifacts on disk) and records every deviation in the PRDs; its lapse is bundling B/C pre-run work into A's PR, which leaves new runs unviewable (export 1.2.0 vs main's z.literal('1.0.0')) until B's run merges, and it says so. PR 11 verifies slice A most thoroughly (four live sessions covering deadline, fail-closed and accept paths, plus the variadic --add-dir fix) and records deviations best, but it overrides the umbrella PRD's explicit delivery plan by implementing B and C directly in a 56-file/+6074 diff, ships vestigial feature directories that would assign already-done work, and hand-writes the completion schema outside the repo's contract convention. PR 9 has perfect scope discipline and is candid that the merge gate was skipped, but its native path is broken on first launch (prompt swallowed by variadic --add-dir; write denied under dontAsk with no allow rule) and it silently fails acceptance bullet 2 by treating a reviewer that asks a question as fatal, while its README claims the opposite. Ranking on this dimension: PR 10 > PR 11 > PR 9.

findings.title: Prompt placed after variadic --add-dir; native reviewer starts with no task
findings.detail: run_reviewer builds the command as `--tools … --permission-mode dontAsk --add-dir <run> <prompt>`. On this host's CLI the --add-dir option is variadic, so the positional prompt is consumed as a second directory and the session starts idle. PR 11 reproduced exactly this live (attempt 1 failed in seven seconds) on the same CLI version and reordered its arguments; PR 10 avoided it by placing --add-dir before --tools. PR 9's launch test asserts the value after --add-dir but never the prompt's position, so offline tests cannot see it. This is the class of launch-time failure PRD §5 says the (skipped) smoke test exists to catch.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:217-220: `command = [self.executable, "--bg", "--name", …, "--tools", self.reviewer_tools, "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]`. `claude --help` (2.1.278): `--add-dir <directories...>  Additional directories to allow tool access to`. Test /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/test_interactive.py:171-193 pins `command[command.index("--add-dir") + 1] == str(self.directory)` only. PR 11's fix and pin: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:220-226 and test_interactive.py:245-249 (`command[-3:-1] == ["--permission-mode", "dontAsk"]`).
findings.verifier_reason: The CLI on this host declares --add-dir as variadic and PR 9 puts the positional prompt immediately after its single value, so commander consumes the prompt as a second directory. Main's own worker launch avoids this by ending with --permission-mode <mode> [--dangerously-skip-permissions] prompt; PR 9 introduced --add-dir and placed it last. PR 9's launch test asserts only the value after --add-dir, never the prompt's position. PR 11 reproduced the failure live and pinned the fix; PR 10 places --add-dir before --tools so its prompt follows --permission-mode.
findings.verifier_evidence: `claude --version` -> 2.1.280; `claude --help | grep add-dir` -> `--add-dir <directories...>  Additional directories to allow tool access to`. /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:217-220: `command = [..., "--tools", self.reviewer_tools, "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]`. Main /home/agentops/dev/md-manager/workflow/interactive.py:148-153 ends `"--permission-mode", ...]; if automatic: command.append("--dangerously-skip-permissions"); command.append(prompt)` and never uses --add-dir. PR 9 test_interactive.py:190 `self.assertEqual(command[command.index("--add-dir") + 1], str(self.directory))` with no prompt-position assertion. PR 10 interactive.py:184-186 `"--add-dir", str(self.directory), "--tools", ..., "--permission-mode", "dontAsk", prompt`. PR 11 interactive.py:220-226 comment `--tools, --allowedTools and --add-dir are variadic: any of them directly before the positional prompt would swallow it` and test_interactive.py:247 `self.assertEqual(command[-3:-1], ["--permission-mode", "dontAsk"])`. PR 11 handoff §4: `Attempt 1 failed in seven seconds ... --add-dir is variadic, so the prompt that followed it was swallowed and the session started idle`.

findings.title: Reviewer asking a question is fatal, contradicting acceptance bullet 2 and PR 9's own docs
findings.detail: PRD §5 bullet 2: 'A reviewer that stops to ask a question can be answered in the pane, and the run resumes when the completion file appears and the session goes idle.' PR 9's wait_review raises the moment the native session reports state `blocked`, and its test codifies that. Both PR 10 and PR 11 observed live that `blocked` is precisely the state a reviewer enters when it ends a turn asking a person something (or when a write is refused). PR 9's feature README nonetheless tells the operator they can answer the reviewer's question in the pane. Not recorded as a deviation anywhere.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:207-208: `if row["state"] == "blocked": raise RuntimeError("Reviewer blocked; inspect quota or native error. No billing/provider fallback.")`. Test test_automatic.py:254-262 `test_a_missing_or_blocked_reviewer_stops_rather_than_relaunching` asserts the raise. Docs claim: features/project-workflows/README.md (PR 9 diff): 'you can answer a question the reviewer asks there'. Live observation: PR 10 handoff attempt 1 ('ended its turn asking a person … `claude agents` reported the session as `blocked`'); PR 11 handoff attempt 1. Contrast PR 10 automatic.py:208-210 and PR 11 automatic.py:219-223, both of which note it once and keep waiting.
findings.verifier_reason: wait_review raises on native state `blocked` and the test codifies it. Both other PRs observed live that `blocked` is the state a reviewer enters when it ends a turn asking a person (PR 10 attempt 1: reviewer asked for permission or a paste, `claude agents` showed blocked, controller killed it). PR 9's feature README tells the operator they can answer the reviewer's question in the pane. One nuance: the handoff does list 'a missing or blocked session stopping rather than relaunching' under covered behaviour, so the behaviour is documented as a test case, but it is never identified as a departure from PRD §5 bullet 2 and the README claims the opposite. The finding stands.
findings.verifier_evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:207-208: `if row["state"] == "blocked": raise RuntimeError("Reviewer blocked; inspect quota or native error. No billing/provider fallback.")`. test_automatic.py:254-262 `test_a_missing_or_blocked_reviewer_stops_rather_than_relaunching` ... `with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "Reviewer blocked")`. features/project-workflows/README.md:33 (PR 9): `you can answer a question the reviewer asks there`. PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md §5 bullet 2 (main): `A reviewer that stops to ask a question can be answered in the pane`. PR 10 handoff attempt 1: `It ended its turn asking a person to grant the permission or paste the JSON; claude agents reported the session as blocked; wait_review treated blocked as fatal`. PR 10 automatic.py:206-210 and PR 11 automatic.py:217-223 both note once and keep waiting. PR 9 handoff Increment 2 lists `a missing or blocked session stopping rather than relaunching` as behaviour covered, with no deviation entry. Main's wait_handoffs (automatic.py:104-105) has the same raise for workers, which is what PR 9 mirrored.

findings.title: Merge gate (PRD §5 controlled live smoke test) skipped; three launch-time defects follow
findings.detail: PRD_REVIEWER_PANE §5: 'Before merging, run one controlled live smoke test … This catches the launch-time failures (late pid, pane not ready) that the first live run showed offline tests do not.' PR 9 says plainly it did not run it (PRD status, handoff 'Not done', PR body item 2). The consequence is concrete: the variadic --add-dir defect, the Write-denied-under-dontAsk defect (PR 9 has no --allowedTools rule; both PR 10 and PR 11 measured live that dontAsk denies the write without an `Edit(//path)` rule), and the blocked-is-fatal defect were all found by the other two PRs' smoke runs within minutes. Honest, but the PRD's stated precondition for merging is unmet and the shipped native path does not work.
findings.evidence: docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:60 (main). PR 9 PRD status line: 'the controlled live smoke test in section 5 has **not** been run'. /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/docs/HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md 'Not done' section. interactive.py:184-185 `reviewer_tools = "Read,Glob,Grep,Write"`, `reviewer_permission_mode = "dontAsk"`, no `--allowedTools` anywhere in the command (217-220). PR 10 handoff: 'had its Write to review.completion.json denied twice ("Permission to use Write has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode")'.
findings.verifier_reason: PR 9 states in three places that the §5 smoke test was not run, and all three defects are real: the variadic order is structural (help text plus PR 11's live reproduction), the Write denial under dontAsk with no allow rule was measured live by both PR 10 (Write denied twice, then probes) and PR 11 (probe matrix), and blocked-is-fatal is in the code. PR 9 ships no --allowedTools rule at all, so the reviewer cannot write the completion file even if the prompt had arrived.
findings.verifier_evidence: PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md §5 (main): `Before merging, run one controlled live smoke test ... This catches the launch-time failures (late pid, pane not ready) that the first live run showed offline tests do not.` PR 9 PRD status: `the controlled live smoke test in section 5 has **not** been run`. PR 9 handoff 'Not done': `Nothing here has talked to a real Claude session`. PR 9 body item 2 same. /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:184-185 `reviewer_tools = "Read,Glob,Grep,Write"`, `reviewer_permission_mode = "dontAsk"`; lines 217-220 contain no `--allowedTools`. Edit(//abs/path) allows that one write`. PR 11 handoff: `Write(//abs/path) matches nothing, and acceptEdits allows every write`. findings.title: Prompt instructs an impossible atomic temp-file-then-rename write
findings.detail: The reviewer has only Read/Glob/Grep/Write and no Bash; it cannot rename a file, and under dontAsk a temp-file write would be denied even with a single-path allow rule. dimensions.summary: I read the three bodies, commit messages and handoffs and checked every checkable claim against the worktrees, main, `claude --help`, the smoke artifacts on disk and the reviewer transcripts under ~/.claude/projects. On reviewability PR 9 is the clear winner: 21 files, one concern, docs that match its code, two explicitly named risks, and a handoff whose per-module counts and mutation-check code points all verify. PR 10 is honest and its live evidence is the best of the three (durable, named, and every number I could recompute matched), but a third of its diff is generated schema, a fifth is feature-run prose, one number disagrees between body and handoff, and its RUNBOOK omits the post-merge 1.2.0-vs-1.0.0 viewer breakage that its own body admits. PR 11 is the hardest to approve: 56 files and 6,074 added lines across six concerns in one commit against a PRD that asked for three focused diffs, a wrong baseline ("59 before" vs main's 70/71), a handoff that claims the completion schema was generated with fixtures when it is hand-written and untested in the contract suite, smoke evidence in an unnamed ephemeral scratchpad that reused the live run id, and feature directories that tell future workers to implement what the PR already implemented. PR 11's RUNBOOK itself is accurate and its live smoke covered more of PRD section 5 than PR 10's.

Estimated 2.5-3.5 reviewer hours. Description accuracy: "no server/ or src/ change" true (diffstat); "94 Python (70 before)" consistent with main's 70 runtime / 71 static and the parent's run; "13 contract (10 before)" matches 8+5 vs 5+5; handoff's "17 passed" test_interactive and "11 passed" test_pipeline match static counts (12 defs minus the BackendTest.test_value fixture at test_pipeline.py:118); mutation-check code points exist (interactive.py:367 `if REVIEWER in mapping`, automatic.py:362 `if failures == ["review"]`), exit codes `[75, 130, 75, 0]` at test_automatic.py:433. Steers to risks: yes, names the dontAsk-write question and the missing live test as the merge gate. Docs: `attach-one --node reviewer` matches `choices=[*NODES, REVIEWER]` with REVIEWER="reviewer"; RUNBOOK/README/INTERACTIVE/VALIDATION are internally consistent except VALIDATION.md's "read-only tool set" and the README/RUNBOOK claim that the reviewer "is allowed to write" only the completion file when the code has no `--allowedTools` at all (grep count 0) and the prompt follows the variadic `--add-dir` (interactive.py:220), so the launch as written cannot work live. dimensions.ranking_reason: PR 9 is a single-concern, 1.2k-line change whose every doc and number matches its code and whose description tells the approver exactly what is unproven; it can be reviewed in one sitting. PR 10 is honest and its live evidence is the most verifiable of the three, but it triples the diff with generated schemas and feature-run prose for slices it does not ship, has a 96/95 inconsistency, and its RUNBOOK omits the viewer breakage its body admits. PR 11 delivers the most but is the least reviewable: six concerns and 6k lines in one commit against a PRD that asked for focused diffs, a wrong baseline count, a handoff claim about generated/fixture-tested schemas that is false for the completion schema, evidence in an unnamed ephemeral directory, and feature directories that instruct future workers to build what already exists.
dimensions.verifier_note: The reviewer's ranking survives verification. PR 9 is a single-concern 1.2k-line change whose every number matches the unittest loader exactly (70 -> 94, 10 -> 13 contracts) and whose handoff and body tell the approver precisely what is unproven; its one confirmed high is that three docs state a single-file write allow-list the code never implements and the launch as written cannot work live, which its own body half-acknowledges (dontAsk) and half-misses (variadic --add-dir). PR 10 is honest and its live evidence is the only durable, named, independently recomputable set of the three (I re-verified the directory, verdict, findings and stop time); after downgrading the scope finding to low (the PRDs assign this pre-run work to a human commit) its remaining debt is the RUNBOOK export paragraph that omits the 1.2.0-vs-1.0.0 viewer breakage its body admits, a 95/96 slip, and read-only wording drift. PR 11 delivers the most and its RUNBOOK section is accurate to its code, but it is the hardest to approve: one 6,074-line squashed commit across six concerns with no rationale for discarding the PRD's focused-diff plan, a handoff claim about fixture-tested regenerated schemas that is false for the completion schema, gate-critical smoke evidence in an unnamed ephemeral scratchpad under the live run's id, and feature directories that assign future workers to rebuild what already shipped. I downgraded its baseline-count finding to low because 124 is exact and the error looks like a module-list slip, not inflation.

dimensions.summary: I checked each PR's stated evidence against what is actually on disk: PR 10's smoke run under ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/smoke/review-smoke-001, PR 11's scratch run under its session scratchpad (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-agentops-dev-md-manager-ultra/9ef1cac0-.../scratchpad/smoke-run), the reviewer transcripts and job metadata under ~/.claude (which preserve the exact launch flags), `claude agents --all --json`, the print-mode probe sessions, and the unittest loader's collected counts (loaded, not run). PR 10's narrative is reproducible to the byte: sessions dccd22b5/5865c9a6, bundle sha256 58308a53 matches the file, verdict blocked 1 P1 + 6 P2, 7/7 requirement quotes found verbatim by my own script, stop marker with stopped_at, pane w5:pW, both attempt logs and all five probe result files retained. PR 11's four sessions (7eb01f17, a4c348e5, 25d99bf4, f36b923d) all exist and the job metadata proves its best discovery (the prompt swallowed by variadic --add-dir on attempt 1); 8/8 verbatim quotes and the section-5 re-export copy check out, but /tmp/permtest is gone (probes recoverable only from transcripts), attempt 2 is misreported as "nine P2 findings" when the payload was 4 P2 + 5 P3, and the "59 before" baseline is wrong (70). PR 9's offline evidence is exact and honest (94/70/13, every named test and mutation-check code path exists) but the launch command it green-tests is proven non-functional by the other two PRs' live runs on the same CLI (no allow rule under dontAsk, and the prompt placed directly after --add-dir).
dimensions.pr9: Honest and internally consistent, but thin on the evidence that matters. Every checkable offline claim holds: unittest loader collects exactly 94 cases (main: 70), contracts 8+5=13 (main 10), test_interactive 17 and test_pipeline 11 as stated; `ReviewCompletionTests` (test_automatic.py:159), `test_only_an_interrupted_review_of_a_live_session_resumes` (:263), `test_recovery_in_actual_new_controller_processes` (:392), the `REVIEWER in mapping` early return (interactive.py:367), the `failures == ["review"]` branch (automatic.py:362), the `reviewer_tools`/`reviewer_permission_mode` constants (interactive.py:184-185) and `FakeSessions.run_reviewer` (test_pipeline.py:68) all exist, and the "8 != 4" mutation result matches the pane test's `before = len(calls)` idempotence assertion (test_interactive.py:253-256, four herdr calls doubled). The handoff says plainly that the PRD section 5 live gate was not run and anticipates the dontAsk write refusal. What it does not know: the launch it pins in `test_reviewer_launches_read_only_in_the_candidate_worktree` is demonstrably broken on this CLI (2.1.278). interactive.py:217-220 passes no --allowedTools and puts the prompt immediately after the variadic `--add-dir <dir>`; PR 11's attempt-1 job record shows exactly that shape swallowing the prompt, and PR 10's attempt 1 shows Write denied under dontAsk even with a Write(//path) rule. So the green suite certifies a command that cannot complete a review. Evidence quality: real and honest, but the merge gate is unmet and the tests pin the wrong behaviour.
dimensions.pr10: The best evidence of the three: modest in scope, flawless in fidelity, and retained where it can be found. The scratch run lives in the persistent state dir with a distinct id (review-smoke-001). Verified: review.completion.json and review.json carry reviewer_session 5865c9a6-46df-4c72-9196-f717dc4819b9, bundle_sha256 58308a53f0bc... (equals `sha256sum review-bundle.json`), candidate b5385b3e50a6..., verdict blocked with 1 P1 + 6 P2; my script found all 7 `requirement` strings verbatim in plan.json nodes/ui/task or nodes/adapter/task (7/7); review.stop.json has stopped: true, pid 827174, stopped_at 2026-09-21T20:00:27.411Z; terminals.json has review pane w5:pW in tab w5:tF bound to the session UUID; events.jsonl has the three timeline lines quoted in the handoff; `claude agents --all` lists dccd22b5 as stopped and 5865c9a6 as done. ~/.claude/jobs/dccd22b5/state.json respawnFlags show `--allowedTools Write(//.../review.completion.json)` and the transcript shows two Write calls both denied over 512.7 s (handoff: 513 s); jobs/5865c9a6 shows the `Edit(//...)` rule and one Write with zero denials over 435.7 s (driver log: 442 s). Both driver logs (smoke_review.log, smoke_review2.log) are retained with the tracebacks the handoff describes, and permtest/out holds exactly the five probe results claimed (write-abs-safe denied, write-abs-nosafe denied, edit-abs-safe done, write-bare-safe done, other denied). The live run was not touched (latest mtime 15:52, version 1.0.0). Tests named as added after attempt 1 exist (test_automatic.py:560, test_interactive.py:204/218). Only nits: the handoff says 95 Python tests where the loader collects 96 (the PR body says 96), and "217 messages" is not reproducible from the transcript (165 user+assistant records). Limits (pane Q&A, live interruption, 1.2.0 export gap) are stated honestly.
dimensions.pr11: The broadest evidence and the most valuable single discovery, with weaker retention and two narrative inaccuracies. The scratch run is not at /tmp/permtest but at the ultra session scratchpad's smoke-run/; all four reviewer sessions exist in `claude agents --all --json` under workflow-project-workflows-001-reviewer with start times 20:02:48 (7eb01f17), 20:07:32 (a4c348e5), 20:28:04 (25d99bf4), 20:41:17 (f36b923d). ~/.claude/jobs/7eb01f17/state.json respawnFlags end with `"--add-dir", "<run>", "<the whole prompt>"`, which is hard proof of the variadic swallow claim; a4c348e5's flags carry `Write(//...)` and its transcript shows one denied Write; 25d99bf4 and f36b923d carry `Edit(//...)`. The attempt-3 file is preserved (attempt3-review.completion.json: 8 findings, severities include three P3, launch_token 03b8675c) and attempt 4's artifacts are complete (automatic-review.json succeeded, accepted_at 20:51:29Z, review.json approved with 8 P2, review.stop.json stopped: true, terminals.json pane w5:p11 in tab w5:tG, four events incl. "Reviewer pane attached"); my script found 8/8 requirement quotes verbatim. Transcript spans 698/734/609 s match the stated 1205-deadline/741/615 s story, and plan.json pins review_timeout_seconds 1200. Section 5 checks out: the copy at scratchpad/runs/project-workflows/project-workflows-001 has version 1.2.0, review approved/print/dd7bdcd1 with 6 findings, and artifact patch-review-2bb474561d3e matches the live review.diff sha256 and 289187 bytes; acceptance-api.log shows every route 200; the live run is untouched. Loader counts match exactly (124 Python, 30 backend, 15 browser, 13 contract). Discrepancies: attempt 2 is described as "nine P2 findings" but the denied Write payload is 4 P2 + 5 P3 (the P3 invention was visible one attempt earlier than the narrative says); "59 before" is wrong (main collects 70); /tmp/permtest no longer exists and the four "variants" are only recoverable as five print sessions in ~/.claude/projects/-tmp (their outcomes do match the claims); attempts 1-3 controller-side logs were overwritten, so "seven seconds", "1205 s" and the deadline message are consistent but not directly checkable; and the scratch run reused the live run's id and launch name.
dimensions.ranking_reason: PR 10 first because every number, hash, session id, timestamp, flag and probe outcome it states was reproducible from retained artifacts in a durable location, and its limits are stated precisely. PR 11 second: its live evidence is larger and its variadic --add-dir finding is the most important fact any of the three produced (and is provable from job metadata), but the handoff misreports attempt 2's severities, mis-states the test baseline, lost the /tmp/permtest directory, overwrote the earlier attempts' controller logs, and parks everything in a session-scoped /tmp scratchpad. PR 9 last: its offline evidence is exact and it is honest that the PRD's live gate was skipped, but the launch command its green tests certify is proven not to work by the other two PRs' live runs, so the evidence would mislead anyone who merged on the test results alone.
dimensions.verifier_note: Ranking unchanged after verification, but two of the reviewer's three findings were overstated and one of its low findings was wrong. PR 10 first: every headline claim I re-derived matched, including two the reviewer called unreproducible or did not check: the session's own turn_duration record gives durationMs 513037 and messageCount 217 (handoff: '513 s and 217 messages'), and cost-state gives USD 6.20 ('about USD 6'); bundle sha256 58308a53... equals `sha256sum review-bundle.json`; 7/7 requirement quotes verbatim by my own script; the Edit(//...) rule, prompt-last order and preflight --allowedTools requirement are pinned in code and tests (test_interactive.py:204-224, pipeline.py:565). Its only inaccuracies are '95 tests' (loader: 96; PR body says 96) and the overwritten attempt-1 controller files. PR 11 second: the broadest evidence and the most important discovery (the variadic --add-dir swallow, provable from jobs/7eb01f17 with an empty intent and no transcript), the deadline path corroborated by a 1202 s cost-state duration, the six audit lenses backed by six subagent transcripts (20:54-21:17Z), gates-final.log matching 130/13/30/15/15/124 exactly, mutation scratch copies present, and section 5 verified (copy at version 1.2.0, dd7bdcd1, 6 findings, 11 x statusCode 200 incl. /reviews/1, /inputs and the patch-review-2bb474561d3e artifact). It loses to PR 10 on fidelity: 'nine P2' (was 4 P2 + 5 P3), '59 before' (main collects 70 across the same seven modules), a cited /tmp/permtest that no longer exists, attempts 1-3 controller logs overwritten, the whole scratch run in a session-scoped /tmp directory, and the live run's id and launch name reused for the scratch sessions. PR 9 last: its offline numbers are exact (94/13, per-module 32/9/2/17/11/11/12; exit codes [75,130,75,0] at test_automatic.py:433; pane idempotence via four herdr calls so '8 != 4' is right; in-place mutation backups a2.bak/a3.bak/automatic.py.bak/i.bak survive in its scratchpad) and it says plainly that the live gate was skipped, but the launch its green suite pins cannot work on this CLI for two independent reasons, and its stated fallback (a bypass mode) is the wrong fix. Honest evidence of the wrong thing.

findings.title: Green-tested reviewer launch is proven non-functional by the other PRs' live runs
findings.detail: PR 9 never ran the live gate and its pinned launch has two defects the live runs of PR 10 and PR 11 exposed on the same claude 2.1.278: (1) no --allowedTools rule at all under --permission-mode dontAsk, so the completion Write is denied (PR 10's attempt 1 was denied even with a Write(//path) rule; PR 9 has none); (2) the prompt is the positional argument immediately after the variadic `--add-dir <dir>`, so it is consumed as a second directory and the session starts idle (PR 11's attempt-1 job record shows exactly this). The test asserts `--add-dir` is followed by the directory but never guards the prompt position, so the suite certifies a command that cannot complete a review. The handoff anticipates (1) but not (2).

findings.title: The handoff's anticipated remedy for a refused write ('--add-dir plus a bypass mode') is the wrong fix and would remove the containment the same handoff relies on
findings.detail: HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md:55 hedges the untested launch with: 'reviewer_tools and reviewer_permission_mode are single constants if the live smoke test shows dontAsk refuses that write; the fallback would be --add-dir plus a bypass mode.' The live runs of PRs 10 and 11 show the actual fix is a single Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json) allow rule under dontAsk plus moving the prompt off the variadic --add-dir; a bypass mode would let the reviewer write anywhere, contradicting the handoff's own containment argument two sentences earlier ('no Bash, no agents, no MCP servers ... worktree must still be the clean candidate'). So the risk statement is not merely incomplete (it misses the prompt swallow) but points a merger toward weakening the security boundary rather than the two-line fix. This is a claims-quality defect distinct from the code bug already in finding 1.
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/docs/HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md:55 quoted above. Live fix in both other PRs: md-manager-high/workflow/interactive.py:184-186 `"--add-dir", str(self.directory), "--tools", "Read,Glob,Grep,Write", "--allowedTools", f"Edit(//{...})", "--permission-mode", "dontAsk", prompt` and md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:223-226 `"--tools", "Read,Glob,Grep,Write", "--allowedTools", f"Edit(//{completion})", "--add-dir", str(self.directory), "--permission-mode", "dontAsk", prompt`. Probe 86c88a78 (Edit(//) rule under dontAsk): allowed.json created, other.json denied; probe ffbed836 (acceptEdits): both writes succeeded. PR 11 test_interactive.py:246-250 comments '--tools, --allowedTools and --add-dir are variadic: the prompt must directly follow a single-value option, or the CLI swallows it and the session starts idle (seen live)'.

findings.title: '59 before' is wrong: main collects 70 Python tests across the same seven modules
findings.detail: The handoff's gate table and the PR body both state 'Python: 124 passed (59 before)'. Loading main's workflow/test_*.py with the unittest loader (not run) gives 16+8+2+12+9+11+12 = 70; test_export.py does not exist on main, so the eight-module command in the handoff could not have produced a baseline on main at all. PRs 9 and 10 both state the baseline correctly as 70.
findings.evidence: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python -B` loader in /home/agentops/dev/md-manager: test_automatic 16, test_feature_launch 8, test_graph 2, test_interactive 12, test_pipeline 9, test_sessions 11, test_verification 12, TOTAL 70; `ls workflow/test_*.py` on main shows no test_export.py. md-manager-ultra/docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md section 3: '124 passed (59 before)'; pr11-body.md: '124 tests (59 before)'. Ultra loader: 48+8+10+2+21+12+11+12 = 124 (matches).

dimensions.dimension: gap:No aggregation rule: not-applicable dimensions are scored 0/1/6, and 'code quality' vs 'did the better job' are never separated
dimensions.summary: I investigated the aggregation gap rather than re-scoring dimensions: I reconstructed per-PR sums from the verifier means quoted in the gap (the full per-dimension table is not on disk; only the aggregates, PR 9's adapter 0 / ui 1 / export 6 and PR 11's adapter 8.5 / ui 8 are known), read the umbrella and slice PRDs on main to establish which surfaces slice A was told not to touch, and verified in code every fact the disputed scores rest on (adapter version gate, the status-to-export rewrite path, plan-schema strictness, schema provenance, reviewer launch flags). Code quality is PR 11 > PR 10 > PR 9 under every convention I tried (PR 11 8.3, PR 10 between 7.1 and 8.2 depending on its two unknown N/A-surface scores, PR 9 4.9). But once one N/A convention (exclude dimensions where a PR shipped nothing by design) is applied consistently and the two questions are separated with equal weight, "did the better job" most likely flips to PR 10 > PR 11 > PR 9 (about 7.7 vs 7.3 vs 5.5); PR 11 wins that question only if code quality is weighted at 65% or more of "the job". So the gap changes the second answer and PR 9's score (4.4 to 5.5), not the code-quality ranking. Along the way I resolved the export-bump contradiction as HIGH for PR 10 (a routine `workflow status` on the historic run rewrites it at 1.2.0 and main's adapter then 500s the entire workflow list), confirmed PR 9's compat score is earned rather than "by omission", and found that the "PR 11 rewarded twice" concern is arithmetically void under a mean (adding 8.5 and 8 to six dims averaging 8.32 yields 8.30).
dimensions.pr9: Code quality 4.9 (six applicable code dims; adapter-server and ui-and-browser-tests excluded as by-design N/A per docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:17 and docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:5; export-and-compat stays in and is genuinely earned because main's planSchema is a non-strict z.object (server/projects.ts:84) so the new reviewer_transport key is harmless and export_state.py:38 keeps "1.0.0"). Process 6.0. Overall (equal weight) 5.5, up from the raw 4.4, but still last on both questions for a substantive reason, not an N/A artefact: the launch at md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:184-185,219-220 passes `--tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write --permission-mode dontAsk` with no `--allowedTools` rule, which PR 10 (handoff line 59-60) and PR 11 (handoff line 54-55) both observed live is denied, so the default native transport cannot produce a verdict; PR 9 skipped the smoke test the PRD makes the merge gate (PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:60) and says so honestly (body item 2). Its attach_panels also never adds the third pane (only attach_reviewer_pane does), against work item 3's wording. Cleanest scope discipline and the tightest diff of the three, but a non-working feature.
dimensions.pr10: Code quality between 7.1 and 8.2 depending on the two verifier scores it received for adapter-server and ui (unknown to me; it shipped no server/ or src/ file, so under the exclude convention both drop out and its six real code dims average (50.4 - a - u)/6); my point estimate is 7.4. Process 8.0, the best of the three: it did exactly the slice A the PRDs describe, proved it live twice with artifacts on disk (~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/smoke/review-smoke-001/ contains review.completion.json, review.json, review.stop.json, review.interactive.json), and its "extra" work is the B PRD's own pre-run list (PRD_REVIEW_RESULT.md:11-19). Overall (equal weight) about 7.7. Its one real code defect is HIGH and I verified the mechanism end to end: `workflow status <run>` reaches `print(f"Report: {report(runtime, state)}")` (md-manager-high/workflow/pipeline.py:688), report() calls export_state (479-481), which writes EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0" (export_state.py:16); main's adapter still has `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)` with '1.0.0' (server/projects.ts:37,52), listRuns (320-346) has try/finally with no catch, and projectRun throws invalidRun -> 500 RUN_STORAGE_INVALID (420-421). One status on project-workflows-001 hides the whole workflow list, and the handoff (line 77) understates this as "that run's listing". It is a narrow, fixable defect that the PRD's own plan half-creates, and it is already priced into its export-and-compat score. PR 10 is also the only PR with a single-sourced completion schema (v1.ts -> generated JSON -> completion_schema() at automatic.py:129-131).
dimensions.pr11: Code quality 8.3 (all eight code dims apply; it wrote adapter and UI code and it is good). Process 6.3, dragged by a confirmed high: it implemented B and C directly in one 56-file, +6074 commit after the user had, in the very commit it branched from (61e4752 "Tighten slice A scope and clarify slice ordering"), split the work so that "each run has a smaller, focused diff and a blocked run loses one slice, not all three" (PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:21), and it rewrote the umbrella PRD's status to say so (its own PRD diff). Overall (equal weight) 7.3. The critic's worry that it is "rewarded twice" for the deviation does not survive arithmetic: its other six code dims average 8.32 and adding 8.5 and 8 moves the mean to 8.30, so under a mean the only net effect of the deviation is the spec-fidelity penalty. It is the only PR under which the existing run keeps loading after re-export or `status` (server/projects.ts:44 EXPORT_VERSIONS = ['1.0.0','1.1.0','1.2.0']; test_export.py:185; projects.test.ts:1049), it caught the variadic --add-dir ordering bug (interactive.py:220-226), and it ran four live sessions. Against that, it hand-writes reviewCompletion.schema.json (contracts/workflow/README.md:12 admits "hand-written, not generated from v1.ts"), adds no contract test for it, and duplicates the shape again in Python (automatic.py:129-141), the same triplication contracts-and-schemas faulted PR 9 for.
dimensions.ranking_reason: This is the "did the better job" ranking under one stated rule: exclude a dimension for a PR that shipped nothing on that surface by design (adapter-server and ui for PR 9 and PR 10; export-and-compat stays for everyone), score each fact once (the PR 10 version mismatch lives in export-and-compat only), then average code-quality and process equally. Under that rule PR 10 scores about 7.7, PR 11 7.3 and PR 9 5.5; PR 10 beats PR 11 for any value of its two unknown N/A-surface scores summing below 10.6, which is near-certain given PR 9 received 0 and 1 on the same two dims for the same reason. Substantively: PR 10 did the slice the user scoped hours earlier, proved it live, and its one high (status rewrites the historic run at 1.2.0 and the whole workflow list 500s) is narrow and fixable; PR 11 has the best code and the most complete feature but did a different, larger job than the one specified, in the single big commit the plan was written to avoid; PR 9 is last on both questions because its native reviewer cannot write the completion file and it skipped the gate that would have shown that. The code-quality ranking is different and robust: PR 11 (8.3) > PR 10 (7.1-8.2) > PR 9 (4.9). PR 11 takes "better job" too only if the person weights code quality at 65% or more of the job; the raw 11-dimension means (7.8 / 6.7 / 4.4) hide that flip because they score PR 9 and PR 10 at or near zero on surfaces the PRD told them not to touch.
dimensions.verifier_note: Rule I applied, stated once and used for all three: (1) code quality = mean over the code dimensions where the PR shipped code, with a dimension excluded (not 0/1) when the PRD told that PR not to touch the surface; export-and-compat is never excluded because every PR writes plan.json/run-state.json that the adapter reads. (2) 'Did the job' scored separately on four checkable facts: does the shipped feature work as launched, does main stay consistent after merge (existing run and new runs keep loading), fidelity to the plan the person wrote in 61e4752, and evidence/honesty (live gate run, handoff accuracy). (3) Overall = equal weight of the two. Code quality is PR 11 > PR 10 > PR 9 under any convention and I agree (8.0 / 7.3 / 4.8). On 'did the job' I do not find the reviewer's flip: PR 11 7.5, PR 10 7.3, PR 9 4.5. PR 11 is the only PR whose result actually works end to end and leaves main consistent (probe: its adapter serves the re-exported live run and 1.0.0 runs; it found two real CLI bugs live and pinned the argv order with a test), against which it ignored the slicing plan, skipped the dogfooding purpose of B's run, and hand-wrote its schema. PR 10 did the prescribed slice, proved it live twice and single-sourced the schema, but merging it makes the first routine `workflow status` on the historic run break the viewer's whole workflow list (probe-confirmed) and its handoff understates that; the window is PRD-designed, but PR 10 neither flagged nor mitigated it. PR 9's native reviewer cannot start (prompt swallowed by variadic --add-dir) or write (no allow rule), and it skipped the gate that would have shown both. PR 10 and PR 11 are within half a point; the order flips to PR 10 if the person weights adherence to their own slicing plan above a merge-safe, working delivery. PR 9 is last on both questions for substantive reasons, not because of N/A dimensions.

findings.title: Three N/A conventions (0, 1, 6) are inconsistent; adopt exclude, and export-and-compat is not N/A for PR 9
findings.detail: Dimensions where a PR shipped nothing by design should be excluded from that PR's mean, not scored 0 (adapter-server), 1 (ui) or 6 (export). The umbrella PRD assigns slice A to `workflow/` + `contracts/workflow/` + docs and defers server/ and src/ to feature runs, and the diffstats confirm PR 9 and PR 10 touch neither directory. export-and-compat is different: PR 9's plan.json gains `reviewer_transport`, which is input to the adapter, so the dimension applies and PR 9's 6 is earned (main's planSchema is a non-strict z.object and zod 4.6.5 strips unknown keys; export_state.py stays at 1.0.0). Recomputed: PR 9 all-11 4.4 -> 9-dim 5.3; excluding export as well would wrongly give 5.2.

findings.title: Separating 'code quality' from 'better job' with a consistent N/A rule most likely flips the second answer to PR 10
findings.detail: Code-only means with N/A excluded: PR 9 29.4/6 = 4.9; PR 11 66.4/8 = 8.3; PR 10 = (50.4 - a - u)/6 where a,u are its adapter/ui verifier scores (not on disk). PR 11 keeps the code lead unless a+u < 0.5. Process means: 6.0 / 8.0 / 6.3. 'Better job' at equal weight: PR 9 5.45, PR 11 7.32, PR 10 = ((50.4-a-u)/6 + 8)/2, which exceeds PR 11 whenever a+u < 10.6. PR 9 received 0 and 1 on those two dims for the identical reason (nothing shipped there), so PR 10's are almost certainly well under 10.6; at a+u = 6 PR 10 is 7.7. PR 11 wins 'better job' only if code weight w satisfies 8.3w + 6.33(1-w) > 7.4w + 8.0(1-w), i.e. w > 0.65. The raw 11-dim means (7.8/6.7/4.4) hide this because they score two PRs near zero on surfaces the PRD told them not to touch.
findings.evidence: Inputs are the verifier aggregates quoted in the gap: raw 11-dim 4.4/6.7/7.8; code-only 3.8 (4.9 sans N/A)/6.3/8.3; process 6.0/8.0/6.3; PR 9 adapter 0, ui 1, export 6; PR 11 adapter 8.5, ui 8. Reconstructed sums: PR 9 code 30.4, process 18.0; PR 10 code 50.4, process 24.0; PR 11 code 66.4 (six non-adapter/ui dims sum 49.9), process 19.0. No verifier score file exists under the scratchpad (`ls` and `grep -rl verifier` returned only diffs and run copies).
findings.dimension: gap:No aggregation rule: not-applicable dimensions are scored 0/1/6, and 'code quality' vs 'did the better job' are never separated
findings.verifier_reason: The arithmetic is correct (PR 10 beats PR 11 at equal weight iff its unknown adapter+ui scores sum below 10.56; PR 11 wins iff code weight > 0.65), but the conclusion 'most likely flips' rests on two unknowns the reviewer guessed: that PR 10 scored near zero on adapter-server and ui, and that equal weighting is the right rule. The reviewer's own text quotes adapter-server crediting PR 10 with 'no run broken at merge time', which suggests a non-trivial score there; at a=7,u=5 PR 10's six-dim code mean is 6.4 and its equal-weight overall 7.2 < 7.32, so no flip. My own substantive assessment (below) also does not support a clear flip: PR 10's one confirmed high is a real merge-time regression the user would hit on the first `workflow status`, while PR 11's penalty is a plan deviation. The separation itself is the right move; the direction of the flip is not established.
findings.verifier_evidence: Threshold check: ((50.4-a-u)/6 + 8)/2 > (8.3+6.33)/2 = 7.32 <=> a+u < 10.56. Weight check: 8.3w + 6.33(1-w) > 7.4w + 8.0(1-w) <=> w > 0.65. No per-dimension score file on disk (`ls /tmp/.../scratchpad`). Counter-example: a=7, u=5 -> PR 10 code (50.4-12)/6 = 6.4, overall (6.4+8)/2 = 7.2 < 7.32.

findings.title: `workflow status` on the historic run rewrites it at 1.2.0 and main's adapter then 500s the whole workflow list
findings.detail: Resolves the export-bump contradiction as HIGH, agreeing with export-and-compat and not with adapter-server's 'no run broken at merge time'. The status CLI branch calls report(), report() calls export_state(), export_state writes EXPORT_VERSION 1.2.0; main's adapter validates `version: z.literal('1.0.0')`, listRuns wraps projectRun in try/finally with no catch, and projectRun throws invalidRun (500 RUN_STORAGE_INVALID). So the first routine status on project-workflows-001 after merge makes the entire project-workflows workflow unlistable, violating the 'existing run must keep loading' criterion. The B PRD does plan a 1.1.0-before-adapter window (pre-run work is ours; server/ is the worker's), so part of this is PRD-designed, but the silent rewrite of the historic run by a read-style command is PR 10's own. Under the score-each-fact-once rule this belongs to export-and-compat; adapter-server for PR 10 should be N/A. Note exportSchema is also a non-strict z.object, so the added review/inputs sections alone would not break anything; only the version literal does.
findings.evidence: md-manager-high/workflow/pipeline.py:686-688 `else:` (status) ... `print(f"Report: {report(runtime, state)}")`; :479-481 `def report(runtime, state)` ... `export_state(runtime, state)`; md-manager-high/workflow/export_state.py:16 `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0"`, :124 `"version": EXPORT_VERSION`. md-manager-high/server/projects.ts:37 `const EXPORT_VERSION = '1.0.0'`, :51-52 `const exportSchema = z.object({ version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION),`; :320-346 listRuns `try { ... projectRun(...) } finally { await directory.close() }` (no catch); :420-421 `if (!parsedExport.success) throw invalidRun(runId, ...)`; :226-228 invalidRun -> `ProjectApiError(500, 'RUN_STORAGE_INVALID', ...)`. Live run today: run-state version 1.0.0 (python probe). docs/PRD_REVIEW_RESULT.md:11 `## 2. Pre-run work (ours, before prepare)`, :17 `Export version 1.1.0`, :27 adapter owns `server/`.

findings.title: Handoff understates the blast radius of the export bump and misses the status path
findings.detail: The handoff knows an explicit re-export would break the viewer for that run but describes the merged behaviour as affecting 'that run's listing' only, when the verified effect is a 500 for the whole workflow list, and it does not mention that `status` re-exports implicitly. A reviewer relying on the handoff would under-rate the risk.

Contrast server/projects.ts:320-346 (list throws) and pipeline.py:688 (status calls report).

findings.title: Why PR 9 is last on both questions: the native reviewer is never allowed to write, and the gate that would have shown it was skipped
findings.detail: Not an N/A artefact. The launch passes Write in --tools under dontAsk with no --allowedTools rule; both other PRs observed live on CLI 2.1.278 that this write is denied, so PR 9's default transport ends every review at the deadline (or, since PR 9 treats native 'blocked' as fatal, immediately). PR 9 is candid about it, which is why its process score is not lower, but the shipped feature does not work.
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:184-185 `reviewer_tools = "Read,Glob,Grep,Write"` / `reviewer_permission_mode = "dontAsk"`; :219-220 `"--tools", self.reviewer_tools, "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt` (no --allowedTools). md-manager-high/docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:59-60 `had its Write to review.completion.json denied twice ("Permission to use Write has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode")`; md-manager-ultra/docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:54 `its single Write of the completion file was denied`. pr9-body.md item 2: `The controlled live smoke test (PRD section 5) has not been run.` docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:60 `Before merging, run one controlled live smoke test`.

findings.verifier_reason: The launch flags are exactly as quoted (Write in --tools, dontAsk, no --allowedTools), both other PRs observed the denial live on the same CLI, and `blocked` is fatal in PR 9's wait_review. The finding is if anything understated: PR 9's argv puts the prompt directly after `--add-dir <dir>`, and `claude --help` shows `--add-dir <directories...>` is variadic, so the prompt is consumed as a directory and the session starts idle (PR 11 hit exactly this live in 7 s). findings.title: 'Rewarded twice, penalised once' is arithmetically void under a mean; the deviation's net effect is one process penalty
findings.detail: PR 11's six code dims other than adapter and ui sum to 49.9 (mean 8.32). Adding adapter 8.5 and ui 8 gives 66.4/8 = 8.30. The extra dims therefore add nothing to its code-quality mean; the only net effect of implementing B and C directly is the spec-fidelity high inside its 6.3 process mean. That is a single, correctly placed penalty, and it is the reason PR 11 loses 'better job' at equal weight despite winning code quality. The deviation itself is confirmed: the branch commit 61e4752 is the one that tightened slice A and set the A-then-runs order, and PR 11 rewrote the umbrella status to record the choice.

findings.title: PR 9's reviewer launch hands the prompt to the variadic --add-dir, so the session starts with no task
findings.detail: The argv ends `"--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt`. `claude --help` documents `--add-dir <directories...>` as variadic, so the prompt is consumed as a second directory and the session starts idle; PR 11 hit exactly this in its first live attempt ('the prompt that followed it was swallowed and the session started idle'). PR 9's own test asserts that `--add-dir` is followed by the run directory but never that the prompt survives, so the suite passes with the bug. PR 10 avoided it by accident of ordering (`--add-dir` first, prompt after `--permission-mode dontAsk`); PR 11 avoided it deliberately and pinned the order with a test. This is a second, independent reason PR 9's native transport cannot produce a verdict, distinct from the missing --allowedTools rule.
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:217-220 `command = [self.executable, "--bg", "--name", ..., "--tools", self.reviewer_tools, "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]`. `claude --help` line 10: `--add-dir <directories...>            Additional directories to allow tool access to`. md-manager-ultra/docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:52 `Attempt 1 failed in seven seconds ... --add-dir is variadic, so the prompt that followed it was swallowed`. md-manager-opus/workflow/test_interactive.py:189 `self.assertEqual(command[command.index("--add-dir") + 1], str(self.directory))` (no prompt assertion). md-manager-high/workflow/interactive.py:182-186 `--add-dir <dir> --tools ... --allowedTools ... --permission-mode dontAsk prompt`. md-manager-ultra/workflow/test_interactive.py:247-249 `self.assertEqual(command[-3:-1], ["--permission-mode", "dontAsk"])` and `assertLess(command.index(option), command.index("--permission-mode"))` for --tools/--allowedTools/--add-dir.

findings.title: The status-triggered rewrite is main's behaviour and the pre-adapter window is the PRD's plan; PR 10's own fault is following it without flagging or mitigating

PR 10 is the only PR that followed that plan literally, so it inherited the breakage. findings.title: By skipping the feature runs, PR 11 also skipped the PRD's dogfooding goal: the reviewer pane has never run inside a full automatic run
findings.detail: The umbrella PRD orders B as a feature run partly so that 'B's run then exercises the reviewer pane live', i.e. the workflow tool reviews its own next change with the new pane. PR 11's four live sessions were all driven-alone review nodes on a scratch copy; no worker launch, handoff wait or integration path ran with the native reviewer. Its handoff says the feature runs were not launched. This makes the spec-fidelity penalty substantive (a stated acceptance path was bypassed), not merely a diff-size complaint, and it means the person still owes a full run before trusting the pane in production.
