dimensions.dimension: gap:One root-cause defect is charged once per dimension with no deduplication; PR 9's launch defect appears in 7 of 11 dimensions, PR 10's export bump in 6
dimensions.summary: I built a distinct-root-cause ledger for each PR from the code (not the other dimensions' write-ups), verified each defect's mechanism and fix size, and resolved the contradictions that touch deduplication. PR 9 has one dominant root cause (an argv/permission/blocked-handling family at md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:217-220 and automatic.py:207-208) whose code fix is three source lines plus one test, but whose real cause is the skipped merge-gating live smoke test; PR 10 has one dominant root cause (EXPORT_VERSION 1.2.0 vs main's z.literal('1.0.0')) whose fix is one line, but its blast radius is larger than PR 10's handoff admits because `workflow.pipeline <run> status` calls report() which re-exports the live run (pipeline.py:688). PR 11's dominant issue (implementing B and C directly) is not a code defect and has no fix; its remaining distinct defects are all low. Charged once each, the three PRs land within 1.5 points of each other: PR 11 7.0, PR 10 6.5, PR 9 5.5. Deduplication removes roughly six duplicate charges from PR 9, about ten from PR 10 and about six from PR 11, which shifts per-dimension averages by well under 1 point and does not move any PR by 2 or more, so the ranking PR 11 > PR 10 > PR 9 on quality survives, with the gap between PR 10 and PR 11 narrowing to a coin flip that depends on how much weight the PRD's shipping plan gets.
dimensions.pr9: Distinct defects (charged once each): (1) HIGH, launch family: `--add-dir <dir>` is variadic per `claude --help` line 10 ("--add-dir <directories...>"), so md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:220 `"--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]` hands the prompt to --add-dir and the session starts idle; no `--allowedTools` so under dontAsk the single Write is denied (PR 10 and PR 11 both saw this live); automatic.py:207-208 then treats native `blocked` as fatal. Fix is ~3 source lines (reorder so the prompt follows `--permission-mode`, add `--allowedTools f"Edit(//{run}/review.completion.json)"`, replace the raise with a note-and-keep-polling) plus rewriting the second half of test_automatic.py:255-260 and the HANDOFF/VALIDATION sentences that describe the old argv. The root cause is not the code but the skipped gate: PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md line 60 says the controlled live smoke test runs "before merging", and the handoff line 63 admits it was not run and even predicts the exact fallback at line 55. (2) MEDIUM, status() at interactive.py:242-249 iterates NODES only and attach_panels (295-338) only ever maps ui/adapter, while PRD item 3 (line 53) asks for "third pane in attach_panels and attach-one"; the reviewer is reachable only through attach_reviewer_pane/attach-one. Fix ~3 lines (PR 11 shows the shape at md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:232). (3) LOW, kept a hand copy of the print-mode REVIEW_SCHEMA (automatic.py:133-141) beside the generated JSON instead of deriving it as PR 10 does; this copy is inherited from main automatic.py:116 and PR 11 keeps it too, so it is charged equally to both. (4) NIT, two names for one node: REVIEWER="reviewer" (sessions.py:20), file_prefix maps to "review" (sessions.py:24-26), receipt node_id "review", `attach-one --node reviewer`; internally consistent but a trap for operators reading PR 10/11 docs. Strengths: smallest and PRD-conformant scope, zod-first contract with generated schema and contract tests (contracts diff +174 across v1.ts/examples/contract.test.ts/schema), honest handoff. Score 5.5: one severe functional defect charged once, but the feature has never run live and the merge gate is unmet, so unknown unknowns remain even after the 3-line fix.
dimensions.pr10: Distinct defects: (1) HIGH, md-manager-high/workflow/export_state.py:16 `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0"` while main server/projects.ts:37/52 validates `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)` with '1.0.0'. Blast radius verified: main listRuns (server/projects.ts:320-345) calls projectRun inside try/finally with no catch, so one invalid run-state throws invalidRun for the whole workflow list; and `python -m workflow.pipeline <run> status` calls `report(runtime, state)` (md-manager-high/workflow/pipeline.py:688, same as main pipeline.py:600) which calls export_state, so a plain `status` on project-workflows-001 after merge rewrites its run-state.json to 1.2.0 and hides the workflow. The handoff (line 76-78) discloses the new-run window and warns only against `workflow export`, not `status`, so the disclosure is incomplete. Fix is one line either side: `version: z.enum(['1.0.0','1.1.0','1.2.0'])` at server/projects.ts:52 (main exportSchema is z.object, zod ^4.6.5, so the extra `review`/`inputs` keys are stripped, not rejected) plus one server test; or keep `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.0.0"` in export_state.py. (2) MEDIUM, the completion binds `reviewer_session` and the prompt (automatic.py:159) tells the reviewer to use "your own session UUID as shown by `claude agents`", but the reviewer has tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write only and cannot run it. The smoke transcript (~/.claude/projects/-home-agentops--local-state-md-manager-workflows-smoke-review-smoke-001-review-worktree/5865c9a6-....jsonl) shows the UUID first enters the model's context at record 204 (Grep result on events.jsonl) and 299 (Read of automatic-review.json), and its first assistant use is the Write at record 310; no earlier assistant mention exists. So the binding works only because the controller leaks the UUID into readable run-dir files; a reviewer that does not go hunting fails the whole review with "no second reviewer". Fix: one prompt line naming review.interactive.json, or ~15 lines to bind a pre-launch token as PR 9/11 do. (3) LOW-MEDIUM, wait_review's stop-recovery branch (automatic.py:196-198) is unreachable from review_candidate: a "running" receipt goes review_native -> run_reviewer -> reconcile (interactive.py:117-128) which raises when locate() finds no live row, and locate (interactive.py:82) only accepts idle/working/blocked/done. So the post-acceptance crash window (stop.json written, receipt still "running") is unhandled and test_stopped_reviewer_recovery_rereads_the_accepted_file (test_automatic.py:572-576) exercises dead code. PR 11 handles this window at md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:236-241. gaps.why_it_matters: The person asked two questions. Using verifier scores, raw 11-dim means are PR 9 4.4, PR 10 6.7, PR 11 7.8. Excluding adapter-server (PR 9 = 0) and ui-and-browser-tests (PR 9 = 1), which the umbrella PRD told slice A not to ship, PR 9 moves to 5.3. Splitting by question changes the second answer: code-only mean (controller, review-protocol, launch-attach-stop, contracts, export, adapter, ui, python-tests) is PR 9 3.8 (4.9 without N/A dims), PR 10 6.3, PR 11 8.3; process mean (spec-fidelity, reviewability, claims) is PR 9 6.0, PR 10 8.0, PR 11 6.3. judges.lens: Long-term maintainer of workflow/, contracts/, server/ and src/projects: structure and abstraction quality, correctness under failure, test durability, backward compatibility of the export/adapter seam, and which code I would rather own and extend in six months.
judges.rationale:
Code quality: PR 11 > PR 10 > PR 9, and the order is robust. PR 11 is the only branch whose review lifecycle has no code path describing behaviour that cannot happen: it persists review.json and marks the receipt succeeded before calling stop_reviewer() (md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:340-363, verified), retries an unconfirmed stop on resume (:234-241, `if receipt.get("transport") == "native" and not reviewer_stopped(runtime): runtime.stop_reviewer()`), re-checks identity/worktree/evidence after the wait (:332-339), and gives the P0/P1 rule one home in check_review/blocking_findings that Pipeline.validate_review and ExportRuntime both call (pipeline.py:42-70, :387, :440). Its adapter code matches main's conventions and is verifiably safer than main (redaction probe: seven new redactions, zero regressions; hash-and-size-checked review.diff; path-free error bodies snapshot-tested). Against that, the hand-written reviewCompletion.schema.json (git diff shows only README +2 and the 39-line JSON under contracts/workflow; no v1.ts, examples or contract test) breaks the repo's "v1.ts is authoritative" rule, automatic.py uses 12 literal "review" strings without importing REVIEW, attach_reviewer_panel is not idempotent, and the UI carries a half-finished support.ts extraction, a third copy of the tab keyboard handler and duplicate Loading/Error panels for one resource. Those are tidy-ups, not defects; I found no functional bug in PR 11. judges.lens: Human approver: reviewability, merge risk as-is, spec fidelity to the PRD plan, and whether the evidence lets me skip re-deriving; scope creep and unverifiable claims penalised, live-broken code disqualifying regardless of size.
judges.rationale:
Code quality is not close: PR 11 wins it (8 vs 7 vs 4.5). It is the only PR with no confirmed functional defect; its reviewer lifecycle is ordered accept-then-stop with a bounded, tested retry (md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:340-363, :236-241), it re-checks identity/independence/worktree/evidence after the wait (:332-339), it pins both live-discovered CLI facts as regression tests (test_interactive.py:245-249 asserts `command[-3:-1] == ["--permission-mode","dontAsk"]` and every variadic option before it), its projects contracts take enums from the policy schema, and I confirmed by probe that its adapter (server/projects.ts:44 `EXPORT_VERSIONS = ['1.0.0','1.1.0','1.2.0']`) serves both the untouched 1.0.0 live run and a re-exported 1.2.0 copy. Its code costs are real but low: ~20 magic "review" strings in automatic.py while pipeline.py uses REVIEW, a hand-written reviewCompletion.schema.json with no v1.ts/examples/contract test (contracts/workflow diff is README +2 and schema +39 only), and duplicated inputs Loading/Error panels in the UI. PR 10 is second on code: the cleanest shared-surface abstraction (reconcile()/launch() at interactive.py:117-161, one finish_review, REVIEW_NODE plus PANE_LABELS, single-sourced completion schema at automatic.py:129-138) but it stops before it persists (automatic.py:298-302), so a failed stop discards an accepted verdict; its wait_review stop-recovery branch (:196-198) is unreachable through review_native; and its prompt tells a Bash-less reviewer to find its UUID via `claude agents` (:159), which only worked because the model grepped the controller's own files. PR 9 is last: run_reviewer is a 54-line copy of run(), acceptance logic is written three times, the reviewer/review dual identity needs file_prefix() to bridge it, and the launch cannot work.

Overall, from the approver's seat, PR 10 edges PR 11 by a hair (7.2 vs 7.0) and the order flips under equal weighting; a colleague should treat them as a tie decided by how much weight the person's own slicing plan in 61e4752 gets. PR 10 did slice A the way the PRD wrote it (binds the reviewer session UUID per the design table, third pane in both attach_panels and attach-one, print fallback), ran the section-5 merge gate twice with durable artifacts I re-verified at ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/smoke/review-smoke-001 (session 5865c9a6, blocked verdict, stop marker 20:00:27, pane w5:pW), and recorded every deviation in the PRDs. Its one high is self-inflicted and understated: export_state.py:16 writes 1.2.0 while main's adapter (server/projects.ts:52) accepts only 1.0.0 and PR 10 ships no server/ change, so every new run is RUN_STORAGE_INVALID and, because `status` calls report() -> export_state (pipeline.py:688, :479-481), the first `workflow status` on project-workflows-001 rewrites it and main's listRuns (no per-run catch) 500s the whole workflow list; the handoff says only "that run's listing" and its RUNBOOK recommends the very command. That is a one-line fix (z.enum in the adapter, or hold 1.0.0) but it is a confirmed regression today. PR 11 delivered the only working, merge-safe end-to-end feature, but it overrode the umbrella PRD's explicit "A, then B's run, then C's run" plan (docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:21, written hours earlier to get smaller diffs and to dogfood the reviewer pane inside B's run), replaced the repo's independent-reviewer process for B/C with a self-run audit, ships features/review-result and features/run-inputs READMEs that say "not an implementation" and would assign finished work if launched, and its handoff claims the schemas were fixture-tested and regenerated by contracts:export, which is false for the completion schema. At 56 files and 6,074 added lines across six concerns in one squashed commit with no split guidance, it is a 12-16 hour review that needs the viewer running; PR 10 is 5-7 hours and PR 9 about 3.

PR 9 is last on every substantive question and its position is not an N/A artefact. Its reviewer launch (md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:217-220) puts the positional prompt directly after the variadic `--add-dir <dir>` (confirmed against `claude --help`; PR 11 hit exactly this live, session 7eb01f17 started idle) and passes Write under dontAsk with no allow rule (grep count 0; both other PRs saw the Write denied live), and wait_review raises on the `blocked` state (automatic.py:207-208) that a reviewer shows when it asks a person, contradicting PRD acceptance bullet 2 and its own README. Its tests are green because test_interactive.py:189 asserts only the element after --add-dir. It skipped the PRD section 5 smoke test that gates the merge and says so candidly, and its handoff's proposed fallback ("--add-dir plus a bypass mode") is the wrong fix. It is the easiest PR to review and every number in it verifies, but honest evidence of a non-working feature does not make it mergeable.
key_points: PR 9 is live-broken twice over: interactive.py:217-220 ends `"--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt` and `claude --help` shows `--add-dir <directories...>` is variadic, so the reviewer never receives its task; and there is no --allowedTools rule under dontAsk (grep count 0), so the one Write the protocol needs is denied (observed live by PR 10 and PR 11). Its suite is green only because test_interactive.py:189 never asserts the prompt's position.

PR 9 additionally treats native `blocked` as fatal (automatic.py:207-208) and pins that in a test, contradicting PRD_REVIEWER_PANE section 5 bullet 2 and its own README claim that you can answer the reviewer's question in the pane; it never stops the reviewer on deadline or rejection, and it skipped the section-5 live smoke test that the PRD names as the merge gate.

PR 10 is the only PR that does slice A the way the PRD wrote it (reviewer session UUID binding, third pane in attach_panels and attach-one, print fallback) and its live evidence is the most checkable of the three: every UUID, hash, timestamp, pane id and the 7/7 verbatim quote rate reproduce from ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/smoke/review-smoke-001.

PR 10's confirmed high: export_state.py:16 `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0"` with no server/ change while main's server/projects.ts:52 is `version: z.literal('1.0.0')`. New runs are RUN_STORAGE_INVALID, and because `status` calls report() -> export_state (pipeline.py:688, :479-481) the first `workflow status` on project-workflows-001 rewrites it and main's listRuns 500s the whole workflow list. The handoff says only 'that run's listing' and the RUNBOOK recommends that command. One-line fix either side.

PR 10 code defects to fix before merge: stop_session runs before finish_review (automatic.py:298-302) so a failed stop discards an accepted verdict; the wait_review stop-recovery branch (:196-198) is unreachable through review_native and its test exercises dead code; the prompt tells a Bash-less reviewer to use `claude agents` (:159) and the binding worked live only because the model grepped events.jsonl; finish_review persists an approved-with-open-P1 record its own export validator rejects.

PR 11 has the best code and no confirmed functional defect: accept-then-stop with a bounded retry on resume (automatic.py:340-363, :236-241, :467-479), post-wait identity/independence/worktree/evidence re-checks (:332-339), explicit launch-window Ctrl-C handling, blocked-as-waiting per the PRD, and the option-order trap pinned by test_interactive.py:245-249. Four live sessions culminated in a proven accept path (f36b923d, 8/8 verbatim quotes).

PR 11 is the only PR whose export, adapter and viewer are coherent: server/projects.ts:44 accepts 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0, and a probe on a copy served both the untouched 1.0.0 live run (404 REVIEW_NOT_FOUND/INPUTS_NOT_FOUND) and a re-exported 1.2.0 run (approved, 6 findings, diff artifact, inputs). Its adapter code is security-minded (better redaction regex, hash-and-size-checked review.diff, path-free errors) and its browser tests cover every PRD B/C scenario id once, unconditionally, in both phases.

PR 11's process debts: it implemented B and C directly in a 56-file/+6074 single commit against the umbrella PRD's explicit 'A, then B's run, then C's run' plan (docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:21, written in the very commit it branched from) and so skipped the dogfooding purpose of B's run; features/review-result and run-inputs READMEs say 'not an implementation' and would assign finished work; the handoff claims fixture-tested regenerated schemas, false for the hand-written reviewCompletion.schema.json (contracts/workflow diff is README +2, schema +39 only); smoke evidence sits in an unnamed ephemeral /tmp scratchpad that reused the live run id; '59 before' should be 70.

PR 11's code nits: ~20 literal 'review' strings in automatic.py while pipeline.py uses the REVIEW constant; the label ternary written twice; attach_reviewer_panel not idempotent; inputs Loading/Error panels rendered in three places (two role=alert on a worker node); a third verbatim copy of the tab keyboard handler focusing via a data-testid; projects.spec.ts still carries private copies of everything support.ts extracted.

PR 9 and PR 10 both define reviewCompletion in v1.ts with examples, contract tests and a generated JSON (repo convention); PR 9 is the only PR enforcing both cross-field rules in TS and Python, but its schema patterns are the loosest and its PRD 'Bound to' row still says session UUID while the code binds launch_token. PR 11 hand-writes the schema (strictest patterns, Python-tested, documented) outside the v1.ts-is-authoritative rule.

Not-applicable surfaces were excluded rather than scored 0: adapter-server and ui-and-browser-tests are by-design N/A for PR 9 and PR 10 (the PRD assigns server/ and src/ to feature runs). export-and-compat applies to all three; PR 9's clean compat is earned (export stays 1.0.0, plan gains a harmless key under a non-strict z.object). Each root cause is charged once: PR 9's launch family, PR 10's export bump, PR 11's direct implementation.

The PR 10 vs PR 11 overall order is a coin flip that depends on weights: under this approver lens (reviewability, plan adherence, checkable evidence weighted up) PR 10 edges ahead 7.2 to 7.0; under equal weighting of code quality and process, PR 11 is ahead by about half a point, as both gap verifiers found. PR 9 is last on every substantive question for reasons unrelated to N/A dimensions.

Cross-PR facts corrected: PR 9 also binds launch_token (only PR 10 binds the session UUID as the PRD table asks); PR 11 uses the `version` key the same way PR 10 does; PR 10's stop path is covered indirectly via the generic stop_session; the two PRs' 1.2.0 export shapes are mutually incompatible, so PR 11's adapter is not a drop-in fix for PR 10.

per_pr_verdict.pr9: Smallest, cleanest to read, and honest about what it did not do, but the feature it ships cannot run: the prompt is swallowed by the variadic --add-dir (interactive.py:217-220), the completion Write is denied under dontAsk with no allow rule, and a reviewer that asks a question kills the run (automatic.py:207-208). judges.merge_recommendation: PR 10: merge with named changes. Strongly recommended in the same PR: persist review.json and mark the receipt succeeded before stop_session (automatic.py:298-302) and delete or make reachable the wait_review stop-recovery branch (:196-198) and its test; name review.interactive.json in the prompt instead of `claude agents` (:159), or bind a controller-issued launch_token; normalise or refuse approved-with-open-P1 before persisting. Then run B and C as the feature runs the plan calls for, cherry-picking PR 11's order-pin test and accept-then-stop retry into A. PR 11: split, or merge whole with named changes if the person accepts abandoning the B/C feature runs. If merging whole: delete or rewrite features/review-result and features/run-inputs so they do not assign finished work; correct the handoff (schema regeneration claim, '59 before' -> 70, name the smoke-run location or copy it to ~/.local/state); add a v1.ts zod source, examples fixture and contract test for reviewCompletion (or document why it is exempt); replace the literal 'review' strings in automatic.py with the REVIEW constant; collapse the triplicated inputs Loading/Error panels. If splitting: pr11-sliceA.diff (14 files, +1699/-178) minus the slice-C prompt.txt writes is a mergeable slice A that is better than PR 10's on correctness and would need only the schema-convention fix. PR 9: reject in its current form and return for rework: reorder the argv so the prompt follows --permission-mode, add `--allowedTools Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json)`, treat `blocked` as a waiting state, stop the reviewer on failure, extend run_reviewer through a shared reconcile()/launch(), fix the tests that pin the old behaviour, update the PRD 'Bound to' row, and run the PRD section 5 live smoke test before resubmitting. Recommended path today: approve PR 10 with the two required changes; it is the fastest route to a live-proven slice A that keeps the viewer working and preserves the plan's feature-run dogfooding. Choose PR 11 instead only if the person values a complete, working, merge-safe delivery over the slicing plan and can spend the review time; do not try to fix PR 10 by transplanting PR 11's adapter, the two 1.2.0 export shapes are incompatible.

judges.lens: PRD author: does the shipped reviewer pane, completion protocol and unattended completion actually work live; was the PRD_REVIEWER_PANE section-5 smoke-test gate honoured; were decisions and deviations recorded honestly in the PRDs; does the viewer keep loading the existing run and new runs after merge; and was PR 11's bypass of the feature-run plan or PR 10's bundling of B/C pre-run work a good call or an overreach.
judges.rationale:
I wrote the PRDs, so the questions that decide this for me are: does the reviewer pane work live, was the section-5 gate I set honoured, does the viewer keep loading project-workflows-001 and new runs after merge, and were deviations written down. I re-verified the facts that carry the ranking rather than trusting the dimension write-ups.

PR 9 fails the first two questions outright. Its launch (md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:217-220) ends `"--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt`; `claude --help` on this host declares `--add-dir <directories...>` (variadic), so the prompt is consumed as a directory and the session starts idle (PR 11 hit exactly this live, session 7eb01f17). `grep -c allowedTools` on that file is 0, so under `--permission-mode dontAsk` the single Write is denied (both other PRs measured this live). And automatic.py:207-208 raises on native state `blocked`, which is the state a reviewer shows when it asks a person, so acceptance bullet 2 of section 5 is violated in code while features/project-workflows/README.md claims the opposite. PR 9's PRD status line says plainly the section-5 smoke test "has **not** been run"; that gate exists precisely to catch launch-time failures, and it would have caught all three. Honest, tidy, smallest diff, convention-pure contract, but a non-working feature and an unmet merge gate. Last on every question.

PR 10 is the only branch that did slice A the way PRD_REVIEWER_PANE wrote it (binds the reviewer session UUID, third pane in both attach_panels and attach-one, print fallback) and ran the gate twice with durable artifacts I re-checked: ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/smoke/review-smoke-001 has automatic-review.json blocked with session 5865c9a6, review.stop.json stopped at 20:00:27, a completion file bound to that UUID with 1 P1 + 6 P2, and the registry lists dccd22b5 stopped / 5865c9a6 done. Its deviations (Edit(//path) rule, blocked-as-waiting) are recorded in PRD section 6. Its bundling of B/C pre-run work is what PRD_REVIEW_RESULT section 2 and PRD_RUN_INPUTS section 3 call "pre-run work (ours)", so that is not an overreach in itself. What sinks it to second is the viewer question: workflow/export_state.py:16 writes 1.2.0 while server/projects.ts:52 on its own branch still says `z.literal('1.0.0')` and the branch has no server/ diff. Every new run is RUN_STORAGE_INVALID and, because main's listRuns has no per-run catch, one such run 500s the whole workflow list. Worse, `workflow status` (pipeline.py:688 -> report() -> export_state at :481) rewrites the historic run to 1.2.0, and PR 10's own RUNBOOK:210 tells the operator to run that command; the handoff (line 77) understates the effect as "that run's listing". That violates the criterion that the existing run must keep loading. Two further real defects: the stop runs before the verdict is persisted, so a failed stop discards an accepted review; and the prompt tells a Bash-less reviewer to find its UUID via `claude agents`, which the transcript shows only worked because the reviewer grepped the controller's own files. All are small fixes, but they are the difference between a merge-safe slice A and one that breaks the product on the first routine command.

PR 11 wins on the two questions I weight most: the feature works and the merge is safe. Its argv (md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:222-226) puts the prompt after the single-valued `--permission-mode`, explains why in a comment, and pins it in test_interactive.py:245-249. It is the only PR that persists review.json and marks the receipt succeeded before stopping the reviewer, retries an unconfirmed stop on resume, re-checks identity/independence/worktree/evidence after the wait, and normalises an approved-with-open-P1 verdict. Its scratchpad smoke-run shows the accept path live: automatic-review.json succeeded with f36b923d at 20:51:29Z, review.stop.json stopped, review.json approved with 8 findings all carrying worker and requirement, and the registry lists four sessions covering the swallowed-prompt defect, the Write denial, the deadline path and the accept path. server/projects.ts:44 accepts 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0, so project-workflows-001 (still version 1.0.0, untouched since 15:52 on Sep 21) keeps loading and re-exported runs serve review and inputs; the export-and-compat verifier reproduced both directions on a copy. Its hand-written reviewCompletion.schema.json (0 hits in v1.ts and contract.test.ts, 39 lines) is a convention break, disclosed in contracts/workflow/README.md:12, that I would fix but not block on.

Where PR 11 loses points is exactly the overreach the lens asks about. The umbrella PRD says "Order: A, then B's run, then C's run ... each run has a smaller, focused diff and a blocked run loses one slice, not all three", and B was ordered after A "so B's run then exercises the reviewer pane live". PR 11 shipped all three in one 56-file, +6074 commit, reviewed B and C with a self-run audit instead of the repo's independent reviewer inside a run, and so the new pane has still never run inside a full automatic run. It rewrote the umbrella status to say so, which is honest, but it did not argue the trade-off anywhere, and it left features/review-result and features/run-inputs saying "**not** an implementation ... Implement the viewer side of slice B" while the implementation sits in the same tree. Its handoff also has three inaccuracies (schemas "regenerated" with fixtures, which is false for the completion schema; "59 before" when main collects 70; attempt 2 as "nine P2" when the payload was 4 P2 + 5 P3), its smoke evidence sits in a session-scoped /tmp scratchpad, and the scratch plan reused run_id project-workflows-001 so four reviewer rows in `claude agents --all` carry the live run's name.

Net: PR 11 delivered a working, merge-safe, best-engineered result by ignoring my delivery plan; PR 10 followed my plan faithfully and proved slice A live but ships a viewer regression it half-disclosed; PR 9 followed my plan exactly and skipped the gate that would have shown its feature cannot run. On code quality PR 11 > PR 10 > PR 9 under every dimension that has code to judge (controller protocol 9/7/3.5, contracts 8/6/7, export-and-compat 8.5/4/6, plus adapter and UI code only PR 11 has). On "did the better job" the same order holds but PR 10 is within a point of PR 11: if the person weights adherence to the slicing plan above a merge-safe working delivery, PR 10 moves first; I do not, because the plan existed to produce a working pane and a loadable viewer, and only PR 11 delivers both today.
key_points: PR 9's native reviewer cannot complete a review on this CLI: interactive.py:217-220 hands the prompt to variadic --add-dir (claude --help: `--add-dir <directories...>`), there is no --allowedTools rule under dontAsk (grep count 0), and automatic.py:207-208 treats `blocked` as fatal against section-5 acceptance bullet 2. Its PRD status admits the section-5 gate was not run.

PR 10 is the only PR that implemented slice A as the PRD table specifies (reviewer session UUID binding, third pane in attach_panels and attach-one) and honoured the gate twice; artifacts verified at ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/smoke/review-smoke-001 (session 5865c9a6, blocked verdict 1 P1 + 6 P2, stop confirmed 20:00:27Z).

PR 10 breaks the viewer after merge: export_state.py:16 writes 1.2.0, its own server/projects.ts:52 still requires z.literal('1.0.0'), no server/ diff; `workflow status` (pipeline.py:688 -> report -> export_state) rewrites the historic run to 1.2.0 and main's listRuns then 500s the whole workflow list. RUNBOOK:210 recommends that exact command; handoff line 77 understates the radius as 'that run's listing'.

PR 11 is the only PR whose protocol is correct at every edge: prompt after single-valued --permission-mode with the reason in a comment and a test pin (interactive.py:222-226, test_interactive.py:245-249), verdict persisted before the stop with a bounded retry on resume, post-wait identity/independence/worktree/evidence re-checks, approved-with-open-P1 normalised.

PR 11 is the only PR with a live accept-path record: scratchpad smoke-run automatic-review.json succeeded (f36b923d, accepted_at 20:51:29Z), review.json approved with 8 findings all carrying worker+requirement, review.stop.json stopped; registry shows four sessions covering swallowed prompt, Write denial, deadline and accept.

PR 11 keeps the viewer working for old and new runs: server/projects.ts:44 EXPORT_VERSIONS = ['1.0.0','1.1.0','1.2.0']; the live run (version 1.0.0, no files modified after 15:52 Sep 21) still loads and a re-exported copy serves review, diff artifact and inputs (reproduced by the export-and-compat verifier).

PR 11 overrode the umbrella PRD's explicit plan ('A, then B's run, then C's run ... smaller, focused diff') with one 56-file, +6074 commit, replaced B/C's independent review with a self-run audit, and so the pane has never run inside a full automatic run (the dogfooding reason B was ordered after A). Disclosed in the PRD status line but never argued.

PR 11 ships features/review-result and features/run-inputs that still say '**not** an implementation' and 'Implement the viewer side of slice B' while the implementation is in the same tree; launching them would assign finished work.

PR 11's completion schema is hand-written (0 references in contracts/workflow/v1.ts and contract.test.ts, 39 lines) against the repo's generate-from-v1.ts convention; disclosed in contracts/workflow/README.md:12 but the handoff's 'npm run contracts:export regenerated the JSON schemas' is false for this file. PR 9 and PR 10 both did it the repo way, and only PR 10 single-sources the print-mode schema from it.

Honesty ledger: PR 9 candid about the skipped gate but its README/RUNBOOK/VALIDATION describe a single-file allow-list the code never implements and its handoff proposes a bypass mode as the fallback; PR 10's numbers all reproduce (one 95/96 slip) but its RUNBOOK omits the export breakage; PR 11's RUNBOOK is accurate but its handoff misstates the test baseline (59 vs 70), attempt 2's severities, and the schema provenance, and parks gate evidence in an ephemeral /tmp scratchpad under the live run's id.

Shared defect in PR 9 and PR 10: the reviewer stop runs before the verdict is persisted, so a failed stop lands in the generic blocked handler and the next resume refuses reconciliation, discarding a fully bound verdict. PR 11 orders accept-then-stop and retries.

Code-quality order is PR 11 > PR 10 > PR 9 under every dimension with code to judge; PR 10 has the tidiest shared-surface abstraction (reconcile()/launch(), finish_review, single node identity) and PR 9 the smallest diff but the least generalisation (run_reviewer copies run(), acceptance duplicated three times, dual reviewer/review identity).

per_pr_verdict.pr9: Disciplined scope, honest status, convention-pure contract, and the easiest of the three to read, but the delivered native reviewer does not work: the prompt is swallowed by the variadic --add-dir, the completion Write is denied under dontAsk with no allow rule, and a reviewer that asks a question kills the run while the README says the opposite. The PRD's section-5 smoke test, the one gate I wrote specifically to catch launch-time failures, was skipped and would have caught all three. It also ships a real contract contradiction (a resolved P0/P1 blocks an approved verdict), never stops the reviewer on failure, and discards an accepted verdict when the stop fails. As PRD author I cannot merge a slice A whose default transport has never completed a review; the three-line code fix is already present in the other two PRs.
per_pr_verdict.pr10: The branch that did what I asked, the way I asked: slice A per the design table, section-5 gate run twice with durable, byte-checkable artifacts, deviations written into PRD section 6, and the cleanest shared-surface abstraction of the three. Its B/C bundling is the pre-run work my own PRDs assign to an ordinary commit, so I do not count that against it. What I do count is that it shipped the export bump ahead of any adapter change and left the product broken for new runs and, via the `status` command its RUNBOOK recommends, for the existing run too, while describing the blast radius as one run's listing. Add the stop-before-accept ordering, the UUID-by-file-leakage binding, the dead stop-recovery branch and the persisted approved-with-open-P1 record, and it is a good slice A that needs four small fixes before it is merge-safe.
per_pr_verdict.pr11: The best code and the only PR that works end to end and leaves main consistent: correct argv with the reason pinned by a test, verdict durable before the stop with a retry, identity re-checked after the wait, adapter accepting 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 so the live run keeps loading, careful security-minded adapter and accessible UI with unconditional browser assertions for every B/C scenario id, and four live sessions culminating in a proven accept path. It got there by discarding my delivery plan: one 6k-line commit instead of A plus two focused feature runs, B and C reviewed by a self-run audit instead of the independent reviewer inside a run, and the pane still never exercised in a full automatic run. It also leaves feature directories that would assign finished work, hand-writes the completion schema outside the contracts convention, and carries three handoff inaccuracies and ephemeral gate evidence under the live run's id. Right result, wrong process; the result is what I would keep.

judges.merge_recommendation: Merge PR 11 with named changes; close PR 9 and PR 10 and port two items from PR 10. PR 11 (merge with named changes): (1) delete features/review-result and features/run-inputs or rewrite their READMEs and task files to say the slices are implemented and the run is optional regression exercise; (2) add reviewCompletion to contracts/workflow/v1.ts with an examples.ts fixture and a contract test, regenerate the JSON via contracts:export, and correct the handoff sentence about regenerated schemas; (3) fix the handoff numbers (baseline 70 not 59; attempt 2 was 4 P2 + 5 P3) and copy the smoke-run artifacts to a durable path under ~/.local/state with a distinct run id; (4) before relying on the pane in production, run one full automatic feature run with the native reviewer, which is the dogfooding the umbrella PRD ordered B after A to get; (5) optionally re-split into three commits (slice A, B, C) using the handoff's per-slice file list so the history matches the PRDs. PR 10 (merge with named changes if the person prefers the PRD-faithful slice A instead): (1) widen server/projects.ts:52 to z.enum(['1.0.0','1.1.0','1.2.0']) with a server test, or hold EXPORT_VERSION at 1.0.0 until B's adapter exists; (2) persist review.json and receipt=succeeded before stop_session and retry the stop on resume; (3) replace the `claude agents` instruction in the prompt with the receipt path or bind a controller-issued launch_token; (4) apply the P0/P1 disposition check before persisting review.json; (5) add the 1.2.0 warning to the RUNBOOK export and status entries. PR 9 (reject): the native launch cannot run on this CLI and the section-5 gate is unmet; do not merge, but port nothing is needed since PR 10 and PR 11 already carry the fixes. Items worth porting from PR 10 into PR 11 regardless: the zod-sourced reviewCompletion with the print-mode schema derived from it, and the explicit stopped_at written into stop markers instead of PR 11's mtime-based confirmed_at.
